designs.lens: Computational economics, explicit baseline first. For each piece of the transport computation I ask what it costs when computed physically on the same state (same patches, same rays, same readout), how that scales, and whether a learned replacement saves anything that a physical cache or an explicit patch-level computation would not also save. Tags used throughout: [code] verified implementation fact, [measured] stored measurement, [worklog] a worklog's interpretation, [inference] my own inference or arithmetic, [hypothesis] unverified.
designs.problem_reconstruction:
EXACT PHYSICS. Let b be outgoing boundary radiance on (x, w). The free-space coupling C_G carries b along unoccluded straight segments of the current geometry G to the next boundary entry; it has no material parameter and every (x, w_in) reads exactly one (y, w_out). The intrinsic response K maps the incident boundary field e + C_G b to the radiance at first exit into free space, in material coordinates. b = K(e + C_G b) is exact when every path segment has one owner (air -> C, inside a domain -> K) and K does not depend on path history ([measured] WL53 reference; WL51 shows the consequence when the reference violates this). With the frozen pointwise ER closure, K = S_ER is local ([code] 69 runtime floats per material, closed-form eval / sample / pdf, no spatial argument), so b = q + T_G b with T_G = S_ER C_G and q = S_ER e, and b = sum_k T_G^k q. Any regrouping of that series is also exact: by segment (K / C), by event count (b = sum_{k<m} T^k q + T^m (I - T)^-1 q; ECRO uses this with the first two camera-side events traced), by vertex class, or by sender class, provided the same T is applied at every path position and both sides of the split use the same classification.

OPTIONAL COMPUTATIONAL APPROXIMATIONS, each with its own error: (a) projection Pi onto a finite boundary basis (ports or patches x direction bins); (b) quadrature of C_G by a finite ray set; (c) truncation of the series; (d) low-rank or factorised forms; (e) replacing a computed map by a parametric function of G. Only (e) is learning. (a)-(d) are available to a learning-free solver holding the same state, which is why that solver is the baseline for every cost claim.

WHAT EACH LEARNABLE OBJECT REPLACES AND WHAT THAT COMPUTATION COSTS PHYSICALLY.
(i) Intrinsic K: K_theta(domain shape, medium) replaces in-domain path simulation. The physical cost is per domain shape, not per pose: [measured] 175-380 s and 1.7-2.0 GB for one 10 x 10 x 1 cm slab at 2.5 mm cells, 92.9 % of a selective update (WL55 / WL56); zero under rigid motion ([measured] resident state update 0.685 s, WL56). With ER, K is already closed form, so nothing global is left to learn in K.
(ii) Coupling C_G: C_phi(G) replaces ray casting. [measured] explicit update 5.0 / 11.1 ms at ~10k / ~40k ports with 128 gathers (WL52); 0.19-0.24 ms kernel for 650,240 state rays (WL86 econ86.json); learned GLT 44 / 672 ms (WL52). At measured scales there is no physical cost here to amortise.
(iii) Higher-order response: R_theta(G) ~ T^m (I - T)^-1 replaces repeated application of T. In a path tracer that is the segments beyond the cut and their variance ([measured] 1.806 vs 0.331 ms per spp, WL86). In a patch-level solver it is J sparse applications over the same state ([inference] of the order of a millisecond at WL86's state; never timed).
(iv) Compressed composed system: G -> reduced (I - T_G)^-1 or a source-to-image operator (the PRT class). It replaces everything and is bounded by what compresses: [prior art] the transport operator is not compact (Soler et al. 2022) and rank is bounded below by region size times angular band limit (Mahajan et al. 2007; Lessig and Fiume 2010).

ECONOMIC READING [inference]. The four objects differ in whether an expensive physical computation stands behind them. (i) has one, for nonlocal media whose shape changes. (ii) has none. (iii) has one only in the form of path length and variance inside a path tracer, and a table filled by any means removes it. (iv) has one only if the operator is reused over many right-hand sides and compresses, which the sharp part does not.

what_each_learnable_object_must_preserve.intrinsic_K: Linearity in the incident field, non-negativity, passivity on every field and every exit direction the coupling actually queries (not only a probe direction), reciprocity, and path-history independence of the target it is fitted to. Direction-resolved incident and exit dependence wherever the material is direction-selective ([measured] WL47: equal-irradiance pairs differ by 0.98-1.11; WL58: 64 / 256 bins lose 52-80 % at GGX alpha 0.04). Sub-port spatial structure near contact on the K side as well as the C side ([measured] WL54 / WL55: +10 to +22 % outgoing flux at 1 cm, <= 1.8 % at 2.5 mm). A separate ballistic term. Economically it must preserve the edit signal: its approximation error has to be below the edit-induced change of the exact operator, about 1 % of the action for the tested dents ([measured] stale exact K 0.5-1.2 % against learned 6-7 %, WL57 / WL59), otherwise not updating is both cheaper and more accurate.
what_each_learnable_object_must_preserve.coupling_C: Which sender point and which sender direction each receiver ray reads (a direction-resolved read, [measured] WL46 / WL48), visibility at the scale on which sender radiance varies, near-field pairs closer than a patch ([measured] WL52: ray-traced patch transfer is as wrong as the learned one, p99 2.30 vs 2.32; WL54: 94 % of the error from pairs closer than 1 cm), row-sum closure and reciprocity, and an exact invalidation set under an edit. It has no material content, so a learned C can preserve at best what a ray cast gives, at [measured] 8-60x the update cost (WL52).
what_each_learnable_object_must_preserve.higher_order_response: Patch-level levels at the locations that carry camera importance, not only the aggregate field: [measured] WL86A Stage B has the back-wall field at oracle noise with flux 0.995-1.006 while the mirror-read region is 7-10 % low because a handful of patches are 8-26 % low. The first flight from a sharp sender must keep its geometric support. Exclusive event ownership against the traced low-order part. Linearity in the source. Geometry dependence in the regions where a stale state fails ([measured] region A 2.6-3.9x, E1 panel 7-8x; elsewhere 0.87-1.6x). An energy bound, because the one-shot operator has none by construction ([code] no passivity constraint; [measured] flux 0.98-1.00 on one geometry and light). From my lens it must also keep a reason to exist: its fill cost and error have to beat an explicit recurrence over the same state.
what_each_learnable_object_must_preserve.compressed_composed_system: Only what is uniformly compressible: transport after at least one broad bounce, over regions and angular bands whose space-bandwidth product fits the retained rank. Sharp sender-to-receiver relations are source- and reader-specific and cannot be held by a source-independent, reader-independent finite basis without a size that grows as alpha^-4 over d_min^2 ([worklog] WL84A derivation calibrated on WL58); they have to stay outside the compressed object. It must preserve reuse: the economic case exists only when one operator serves many right-hand sides, and under a geometry edit the operator itself is the thing invalidated.

historical_failure_synthesis.common_to_four_part_K_and_ECRO:
Checked item by item; I do not find one common cause.

Exclusive path ownership. Both enforce exclusivity at the boundary between the physically computed part and the learned part, and neither enforces it inside the learned sum. FNTO: K versus C is exclusive through how the probes are rendered, but [code] K_glob, K_band and K_mid are fitted jointly to one residual with nested supports and no partition, against the contract's own line 74. ECRO: the cut between traced events 1-2 and the table is exact, but [code] the single flight and the rank-24 global term are supervised only on their sum, so which term owns which event order is an analysis convention. Shared.

Directional support. Both resolve the sender's direction dependence more coarsely than the stage that reads it. FNTO supervised exits only toward cameras and read the sender at the port normal ([measured] 5-9x deficit at the normal, rho 9.4-17.1 when read off-normal, WL46 / WL48). ECRO passes every patch's bin-to-bin scattering, the sharp panel included, through 16 non-negative channels and reads senders through 8 rays per incident bin ([code]; [measured] 7.8-17 panel-hitting rays per important patch). Shared in kind, different in detail: ECRO's outputs were supervised everywhere, FNTO's were not.

Identifiable learning targets. Both supervise a sum, and in both a geometry-poor term fills in for a geometry-specific term that under-delivers: [measured] K_glob carries 86 % of the Yellow red mode while band / mid are 5-9x low at the read direction (WL51); ECRO's global term is +0.017 to +0.064 above the >= 3-event truth while the panel flight delivers 1-18 % (WL86A, post hoc). Shared.

Stable repeated application. Not shared. FNTO recursed a learned operator and diverged (rho 2.1 to 17, 64/64 solves, WL41 / WL42 / WL46 / WL50); the cause was a non-passive, path-history-dependent target recursed through a high return fraction ([measured] rho = gain x return, 8.08 x 0.851 = 6.888, WL51). ECRO applies its operator once and shows no instability ([measured] flux 0.980-0.998). This failure is specific to recursion over a learned operator fitted to a non-passive reference.

A principled computational partition. Neither partition was derived from cost, and this is the commonality my lens adds. In FNTO the learned K was the expensive part of the pipeline ([measured] K 95 % of a step, 787 ms against 23 ms for C, WL52 Stage A) and its range split (5 cm / 30 cm / global) had no cost model. In ECRO the learned operator replaced the patch-level flights, whose explicit evaluation over the same state rays was never timed or scored ([code] econ86.py has only the arms 'pt' and 'ecro'), while the measured saving comes from the place where the camera path is cut ([measured] 5.45x per sample) and from a noise-free higher-order term ([measured] 1.6-1.7x fewer samples), both of which any filled table provides. In both programmes the same-state physical counterpart of the learned term was not the comparator. The one time it was (WL52, learned C against GPU explicit C) the learned object lost by 8-60x.
mechanism_specific_findings: Divergence of the composed solve (WL41, 42, 46, 50) is specific to recursing a learned nonlocal operator; with a non-passive camera-vertex Burley target the loop gain is gain x return ([measured] WL51). It does not transfer to a one-shot operator or to an explicit recurrence over a certificate-passive ER.

The Yellow SSS findings (WL44-51) are bound to Cycles 3.5.1 object-scoped Burley semantics ([measured] diffuse-ancestor vertex exactly 0 against 0.845 at a camera vertex). They constrain use of that reference, not learned operators as a class.

K44's normal-direction sender deficit, the 19-bin band term and representative-sampled supports (WL46-49) are properties of that kernel family; DASQ removed the aggregation loss at 2.2-2.8x the elements ([measured] WL49).

ECRO's sharp miss is specific to this operator form and state: shared rank-16 non-negative factors, 512 receiver-stratified rays, 64-bin sender radiance, unweighted relative-L2 loss, point-light training. Which of these binds was not isolated ([measured] free-factor fit leaves 49-68 %, capacity and optimisation confounded; no retraining).

The dense N x M pair evaluation that made learned C slow (WL52: 44 -> 110 -> 672 ms, 10x memory at 40k ports) is specific to the GLT architecture; ECRO's generator also builds a dense N x N form-factor matrix for message passing ([code] model86.py), unmeasured beyond 1,270 patches.

Learned-K transfer limits on the slab (WL68-80: good within 5-18 mm of a supervised source, far-boundary contrast 0.67-0.95 against oracles 0.13-0.27, late-training drift after 2k-6k steps) are measured on one homogeneous index-matched fixture with 4-16 supervised sources and one family of factorisations.

Selective state update has no economic value at the state sizes tested: [measured] ECRO 0.06 vs 0.19-0.20 ms kernel for 650,240 rays (21 vs 26-28 ms wall); WL59 saves 1.4-1.7 % because geometry and ballistic rebuild dominate. This is a statement about these state sizes, not about selection in general.
ECRO's 9x per-frame and 3-6x edit-to-first-frame figures are relative to a six-vertex path tracer without Russian roulette at noise-level quality; the protocol verdict is NOT TESTED.
constraints_on_any_future_architecture: A learned component must be compared with the explicit computation on the same state before it is compared with path tracing. Where this was done the learned object lost on cost (WL52). Where it was not done (WL86) the measured saving cannot be attributed to learning.

Costs must be kernel GPU time or work counts on an idle GPU. [measured] In the Dr.Jit harness Python tracing is 70-95 % of wall; WL52's sign flipped under contention; the ECRO operator has only a wall time (11.3 ms) and no kernel time.
Whatever is read through a near-mirror vertex must be accurate per sender patch at the importance-weighted locations; aggregate field error and flux do not bound it ([measured] WL86A Stage B).

A finite receiver-side gather with a fixed, source-blind ray allocation does not place a sharp sender's reflected lobe at patch level even with exact sender radiance ([measured] RAY -20 %, patch RMS 0.50-0.93 at 512 rays, two cases, one ray set, marginal rule). Any design, learned or explicit, that reads sharp senders this way inherits it.

A fixed direction-bin interface is a fixed-bandwidth mollifier for lobes narrower than the bin ([measured] WL58 analytic gate; [prior art] path-space regularisation). More training does not remove it.

Terms supervised only on their sum are not separately identified; a term without pairwise visibility will absorb what a geometry-specific term fails to deliver ([measured] WL51 mode shares, WL86A term split; [prior art] the 'intelligent ambient term' of MRT, VPL clamping plus compensation).

An operator applied recursively must be passive on the fields and directions its own composition returns to it; first-event fidelity, linearity and non-negative weights do not provide this ([measured] WL42, 46, 50, 51).

The reference must be path-history independent and the local closure's own gap must be separated from the global mechanism's error: [measured] on sharp receivers g(REF-ER vs REF-P) is 0.059-0.069, the size of ECRO's gate (0.06) and of its miss (0.063 / 0.072).

On the workloads measured so far a quality-matched path-traced re-render takes 1-5 s wall or less ([measured] WL67 4.67 s, WL69 2.4 s, WL70 2.09 vs 2.40 s, WL85 0.39 s GPU to reach g). Any stored state must fit its build amortisation, update and readout under that or name a larger workload.

Stored-state cost scales with scene size times directional complexity; path-tracing cost scales with pixels times samples times depth. [inference] At WL86's size the table has 81,280 entries against 262,144 pixels; at Lego scale (854k ports x 64 bins) it would be about 55 M entries. A stored global state is economic only where scene x direction is small against the pixel budget or the state is reused over many views, frames or lights.

sharp_transport_answers.is_finite_ray_sampling_incompatible: Not incompatible in principle; incompatible in the form ECRO used it. [measured] With exact once-scattered panel radiance read through the deployed 512 cosine-stratified rays per patch, the light -> panel -> Lambert-patch family is 20 % low in aggregate with patch RMS 0.50-0.93 (WL86A amendment 2; two cases, one ray realisation, each case passing through a different clause, one by 0.4 points). The median number of rays that hit the panel per important patch is 13-17 of 512. [prior art] A receiver-side gather finds a sender lobe with probability proportional to the lobe's solid angle (Veach section 8.3), so the receiver-side ray count needed per patch grows as about 1 / r50^2. [inference, economics] Rays themselves are cheap at this scene size: 650,240 state rays cost 0.19-0.24 ms kernel (2.7-3.4 M rays per ms), so 16x the ray set would cost about 3 ms. What does not scale is a fixed, source-blind, receiver-stratified allocation: N x r50^-2 rays for every receiver whether or not a sharp sender illuminates it. A sender-side evaluation (sample the sender's lobe from the light) costs in proportion to the lit sharp-sender area times the number of lights and is independent of lobe width; it is also source-dependent work, which a source-independent learned operator cannot use. More rays is therefore a justified answer only at small N and moderate r50; neither it nor a learned operator on the same 512 rays changes the scaling.
sharp_transport_answers.support_without_exhaustive_rays: The support of light -> sharp sender -> receiver is fixed by geometry: reflect the light direction about the sender normal and open a cone of about the lobe's r50; receivers inside the cone and visible from the sender are the support. [inference] It can be found sender-side at a cost of (sharp-sender samples x lights x one ray), without enumerating receiver-sender pairs: for WL86, 42 panel patches and one light, of the order of 10^6 rays, under a millisecond at the measured ray rate. A source-independent version has to store, per sharp sender, the map incident direction -> reflected cone -> receiver set at the sender's own angular resolution; that is rays proportional to (sharp patches x r50^-2 x samples), restricted to sharp senders but growing toward the alpha^-4 tabulation bound of WL84A as lobes narrow. Nothing in this needs learning: the support is the mirror-reflection construction, and the published dynamic method that handles this family (Xu et al. 2014) integrates sender-centred in closed form and stores nothing. I found no evidence that a learned generator given only patch tokens and 512 receiver-side rays can recover that support; [measured] ECRO's flight delivered 1-18 % of the family.
sharp_transport_answers.role_of_material_angular_structure: The material's angular structure is known in closed form and is the cheapest information in the system: [code] each ER state is one Lambert plus seven GGX lobes with exact eval / sample / pdf. It decides three things. (1) Which senders can be aggregated: [measured] WL85 census - the floor is 99.8 % broad (r50 0.60), the sphere 97 % moderate (0.36), the panel 43 % sharp / 56 % moderate (r50 0.146, 0.09 at 80 degrees); on the hard material population a median 94 % of albedo is in moderate lobes. (2) The angular resolution a stored sender radiance needs, about r50^-2 bins; ECRO's 64 bins are roughly 0.35-0.7 rad wide against a 0.15 rad panel lobe. (3) How to sample: the lobe pdf places samples in the reflected cone at no search cost. ECRO discarded this structure by forcing every patch's scattering through 16 shared non-negative channels ([code]). [inference] From a cost view, evaluating ER exactly at a ray hit is one 8-lobe closed-form evaluation; no table and no learned factor is cheaper than that for a sharp lobe.
sharp_transport_answers.preserve_support_or_aggregate: Aggregate where the reader integrates, preserve where the reader or the sender is narrower than the stored resolution. [measured] The learned table is at 0.003-0.006 on stationary and broad regions on both edits, and the same table is 0.063 / 0.072 where it is read through the panel and sphere mirrors; the level error of a few Lambert patches (-0.058 to -0.069) dominates the directional error (-0.002 to -0.004). [prior art] Every runtime cache surveyed guards its read with a footprint or roughness test (NRC spread, SHaRC cone spread, Lumen roughness bands, ReSTIR PT reconnection above roughness ~0.2). [inference, economics] Preserving support by sampling costs path segments only on the paths that need it (region C is 1.5 % of the frame on E2), while preserving it in storage costs alpha^-4. So the economic rule is: store what is broad, trace what is sharp, and decide by comparing the reader footprint and the sender lobe with the table resolution. Neither pure aggregation nor a uniformly finer table is justified.
sharp_transport_answers.representability_vs_identifiability: Representability is settled only for the container and partly for the encoding. [measured] A path-traced 1,270 x 64 table through the same readout is at reference noise (E_H 0.0025-0.0137; not for class E on E1 and the sphere object). [measured, pre-registered] An incident field with the same 64-bin encoding leaves region C's reading within 0.002 of truth for three point-light cases, so a linear geometry-determined operator on that encoding exists for those cases; it is not shown for narrow sources ([measured, post hoc] one beam pair with identical encodings reads 2.9x differently). Representability inside the rank-16 / rank-24 factor family is indeterminate ([measured] free-factor fit leaves 49-68 % of the deficit; capacity confounded with optimisation and the unweighted loss). Identifiability is weak by construction: only the sum of the two terms is supervised, the panel-relevant entries are a small share of 81,280 equally weighted entries, and the flight's patch-level signal arrives through 13-17 rays with 50-93 % RMS error. [worklog, speculative] The worklog reads this as a signal a squared-error fit would suppress; no retraining tested it. [inference] From my lens the distinction matters less than it appears: the single flight is a quantity that can be computed for milliseconds on the same state. A term that is cheaper to compute than to identify does not need to be learned, and the identifiability question then applies only to what is left after it is computed.
sharp_transport_answers.avoiding_global_term_compensation: Compensation is a consequence of three choices together: a geometry-specific term that is information-starved, a second term with no pairwise visibility, and a loss on their sum. [measured] The global term sits +0.017 to +0.064 above the >= 3-event truth on E2 and +0.039 / +0.041 on E1's panel, with opposite net sign on the two edits. Remedies that follow from the evidence, without assuming a particular architecture: (1) compute rather than learn the term that has a cheap physical evaluation (the flights), so there is nothing to compensate for; (2) if a learned correction remains, supervise it on a defined residual against a fixed deterministic explicit part, not on a sum with another free term; (3) score per path family with path-tagged truth (the WL86A split of two-event-via-panel, two-event-other, three-or-more) and per importance-weighted patch, because the aggregate gate passed at 1.12-1.13 while box patches were 1.6-2.7x worse on unseen geometry. [inference] Loss reweighting or a larger rank would change how compensation is distributed but not the fact that a rank-24 mixing has no visibility; I do not treat either as a justified fix.

hypotheses.name: H1. Explicit same-state fill of the higher-order table, sender-side routing of sharp senders, no learned global operator (the learned component stays in the local closure)
hypotheses.central_principle: [inference] At the state ECRO operated on, every step that turns (geometry, source) into the higher-order patch x bin table is a sparse linear recurrence that is cheap to evaluate physically. ECRO's measured saving comes from where the camera path is cut and from a noise-free higher-order term, and any filled table provides both. Until an explicit fill on the same state is shown to be less accurate or more expensive than the learned fill, a learned global operator has no economic role on this workload class. This is a null hypothesis with a definite construction, and it can fail.
hypotheses.primary_operator_math:
Estimator, as in ECRO ([code] pt86.py): I = PT[events 1..2 with next-event estimation] + throughput(x1) * B_H[patch(x2), bin(x2 -> x1)].
Table: B_H = Pi_out * sum_{j=1..J} That^j q, with That = Shat * Chat_G.
Chat_G (state rays): E_n(w_r) = B[hit(n, r), bin(-w_r at the hit)], r = 1..R per patch.
Shat (persistent, per material): B_n[o] = sum_r wt_r * M_mat(n)[o, r] * E_n(w_r), where M[o, r] is the average over outgoing bin o of f_ER(w_r -> w_o) cos. The ray template is identical in every patch frame ([code] same stratified offsets for every patch), so M is one 64 x R x 3 table per material.
First flight (j = 1): the sender value is not read from bins. It is the exact once-scattered radiance q(y, -w_r), one next-event evaluation through the ER lobe at the hit point y. For senders classed sharp (closure r50 below the outgoing bin width) the family light -> sharp sender -> receiver is removed from the gather and deposited from the sender side: sample the sender area, sample the ER lobe for the light direction, trace one ray, deposit on the receiver patch. The class threshold is applied identically in the gather (excluded) and the deposit (included).
Flights j >= 2 read the stored 64-bin sender radiance.
hypotheses.what_is_learned: Nothing in global transport. The frozen ER closure remains the only learned object ([code] 150,848-parameter compiler, 69 runtime floats per material, GM0).
hypotheses.what_is_physically_computed: BVH update, state rays, source terms by next-event estimation, per-material transfer tables M, every flight of the recurrence, sender-side deposits for sharp senders, the 1-2-event camera paths and the readout.
hypotheses.runtime_inputs_outputs: Inputs: current patch tables and BVH, per-material ER states, the light list. Outputs: B_H [N, 64, 3] and the image. No reference image, no post-edit supervision, no source identity. The recurrence is linear in q, so superposition holds exactly. The sender-side deposit is source-dependent work; that is permitted here because no learned rule depends on it.
hypotheses.persistent_vs_edit_dependent_state: Persistent, in material coordinates, never invalidated by a rigid edit: the M tables, the per-object patch parametrisation, the ray template. Edit-dependent: the BVH, state rays whose segment crosses the old or new mover volume ([measured] 8.7-10.2 % dirty; 0.06 vs 0.19-0.20 ms kernel, so selecting them is economically irrelevant at this size), the source terms, and the whole table, which is re-solved in full. A light-only change redoes the source terms and the recurrence and traces no geometry rays.
hypotheses.spatial_angular_information: Outgoing side: patch x 64 bins is a sufficient container for exit radiance of two or more events on the WL86 room ([measured] oracle E_H 0.0025-0.0137; closures with r50 >= 0.15 rad). Incident side: kept per ray, not binned, so the 64-bin incident mollifier of ECRO's encoding is not introduced. Sharp senders: once-scattered radiance is evaluated exactly per ray or deposited sender-side; their exit radiance of two or more events held in 64 bins is blurred by the bin width and would need sender-local angular refinement growing as r50^-2 on those patches only (42 of 1,270 here). Near contact: patch-constant senders lose sub-patch structure for pairs closer than about one patch ([measured] WL52, WL54); H1 does not resolve this without refinement.
hypotheses.path_ownership_and_composition: Camera side: the event-count cut is the same exact partition as ECRO (events 1-2 traced, three or more read once). Table side: one operator That owns every flight and there is no second additive term, so no term can stand in for another. Gather versus sender-side deposit is exclusive by sender class at the first flight. No learned operator is recursed: [inference, not measured for this construction] the recurrence's gain is bounded by the largest ER albedo times ray weights that sum to at most the hemisphere measure, and ER is certificate-passive.
hypotheses.unseen_geometry_and_illumination: There are no parameters and therefore no training distribution: any geometry, any light type that next-event estimation or light sampling handles, and non-rigid edits (patches are re-tabulated). Its errors are discretisation errors; they fall under refinement and can be measured by doubling R, N or the sender bins. Narrow spots and coloured or multiple lights, which ECRO was not trained on ([measured] narrow-spot field error 0.78-0.89, LSPOT hl/h 1.07-1.11), are covered by the exact first flight.
hypotheses.source_of_compressibility: Structural and physical, not statistical. C_G is sparse (R non-zeros per patch row). S is block-diagonal with one shared block per material. Each broad bounce low-pass filters radiance, so radiance of three or more events is smooth at patch x 64-bin scale on this workload ([measured] WL86 Stage 1). No compression of sharp transport is claimed; it is carried by sampling and not stored.
hypotheses.cost_model:
Symbols: N patches, B_o outgoing bins, R rays per patch, J flights, L lights, N_s sharp patches, n_ph sender-side samples, P pixels, s samples per pixel.
Offline supervision and training: none ([measured] ECRO: 10.7 + 4.4 min supervision and 21.7 min training per scene family).
Geometry state and relation discovery: N*R rays; [measured] 0.19-0.24 ms kernel for 650,240 rays (26-28 ms wall in the harness). Sender-side: L * N_s * n_ph rays.
Learned-state generation: none ([measured] ECRO: 11.3 ms wall per edit, kernel time not recorded, 42.9 MB of factors).
Source application: N*R*L shadow rays plus one ER evaluation each for the exact first flight; [inference] a fraction of a millisecond per light at the measured ray rate.
Solve: J * (N*R gathers + N*R*B_o multiply-adds); [inference from operation counts, never timed] about 0.5 G multiply-adds for J = 4, of the order of a millisecond of kernel time.
Per-edit update: dirty rays plus a full re-solve. Per-frame render: [measured] 0.331 ms per spp at 512^2 against 1.806 ms for the six-vertex path tracer.
Memory: [measured] ray state 17.6 MB, table 0.98 MB; M tables below 1 MB [inference].
Break-even against plain path tracing [inference from econ86.json]: a fill pays within a single frame when fill < 1.475 ms * s, i.e. 1.5 ms at 1 spp, 24 ms at 16 spp, 380 ms at 256 spp.
Scaling: linear in N*R. Receiver-side R grows as r50^-2; sender-side replaces it by N_s * n_ph. Stored sharp exit radiance grows as r50^-2 bins per sharp patch, and the general tabulation bound is alpha^-4 / d_min^2 ([worklog] WL84A). Worst case: a closed all-sharp scene, where nothing may be read from the table and the method degenerates to path tracing with no saving. Scene size: the table grows with N * B_o while path tracing grows with P * s; [inference] at Lego scale the table would have about 55 M entries.
Amortisation: the table is view-independent, so views and frames at fixed geometry and light share one fill; each additional lighting state costs one re-solve.
This hypothesis needs exhaustive patch-level visibility sampling (N*R rays per geometry). That is cheap at 10^5-10^8 rays ([measured] 109 M rays in 0.105 s trace-only, WL52) and is a plain threat to the economics beyond that.
hypotheses.is_saving_unique_to_learning: No, by construction. The 5.45x per-sample factor and the 1.6-1.7x sample reduction belong to the two-tier estimator and are available to a learned fill (measured), a path-traced fill ([measured] at most about 0.16 s of GPU time per 256-spp table, 1.2-1.5 s wall in the harness; [inference] about 0.61 ms per table spp, a probe path costing 7.5 ns against 6.9 ns for a camera path) and this explicit fill alike. H1 asserts that learning adds nothing to them at this state.
hypotheses.how_it_could_fail: (1) The explicit recurrence is biased on broad or moderate transport at 64 outgoing bins: [measured] WL58 has a 64 / 256-bin interface marginal (9.9-17.7 %) at alpha 0.25, and the floor and sphere closures have r50 0.60 and 0.36. If its bias exceeds the learned operator's 0.003-0.006 on stationary regions, the learned operator has a real accuracy-per-state advantage. (2) Near-contact sub-patch error around the boxes (region A), as in WL52 / WL54. (3) Sharp senders of radiance of two or more events stay mollified ([measured] BIN read -16 % / -26 % for the once-scattered case). (4) The solve estimate is wrong by an order of magnitude once exact per-ray ER evaluation per light is included. (5) The two-tier estimator itself has little room against an optimised path tracer: the comparator had no Russian roulette, and [measured] WL85's cold path tracer reaches g in 0.39 s of GPU time on its fixture. (6) Under the project's rules a mechanism with no learned global state may be admissible only as a baseline ([worklog] WL84A X7; open human decision).

falsification.smallest_physical_test: On the frozen WL86 edits E1 and E2, with their existing references, masks and state rays: fill the same 1,270 x 64 table by the explicit recurrence in three variants (binned senders; exact first flight; exact first flight plus sender-side panel deposit), read it with the identical readout, and score E_H per region and per object against REF-ER and against the oracle table, with uncontended kernel time for the fill. Add a path-traced table ladder (16 to 4,096 spp) with kernel time through the same readout.
falsification.challenging_baseline: The frozen ECRO operators ([measured] 0.003-0.006 on stationary and broad regions, 0.063 / 0.072 in E2 region C, 11.3 ms wall inference). A path-traced table at equal fill time. A path tracer with Russian roulette at matched quality, scored in region C as well as on stationary pixels ([measured] plain path tracer region C 0.145 / 0.078 / 0.040 at 256 / 1,024 / 4,096 spp against the learned floor near 0.073).
falsification.controls: The oracle table as the container ceiling; the STALE state; R raised from 512 to 8,192 to separate ray quadrature from projection bias; sender-only bin refinement; independent ray seeds, since WL86A used one ray realisation; the WL86A path-family truth split (two events via the panel, two events via other senders, three or more) so that each variant is scored per family.
falsification.most_likely_decisive_failure: The binned explicit recurrence shows a level bias of a few per cent on chains through the ER floor and sphere, or in region A near the boxes, above the learned operator's error there. That would show the same-state explicit fill is not a free replacement and would hand the remaining question to H2.
falsification.evidence_needed_before_training: H1 needs no training. Its ladder is the evidence that should exist before any further learned global mechanism is trained: explicit-fill accuracy and kernel time, the path-traced-table accuracy-versus-spp curve, and a Russian-roulette path tracer at matched quality.
falsification.which_of_five_test_kinds: Operator representability (does the discretised explicit operator on this state reproduce the field); information sufficiency (ray-count and bin-refinement controls); dynamic response (T1 - T0 slope in regions A, C, D against STALE); end-to-end economics (fill plus render against path tracing and against a path-traced table).

hypotheses.relation_to_history_and_prior_art: No novelty. It is the classical two-pass structure: a view-independent finite-element solve with a traced final stage (Wallace et al. 1987; Sillion et al. 1991; Immel et al. 1986 for patch x direction radiance) and light-side handling of light -> specular -> diffuse (Heckbert 1990; Jensen 1996). In project terms it is the oracle of WL86 Stage 1 with the fill made deterministic, the explicit C0 that beat the learned C in WL52, and it is close to WL84A's lobe-partitioned graph, which its own advocate withdrew (sharp part retraced, point-sampled field aliasing, dense per-edit solve). Differences from that track: patch-averaged rather than point-sampled senders and a solve that is sparse through rays; the alpha^-4 scaling objection applies unchanged. It relates to ECRO as its same-state physical control, which WL86 lists among its unmeasured comparators.

hypotheses.name: H2. Learned prolongation (sub-patch and sub-bin closure) inside the explicit recurrence
hypotheses.central_principle: [hypothesis] If the explicit same-state recurrence of H1 is biased, the bias is the unresolved part Pi T (I - Pi) b of the projected equation. The only global-side quantity a learned component could then supply without duplicating a cheap physical computation is a reconstruction of sub-patch and sub-bin sender radiance from the coarse table and local geometry, used inside the same explicit operator. Its prize is bounded by H1's measured bias and its cost must be below explicit refinement.
hypotheses.primary_operator_math: Projected equation: Pi b = Pi q + (Pi T P) Pi b, with P a prolongation from the coarse table to fine sender radiance. Piecewise-constant P is H1. Here P_theta(d)[fine | coarse] >= 0 with Pi P_theta = I, so each patch x bin cell's fine profile averages to its coarse value; the learned part redistributes radiance inside a cell and cannot create energy. d is a local descriptor of a (sender patch, receiver ray) pair: distance over patch size, dihedral angle, distance to the nearest contact line, sender lobe r50 over bin width. Table: B_H = Pi * sum_j (Pi T P_theta)^j q, with the first flight and the sharp-sender routing as in H1.
hypotheses.what_is_learned: One small local function P_theta, shared by all patches and scenes, source-independent, fixed after training.
hypotheses.what_is_physically_computed: Everything in H1: rays and visibility, ER evaluation, the recurrence, the exact first flight, sender-side deposits, the camera paths and readout.
hypotheses.runtime_inputs_outputs: Inputs: H1's inputs plus per-pair local descriptors computed from the current geometry. Outputs: the same table and image. The learned function sees no source and no radiance other than the coarse table values it redistributes.
hypotheses.persistent_vs_edit_dependent_state: Persistent: theta and H1's material tables. Edit-dependent: descriptors and prolongation weights for pairs whose local geometry changed (near the mover), in addition to H1's edit-dependent state.
hypotheses.spatial_angular_information: Local geometry at the pair level and the coarse table only. It cannot recover sub-patch structure that depends on the source, such as a direct shadow edge inside a patch; that structure lives in q and is handled exactly by the first flight. It cannot recover sub-bin structure of sharp lobes, which is excluded on information grounds ([measured] WL58; [measured, post hoc] WL86A beam pair).
hypotheses.path_ownership_and_composition: One operator; the learned part multiplies the explicit transfer and owns no path family. The target for theta is the difference between a refined explicit solve (or a path-traced field) and the coarse explicit solve, and because the explicit part is fixed and deterministic that target is unique. This is a correction of discretisation error, not a path-class partition, and should be described as such. Mean preservation bounds the energy; no learned operator is recursed without that constraint.
hypotheses.unseen_geometry_and_illumination: Transfer rests on locality of the descriptor. [prior art] The precedents that transfer without retraining use query-centred local descriptors for smooth remainders (Deep Scattering 2017; Vicini et al. 2019). It is independent of the source by construction. It has no mechanism for non-local sub-structure, and the project's own record on local transfer is poor ([measured] WL71-78: transfer within 5-18 mm of supervised sources, far-boundary failure), although on a different operator and fixture.
hypotheses.source_of_compressibility: Physical: the near-field kernel has a known local form ([measured] WL54: convex sub-port source structure with exponential decay, 94 % from pairs closer than 1 cm) and the sub-bin shape of a broad lobe is a known function of the lobe. The claim is that the unresolved part is a function of a few local quantities for broad and moderate transport.
hypotheses.cost_model: Offline: the teacher is a refined explicit solve, deterministic and cheap, so supervision has no Monte Carlo noise and no path-traced cost; training cost is unmeasured. Runtime: one descriptor and one small network evaluation per (patch, ray) pair, O(N*R) on top of H1; [inference] comparable to the H1 solve itself. Memory: weights per pair if cached, O(N*R). Comparator cost: [measured] contact-adaptive refinement (CASP) reached 35 / 36 groups at 1.00-1.04x GPU work at an equal ray budget, with unknowns 1.2-2.8x on floor scenes and 7.35x on a 4 mm gap (WL54). Scaling: the saving, where it exists, is the avoided refinement factor (up to about 7x in unknowns spatially, r50^-2 angularly) applied to a solve that costs milliseconds at WL86 size. Amortisation: one rule over all scenes. It needs the same exhaustive patch-level visibility rays as H1.
hypotheses.is_saving_unique_to_learning: No in general. Explicit adaptive refinement (CASP, hierarchical or wavelet radiosity, DASQ-style full-coverage quadrature) reaches the same accuracy at 1.00-1.04x GPU work on the measured fixtures, and an analytic profile (linear or exponential within a patch) is a learning-free prolongation. Learning would be unique only where refinement multiplies the state several times and no analytic profile fits, and even there the absolute saving is a fraction of a millisecond-scale solve at the measured sizes.
hypotheses.how_it_could_fail: H1's bias is small, so there is no prize. An analytic prolongation does as well. The unresolved part is not a function of local descriptors (equal descriptors, different fine profiles). Local transfer fails as it did for the learned K. The network evaluation costs more than refining.

falsification.smallest_physical_test: Measure H1's bias map on the WL86 fixtures against a refined explicit solve (patches and sender bins doubled until converged). If the bias is below g and below the frozen gates everywhere it matters, H2 has nothing to learn and is closed without training.
falsification.challenging_baseline: Contact-adaptive explicit refinement at equal kernel time, and an analytic (non-learned) prolongation.
falsification.controls: Piecewise-constant P (H1); analytic P; refined explicit solve as ceiling; pairs with equal descriptors but different fine profiles as a direct information test; held-out geometry away from every supervised pair and its symmetry images.
falsification.most_likely_decisive_failure: The bias of H1 is confined to sharp senders and near-contact pairs, where the first is excluded by information and the second is already handled by explicit refinement at about equal cost.
falsification.evidence_needed_before_training: The H1 bias map, the cost of explicit refinement to remove it on the same fixtures, and the equal-descriptor information test. All three are learning-free.
falsification.which_of_five_test_kinds: Information sufficiency (equal-descriptor pairs); operator representability (analytic versus free prolongation against the refined solve); learned generalisation (held-out geometry); end-to-end economics (against refinement at equal kernel time).

hypotheses.relation_to_history_and_prior_art: Closest in the project: CASP (WL54) and CAK (WL55), which are the explicit forms of the same correction; DASQ (WL49 / WL50), a learned weighting over a full-coverage quadrature, whose first-event gain was real and small (+0.3 to +0.65 dB) and whose composition failed for an unrelated reason; WL52's finding that the learned C was no better than the ray-traced transfer on the same patch representation, which is direct evidence against a learned operator correcting patch-level loss when it is not given sub-patch information. WL80A's objection to candidate C2 (a learned compression that depends on the explicit operator as teacher) applies. Prior art: hierarchical and wavelet radiosity, discontinuity meshing, three-point transport. It is not ECRO's two terms renamed: the physical part is computed, and the learned part has a unique residual target and no additive rival.

hypotheses.name: H3. Learned generator of the intrinsic nonlocal K for domains whose shape changes, with explicit coupling and explicit solve
hypotheses.central_principle: [inference] The only large measured physical cost in the K / C system is constructing K for a changed nonlocal domain. If learning is to be the unique source of a saving anywhere, the numbers place it there and not in global transport. [measured] The fidelity evidence so far is against it, and it lies outside the ER-only GM1 scope. It is listed because it identifies the regime, not because it is ready.
hypotheses.primary_operator_math: b = K_theta(G_dom) (e + C_G b). K_theta = computed zero-collision (ballistic) term + learned collided response, column-substochastic by construction, expressed in material coordinates, generated from the domain's own shape only. C_G explicit (rays). The solve is the explicit iteration over ports; K_theta is recursed, so passivity must hold for every incident field and exit direction the coupling queries.
hypotheses.what_is_learned: A rule that maps a domain's shape and medium parameters to the coefficients of its collided entry-to-first-exit operator (the WL57-80 family is one instance: shared angular bases, geometry-conditioned spatial factor, about 160k parameters).
hypotheses.what_is_physically_computed: The ballistic term, the boundary cells, the free-space coupling, the incident field, the coupled solve and the readout ([measured] together 0.685 s resident for two slabs, coupling 0.02-0.035 s of it).
hypotheses.runtime_inputs_outputs: Inputs: current domain geometry in material coordinates and medium parameters; current scene geometry for C; sources. Outputs: K coefficients per changed domain, then the composed boundary radiance and image. No target K, no reference query, no post-edit supervision.
hypotheses.persistent_vs_edit_dependent_state: Persistent: rule parameters; K coefficients of every domain whose shape did not change (rigid motion leaves them valid, [measured] WL53 / WL55 / WL56). Edit-dependent: K coefficients of deformed domains (regenerated, not retrained), and all coupling, incident-field and solve state.
hypotheses.spatial_angular_information: Entry and exit position at sub-port resolution near contact ([measured] WL55), incident and exit direction. For the homogeneous slab the incoming-direction dependence of collided transport is small and low-dimensional ([measured] about 3-5 contrast directions, 0.7-1.0 % of response energy, WL66); for direction-selective interiors it is not ([measured] WL47 mirror cavity). The edit signal is about 1 % of the action, so the required precision is below that.
hypotheses.path_ownership_and_composition: The contract's segment partition: in-medium segments to K, air to C, enforced by supervising K on isolated-domain entry-to-first-exit transport with a path-history-independent reference ([measured] WL53: disjoint rho 0.42-0.82, double claim 4.75). Stability by construction of a substochastic K ([measured] column sums <= 0.9997 in every trained model).
hypotheses.unseen_geometry_and_illumination: Source independence is structural (K is linear in the incident field). Geometry transfer is the unsolved part: [measured] fit-population accuracy 0.04-0.13 against new-source error 0.56-0.94 (WL68); transfer within 5-18 mm of supervised sources; far-boundary contrast 0.67-0.95 against oracles 0.13-0.27; no learned map met the signed-deformation gate.
hypotheses.source_of_compressibility: Physical: in an optically thick medium collided transport is diffusive, smooth and local at the scale of the diffusion length ([measured] dent change local and low-rank, rank90 8-18; a bend is dense, rank90 133-151). The compressibility is therefore edit-dependent, and it is also available to learning-free operators for homogeneous media (a three-scalar diffusion profile tied the learned K on Yellow, WL45; collision-probability operators, WL80A / 80B, unmeasured).
hypotheses.cost_model:
Offline supervision: Monte Carlo oracle K, [measured] 7.9 M / 31.5 M / 125.8 M photons and 22.5 / 78 / 175-380 s per slab at 1 cm / 5 mm / 2.5 mm; photons x4 per halving of cell size and x4 for 8 x 8 incoming bins; deformation labels below SNR 3 in 492 of 576 cells even at 128-512 M photons (WL65). Learned-state generation per changed domain: [measured] 0.015 s for the W+UV family, 75 s for FIA. Application: [measured] 1.3-2.1 ms per light. Geometry state, coupling, solve: [measured] 0.685 s. Memory: oracle K 1.7-2.0 GB per slab; learned coefficients megabytes. Comparators: [measured] path-traced re-render at contract quality 4.67 s (W1), 1.2-2.4 s (C1); oracle selective update 189 s.
[inference] Rigid sequences: a physically built K pays back after about 175 / (4.67 - 0.685) = 44 frames (95 at 380 s) with no learning involved. Non-rigid edit every frame: physical K costs 175 s or more per frame, a learned K about 0.7 s, path tracing 1.2-4.7 s. That last row is the only place in the project's measurements where learning is the unique source of a saving, and it is a factor of about 2-7 against path tracing, conditional on fidelity the learned K has not reached.
Scaling with domain volume, optical thickness, albedo and heterogeneity is unmeasured. The explicit coupling needs exhaustive port-level visibility rays, cheap at measured scales.
hypotheses.is_saving_unique_to_learning: Partly. Against a Monte Carlo-built K under non-rigid edits or for many distinct shapes: yes. Against learning-free physical operators for homogeneous media (diffusion profile, collision probability): not shown, and those have structural transfer. Against path tracing: only where in-medium paths are long (high albedo, thick media) and many frames, lights or views share one domain shape. Uniqueness would be clearest for heterogeneous or anisotropic media with no closed-form operator, which are untested.
hypotheses.how_it_could_fail: It already has, on the evidence: [measured] every learned K is 5-6x worse in absolute terms than reusing the stale exact operator; none met the directional or deformation gates; none was ever composed with C; the exact oracle composition itself passes only 9 / 12 channel tests while path tracing meets the contract in seconds. Supervision precision for deformation is a hard cost. ER materials have no nonlocal K, so this does not address sharp glossy interreflection at all.

falsification.smallest_physical_test: A stale-control test on the existing slab family: does any generated K, on an unseen dent, have error below the stale exact operator's 0.5-1.2 % at independent sources, at a generation cost below a path-traced re-render of the same fixture.
falsification.challenging_baseline: The stale exact operator (free), a learning-free diffusion or collision-probability operator, and path-traced re-render at contract quality (1.2-4.7 s).
falsification.controls: Independently qualified evaluation labels (WL61 showed 89-94 % of an apparent gap was label error); early-checkpoint versus final-iterate scoring (drift); sources away from supervised positions and their symmetry images; signed-change slope with a reference-noise model.
falsification.most_likely_decisive_failure: No learned map goes below the stale-operator error, as in every batch so far, so regenerating K is worse than not updating it.
falsification.evidence_needed_before_training: A workload where a nonlocal medium is in scope and path tracing through it is expensive enough that 0.7 s per edit would matter; an oracle fit showing a source-independent, geometry-conditioned family member exists below 1 % (WL71 left this undecided); the cost of a learning-free operator on the same fixture.
falsification.which_of_five_test_kinds: Operator representability (existence of an admissible family member below the edit signal); learned generalisation (unseen sources and dents); dynamic response (signed deformation change against the stale control); end-to-end economics (against path-traced re-render).

hypotheses.relation_to_history_and_prior_art: This is the FNTO contract's K with the lessons of WL53-80 applied; it is not a new proposal. It differs from the four-term K in having one collided term plus a computed ballistic term, a path-history-independent target and passivity by construction. Prior art: DeepPRT (geometry in, linear transfer coefficients out, low frequency), the shape-adaptive SSS model of Vicini et al. 2019 (local geometric conditioning, used as a sampler inside a path tracer), Deep Scattering. WL77A / 80A / 80B found no reviewed candidate defensible as a learned K on the slab.

designs.strongest_counterargument_to_own_best:
Against H1 (explicit same-state fill, no learned global operator).

1. Its key cost and accuracy figures are mine, not measured. The explicit recurrence over the WL86 state rays was never run. The millisecond solve is an operation count, and its accuracy on broad and moderate transport is unknown. The learned operator did reach oracle-noise accuracy (0.003-0.006) on stationary and broad regions with only 512 rays and 64 bins. An explicit bin-to-bin recurrence at that resolution may not: WL58 puts a 64 / 256-bin interface at 9.9-17.7 % loss for alpha 0.25, and the floor and sphere closures sit near that regime. If so, the learned operator is buying accuracy per unit of state through supervision on path-traced fields, which is a real, learning-specific benefit that H1 denies.

2. The evidence that the explicit route fixes the sharp family is thin. It rests on WL86A amendment 2: post hoc, two configurations, one ray realisation, a rule satisfied through a different clause in each case and by 0.4 points in one. The same data show that exact sender radiance through 512 rays is still 20 % low, so H1 needs either many more rays or a source-dependent sender-side pass. The latter grows with lights times sharp senders and is exactly the kind of separate sharp solver the brief says must not be assumed.

3. H1 may be economically empty. Its saving is the two-tier estimator's, measured only against a six-vertex path tracer without Russian roulette at noise-level quality. WL85's cold path tracer reaches the ER-gap quality in 0.39 s of GPU time on its fixture, and WL84A's coordinator wrote that at about a second or less no reuse scheme has room. With Russian roulette, a denoiser or a larger scene (the table grows with the scene, the path tracer with the pixels), the factor could fall toward one.

4. H1 is not an answer to the project's research question. It contains no learned transport response, so under the current documents it can be a baseline at most; whether a learning-free global solve around frozen ER is admissible at all is an open human decision. As an architecture it has no novelty: it is the 1987-1996 two-pass design.

5. It says nothing about scale. All of its numbers come from one room with 1,270 patches. A learned generator working from coarse tokens could in principle scale better than N x R rays, although the only scaling measurement in the project (WL52) went the other way.
evidence_gaps_that_change_the_decision: Accuracy and uncontended kernel cost of an explicit recurrence over the deployed WL86 state (binned; exact first flight; with sender-side routing), through the identical readout. If it matches the learned table on broad regions and improves the sharp region at millisecond cost, a learned global operator has no role at this state; if it is biased on broad regions, a learned accuracy-per-state benefit exists and H2-type questions open.

An accuracy-versus-spp ladder with kernel time for a path-traced patch x bin table through the same readout. Only contended wall times exist (about 0.16 s aggregate GPU per 256-spp field, 6-24 s at 4,096 spp). This fixes what a physical cache with the same state costs for a given rendered error, including the mirror-read region.

A path tracer with Russian roulette (and, if the project treats denoised output as valid, a denoiser) at matched quality on the WL86 room, scored in region C as well as on stationary pixels. This decides whether the two-tier estimator has economic room at all; the 5.45x per-sample factor was measured against a no-roulette six-vertex kernel.

Kernel GPU time of ECRO's generator and application (only 11.3 ms wall is stored) and their scaling with patch count, given the dense N x N form-factor message passing. Without it the learned fill cannot be placed on the same cost axis as an explicit fill.

Whether GM1's valid output is one camera at one lighting state or many views, frames or lights per geometry (WL84A lists this as an open human decision). Every stored-state mechanism, learned or not, is economic only under reuse; the answer moves the break-even by orders of magnitude.

The higher-order share of radiance on the intended workload. It is 23 % at three or more events in the WL86 room and 3.3 % in the WL85 open scene, where it is below the ER gap on sharp receivers (0.056-0.069). A mechanism for higher-order transport has a prize only on the first kind of workload.

Scaling of stored-state cost and error at 10-100x the patch count and at lobes sharper than the r50 0.15 rad exercised (the closure permits alpha down to 0.004). The alpha^-4 argument is a derivation calibrated on WL58, not a measurement on a global mechanism.

Whether the learned operator at fixed state beats an explicit operator given the rays that the learned generator's kernel time would buy (a state-efficiency comparison at equal kernel time). This is the only form in which a learning-unique saving in global transport could show up on current workloads.

For the K-side regime only: whether nonlocal media return to scope, what path tracing costs in a medium where in-medium paths are long, and whether any source-independent geometry-conditioned K exists below the 1 % edit signal. These decide whether H3's regime is real or empty.
designs.overall_assessment:
Nothing is selected here. The assessment is by cost attribution.

WHERE THE MEASURED SAVING COMES FROM. [measured] ECRO's 9x per-frame figure is 5.45x cheaper samples (0.331 vs 1.806 ms per spp, because the camera path stops at two events) times 1.6-1.7x fewer samples (the higher-order term carries no noise). [inference] Both factors are properties of the two-tier estimator and belong to any filled table. What learning contributes is only the fill: about 38 ms wall per edit (state 21, source 5, operator 11.3, transfer 1.5), with 42.9 MB of generated factors, a bias floor near 0.073 on the mirror-read region, and 37 minutes of offline supervision and training per scene family.

WHAT THE FILL COSTS PHYSICALLY ON THE SAME STATE. [measured] The 650,240 state rays cost 0.19-0.24 ms of kernel time. A path-traced 256-spp table costs at most about 0.16 s of GPU time. [inference] An explicit recurrence over the same rays is of the order of a millisecond by operation count and was never timed. Against a 256-spp path-traced table the learned fill saves at most about 0.12-0.15 s per edit, so the 2,200 s of offline cost is recovered after roughly 15,000 edits; against an explicit recurrence there is no saving to recover. With a 256-spp path-traced table the edit-to-frame advantage over the plain path tracer would be about 2.3x at quality 0.05 and 4.3x at 0.03 instead of 9x, with no training, assuming such a table renders as well as the learned one on stationary pixels, which is unmeasured.

REGIME MAP: IS LEARNING THE UNIQUE SOURCE OF A SAVING? [inference from the measured costs]
- More lights or changing lights at fixed geometry: no. An explicit recurrence re-solves per light for about the same cost as the learned apply; only a path-traced table pays per lighting state.
- More views or frames at fixed geometry and light: no. The table is view-independent whoever fills it.
- An edit every frame at low spp: learning beats a path-traced table (tens of ms against 0.16 s), not an explicit recurrence, and at 1 spp any fill must stay under about 1.5 ms of kernel time to pay within the frame.
- Larger scenes: no. Explicit state grows as N x R; ECRO's generator is dense N x N; the one measurement (WL52) has the learned update going from 44 to 672 ms while the explicit one goes from 5 to 11 ms. Path tracing grows with pixels, so every stored global state loses ground as the scene grows.
- Sharper materials: no. The stored representation grows as alpha^-4, the learned operator receives the same starved samples ([measured] 1-18 % of the panel family delivered), and the physical remedy is sampling, which stores nothing.
- More expensive materials: yes, at the local level, and it is already taken: [measured] ER is 44-10,600x cheaper than a quality-matched layered evaluation in isolation and 1.45-2.9x per sample in a renderer.
- Nonlocal media whose shape changes every frame, or many distinct shapes: yes on paper. [measured] A physically built K costs 175-380 s per shape against 0.015 s to regenerate a learned one and 1.2-4.7 s for a path-traced re-render. This is the one place where the numbers make learning the unique source of a saving, and [measured] every learned K so far is 5-6x less accurate than not updating at all.

STATUS OF THE CANDIDATES UNDER THIS LENS.
- A learned global higher-order operator of the ECRO type: weakened. Its fidelity on broad transport is supported on one room family; its sharp failure is attributed to a flight that is cheap to compute physically; its economic necessity is unsupported, because the same-state explicit and path-traced fills were never measured. It is not contradicted for broad transport and not shown to be needed.
- A learned free-space coupling: contradicted on cost at measured scales (WL52), and it brings no accuracy the ray-traced transfer on the same representation lacks.
- A recursed learned nonlocal K written as a sum of jointly fitted terms: contradicted for that mechanism (WL41-51); the divergence part is specific to recursion over a non-passive, history-dependent target.
- A compressed source-independent composed operator carrying sharp transport: contradicted by the information bounds in the prior art and by WL58; not tested directly.
- H1, explicit same-state fill with no learned global operator: defensible as the null hypothesis and as the missing comparator; unmeasured; possibly admissible only as a baseline.
- H2, a learned prolongation inside the explicit recurrence: weakly defensible and conditional on H1 showing a bias that explicit refinement cannot remove at about equal cost; WL54's 1.00-1.04x refinement cost makes that unlikely on current fixtures.
- H3, a learned K generator for changing nonlocal domains: not defensible on current fidelity evidence; informative because it is where the measured physical cost is.

CONCLUSION OF THIS LENS. On the measured workloads the numbers do not support selecting any learned global mechanism. The decisive missing evidence is learning-free: the explicit and path-traced fills on ECRO's own state, and a Russian-roulette path tracer at matched quality. Those measurements determine whether there is a cost or accuracy gap for a learned global component to fill; at present no such gap has been shown.
