designs.lens: Information, sampling and identifiability: what a finite patch x direction interface and a finite set of geometric relations can carry, where transport measure concentrates, which side of a path can sample it, and what a supervision target must look like for each learned term to be identifiable. Labels used below: (F) verified implementation fact, (M) measured evidence, (W) a worklog's interpretation, (I) my own inference, (H) unverified hypothesis.
designs.problem_reconstruction:
EXACT PHYSICS. Let Gamma be boundary phase space (boundary point x, direction w). b is radiance leaving an optical domain at first exit, e the incident field delivered by emitters, C_G free-space propagation (b at (x,w) becomes incident radiance at the first boundary point hit along w). C_G is a composition operator: it relabels (x,w) through a visibility map fixed by geometry alone. It does not blur, has no free parameter, and is discontinuous at silhouettes. K is an integral operator with kernel k(x_i,w_i -> x_o,w_o) in material coordinates. With the frozen ER closure K is pointwise in x ((F) closure82.py has no position argument), so K = S_ER, T_G = S_ER C_G, q = S_ER e, and b = sum_k T_G^k q.

Three partitions of path space are exact and exclusive: (1) by segment owner, in-domain -> K, air -> C ((M) WL53: disjoint rho 0.42-0.82, double claim 4.75); (2) by scattering-event count (ECRO: <= 2 traced, >= 3 tabulated); (3) by lobe class at every vertex. (3) is exact because ER is a sum of non-negative lobes, each symmetric in (w_i,w_o), under one softmax weight budget, so any lobe subset is itself reciprocal, non-negative and passive: S_ER = S_B + S_S, T_G = T_B + T_S for any lobe-wise width threshold (I, from the closure description). The resolvent then factors exactly: (I - T_B - T_S)^-1 = sum_n (R_B T_S)^n R_B with R_B = (I - T_B)^-1. Every path is a unique sequence of broad-only runs separated by sharp events (I).

WHAT LEARNING MEANS FOR EACH OBJECT.
(i) Intrinsic K: fit the kernel k as a function of material (and, for nonlocal media, domain shape), independent of layout and source. The target is the isolated domain's boundary Green's function. It is identifiable only if the probes span the incident fields the composition will produce and every exit (x,w) that C reads is supervised.
(ii) Coupling C_G: fit geometry -> operator where the exact value is a visibility relabelling. Nothing statistical is being estimated; the exact value costs one ray per query ((M) WL86: 650,240 state rays, 0.19-0.20 ms kernel for a full rebuild; WL52: 5 ms at ~10k ports). Learning C can only trade exactness for speed, and the measured trade was negative (WL52: 44-672 ms, same contact errors as the ray-traced patch transfer).
(iii) Higher-order response: fit H_G = sum_{k>=m} T_G^k, or R_G, as a geometry-conditioned, source-independent linear map. This is the only one of the four that is a derived quantity: fully determined by K and G, but costly to evaluate by sampling. Its regularity comes only from broad scattering events; propagation and sharp scattering do not smooth (I; consistent with Durand 2005 and Soler et al. 2022 in the prior-art file).
(iv) Compressed composed system: fit Pi R_G Xi, the map from a finite source encoding s to a finite output table B. This is a reduced-order model. It is well defined only relative to a declared source class (s must be a sufficient statistic for the table over that class) and a declared reader class (the table's cells must be no wider than the narrowest lobe through which it is read). Non-compactness of the transport operator (Soler 2022) means no finite-rank version has an error bound uniform over sources.

OPTIONAL COMPUTATIONAL APPROXIMATIONS (not physics): projection onto patches x direction bins; truncation by event count; reading a table at a path vertex; a fixed ray set as the geometric relation; low-rank factors; a 16-point source estimator. Each is a mollifier or a quadrature with its own bandwidth. Error appears wherever the transported quantity, or the lobe that reads it, is narrower than that bandwidth.

what_each_learnable_object_must_preserve.intrinsic_K: Linearity in the incident field, non-negativity, reciprocity, and passivity for every incidence including the grazing limit ((M) WL81: the albedo supremum sits at mu = 0 for 100 % of materials). Lobe position and width, not only albedo: WL57-66 show a model can pass 10-15 % absolute-action norms while its directional contrast is ~100 % wrong ((M) WL63 0.91-1.12). Correct response at every exit (x,w) the coupling reads, not only at supervised camera directions ((M) WL46: rho 9.4-17.1 off-normal against 0.55 at the normal). Path-history independence of the target ((M) WL51: camera vertex 0.845 against exactly 0 after a diffuse ancestor). For nonlocal media additionally first-exit semantics, a separate ballistic term ((M) WL55: -33.5 % -> -1.7 %), and an approximation error below the edit-induced change it is meant to track ((M) WL57/59: learned 6-7 % against 0.5-1.2 % for the stale exact operator).
what_each_learnable_object_must_preserve.coupling_C: Binary visibility at the resolution of the narrowest reader, direction identity (C must not mix directions; any binning of C is an angular blur), the throughput measure (closure <= 1, reciprocity), dependence on current geometry only, and sub-element source structure when sender and receiver are closer than about one element ((M) WL54: +6 to +44 % at 1 cm, 94 % from pairs closer than a port; WL52: the ray-traced patch transfer is as wrong as the learned one, p99 2.30 against 2.32). C contains no statistical regularity to learn; what must be preserved is exactness per ray.
what_each_learnable_object_must_preserve.higher_order_response: Source independence and exact superposition; exclusive ownership of a path class that the reference can tally separately; an energy bound consistent with the class (for a one-shot tail, roughly rho^m/(1-rho) of the input, I); zero response where no path exists (visibility-specific, not a geometry-blind average: (M) WL86A global term +0.04 on E1 where the panel family is 1.4 % of the reading); per-patch level accuracy wherever a sharp reader can put its weight ((M) WL86A: field flux 0.995-1.006 and wall error at oracle noise while a few patches 8-26 % low give a 7-10 % rendered deficit); and the signed change under an edit, which is small relative to the level ((M) region C change slope 0.36-0.63, ungated).
what_each_learnable_object_must_preserve.compressed_composed_system: Sufficiency of the source statistic for the declared source class ((M) holds within 0.002 for three point-light cases; fails for narrow sources: beam pair with identical encodings read ~2.9x apart, narrow-spot contract error 0.78-0.89, LSPOT panel 0.056 / 0.118). Adequacy of the output cells for every reader ((M) oracle table 0.0025-0.0137 on this fixture; (M) WL58: 64/256 bins lose 52-80 % at alpha 0.04). An identical event or class boundary on the traced side and the tabulated side so each path is counted once. Accuracy measured under the adjoint: the error that matters is the table error weighted by the importance of the reading path, not an entry-wise aggregate. Internal intermediates that the operator itself reads (ECRO's once-scattered sender radiance Bq) need the same guarantees as the output, because the operator is a composition even when it is applied once.

historical_failure_synthesis.common_to_four_part_K_and_ECRO:
Checked item by item; no single cause is forced.

1. EXCLUSIVE PATH OWNERSHIP. Both enforce the outer boundary exactly and nothing inside it. FNTO: K against C is exclusive by how probes are rendered, but K_glob / K_band / K_mid are fitted jointly to one residual with nested supports and no partition ((F) code; contradicts line 74 of the v0.1 contract). ECRO: <= 2 against >= 3 events is exclusive, but the single flight and the rank-24 global term are trained on their sum only ((F) model86.py apply; the event-order reading of the two terms is an analysis convention of WL86A). In both, one term ends up carrying another's share: K_glob carries 86 % of the Yellow red mode (WL51); ECRO's global term adds +0.017 to +0.064 while the flight from panel senders delivers 1-18 % of its family (WL86A). Shared.

2. DIRECTIONAL SUPPORT. Both use a fixed bin interface wider than the sharpest lobe in scope (19 bins; 64 bins of ~0.35 rad against a panel lobe r50 ~0.15 rad, ~0.09 at 80 deg) and both read the sender in semantics the reader does not share: FNTO one isotropic value at the port normal (5-9x low there, WL48); ECRO bin-averaged sender radiance pushed through 16 shared non-negative channels ((F)). A near-mirror bin-to-bin map is close to a permutation of 64 bins; 16 non-negative channels cannot represent it without spreading energy over several bins (I). Shared.

3. IDENTIFIABLE TARGETS. In both, the quantity the composition reads is not the quantity that was supervised. FNTO supervised first-event exits toward cameras at visible pixels and then read normal-direction senders at ports never observed (64 % of Yellow area unobserved; 82 % of predicted Yellow indirect from non-visible ports, WL45). ECRO supervised every table entry (an improvement in output coverage) but never the intermediate Bq that the flight reads, and weighted all 81,280 x 3 entries equally although the failing reading sits on ~44-58 patches. Shared in kind, different in degree.

4. STABLE REPEATED APPLICATION. Not shared. FNTO iterates a learned operator through C and diverged (rho 10.47 unconstrained; 6.9-9.0 with the WL50 arms; 9.4-17.1 read off-normal); for Yellow the proximate cause was a path-history-dependent reference recursed at every bounce (WL51: gain 8.08 x return 0.851 = 6.888). ECRO applies its operator once, has no passivity constraint, and showed flux 0.980-0.998 and no divergence. What the two share is weaker: responses to inputs outside the supervised distribution are uncontrolled (ECRO: LSPOT hl/h 1.07-1.11, narrow spots 0.78-0.89). Recursion turns that into divergence; one-shot use turns it into bounded bias.

5. PRINCIPLED COMPUTATIONAL PARTITION. Neither partition is aligned with what a finite interface can carry or with which side can sample a family. FNTO splits by distance band and local / nonlocal. ECRO splits by event count, which is exclusive but orthogonal to bandwidth: the >= 3-event class still contains light -> sharp panel -> Lambert patch -> (read through the sharp panel), i.e. the caustic family, which the prior-art file documents as unsampleable by receiver-side gathering (Veach 8.3; Jensen 1996; Krivanek 2005). Shared.

NOT COMMON: the Yellow divergence (reference semantics x recursion), the WL54/55 near-contact errors (sub-port discretisation on both K and C sides), the WL57-80 learned-K transfer failures (a geometry -> state map unidentified from 4-16 supervised sources: transfer only within ~5-18 mm; equal-fit runs disagree off-support, 0.668 against 0.860), and ECRO's failure (receiver-side sampling of a sharp sender plus a sum-only target) are four different mechanisms. The one thread that runs through all of them is an information statement, not a mechanism: each learned term was asked to produce something its inputs or its supervision did not determine, and a co-trained or downstream component absorbed the difference without being constrained to be right.
mechanism_specific_findings: Cycles 3.5.1 Burley BSSRDF applied only at vertices without a diffuse ancestor (WL51): binds any use of that reference, not learned operators as such.
The passivity hinge evaluated at the port normal on a uniform field (WL42): a bound for one direction and one field only; the same kernel read off-normal has rho 9.4-17.1.
K_band / K_mid representative subsets observe 29 % of the red in-support shadow response (WL49); full-coverage quadrature removes it at 2.2-2.8x the elements. Specific to representative sampling.

128 cosine gathers per port are inadequate for alpha 0.04 and for kappa 8 known fields (WL46, WL48: 0.139 against 0.034 with 2,048 rays). Specific to that quadrature, but the same kind of limit as ECRO's 512 rays.

ECRO's 512 cosine-stratified rays per patch with identical offsets for every patch (F): exact panel radiance read through them is -20 % in aggregate with patch RMS 0.50-0.93 (M, one ray realisation, post hoc rule). My arithmetic reproduces the magnitude: ~13-17 rays hit the panel, the half-energy highlight is roughly 0.01-0.03 sr, so 1.5-4 rays carry the family per patch, giving an RMS of 0.5-0.8 (I). Because the offsets are shared, the error is coherent across patches and need not average out, which would explain an aggregate deficit rather than zero-mean noise (I, unverified: no replicate ray set exists).

ECRO's shared rank-16 non-negative c / a factors serving three roles, and an unweighted relative-L2 loss on 256-spp targets (F). Capacity, loss weighting, optimisation and coverage were never varied one at a time (WL86A: indeterminate).

The WL57-75 learned-K family: one global geometry-independent angular basis (frozen-A floor 0.37-0.55, WL66), absolute-position inputs acting as source-identity keys (WL78), late-training drift (WL71A), labels from single low-photon realisations (WL60/61/65).
FIA's ring-lobe and azimuthal floors (WL76/77) were dominated by q = 1,024 single-scatter quadrature noise inside the diagnostic (WL77A, non-evidence, 2-3 sources).

Learned C as a dense receiver x patch transformer (WL52): O(N*M), 8-60x slower than ray casting. Specific to dense pair evaluation; the information loss at contact was in the patch representation, not in the learning.
constraints_on_any_future_architecture: Each path has one owner, and this must hold among learned terms, not only between the learned part and the traced part. Terms trained on a sum with overlapping function spaces are not separately identified; ownership then has to be enforced by separately tallied targets (path tagging costs nothing in the reference tracer; WL63 and WL86A already did it).

A learned term's inputs must be a sufficient statistic for its own target over the declared source class, at the granularity the reader needs. This is measurable before training as the variance of the target among inputs with identical encodings (WL47 equal-irradiance pairs: outputs differ 0.98-1.11 at delta-E <= 5e-6; WL86A beam pairs).

Every quantity the composition reads, including internal intermediates and unsupervised exit directions, is either supervised or bounded by construction (WL45, WL46, WL47 B0: hidden outputs wrong 1.03-1.06 and non-passive 1.77; WL86A Bq).

A fixed piecewise-constant direction interface cannot carry a lobe narrower than its bin (WL58: 52-80 % loss at alpha 0.04 with 64/256 bins; two inputs in one bin force >= 56 % error). Applies to any fixed-basis table, learned or not.

A sharp sender illuminated by a small or delta source cannot be found by a receiver-side ray set chosen before the source is known, at budgets that scale as the inverse lobe solid angle per receiver (Veach 8.3 in the prior-art file; consistent with the WL86A state-relation measurement).
Aggregate norms (field relative L1, flux, whole-image PSNR, absolute-action norms) certify neither sharp reads, nor directional contrast, nor edit response (WL42 -> WL44/45; WL57-63; WL86 -> WL86A).

A recursively applied learned operator must be passive on the fields and exit directions the composition actually produces (WL41/42/46/50). For a one-shot operator this is not established as necessary (ECRO), but out-of-distribution sources are then a bounded-bias risk.
The supervision target must be the operator the composition applies at that path position, from a path-history-independent reference (WL51, WL53).
A source representation averaged over more than about half the near-field distance loses contact and visibility-transition transport, learned or not (WL52, WL54, WL55).

A learned approximation only adds value on an edit if its error is below the edit-induced change (WL57/59), and the whole mechanism only adds value if edit-to-valid-output cost is below quality-matched path tracing (WL85: 0.39 s GPU to reach g; WL67/69/70: 1.2-4.7 s) and below an explicit GPU coupling update of ~5-11 ms (WL52).
Selective state update is not where savings are when the state rebuild is already milliseconds (WL86: 21 against 26-28 ms wall; WL59: 1.4-1.7 %).

sharp_transport_answers.is_finite_ray_sampling_incompatible: Not in general; the incompatibility is with one specific conjunction: (a) rays cast from the receiver, (b) fixed before the source is known, (c) reading a sharp sender whose far end is a small or delta source. Evidence: (M) the deployed 512 rays reading EXACT panel radiance give -20.4 % / -19.9 % in aggregate with patch RMS 0.496 / 0.926 (two cases, one ray realisation, post hoc thresholds, one margin of 0.4 points); with bin-averaged sender radiance -15.8 % / -26.0 % and RMS 0.377 / 0.468; a median 13-17 of 512 rays hit the panel per important patch. (I) The size is what counting predicts: from a back-wall patch the panel subtends ~0.16 sr and receives ~15-25 cosine rays; the half-energy highlight of a lobe with r50 ~0.1-0.15 rad around the mirror image of a point light is ~0.01-0.03 sr, so 1.5-4 rays carry the family, giving 0.5-0.8 relative RMS. A 10 % patch error needs ~100 effective rays, i.e. roughly 30-70x more rays per patch at this sharpness, growing as 1/alpha^2; the closure permits alpha down to 0.004. So 'more rays' on the receiver side is a quadratic-in-sharpness cost, not a fix. Finite ray sampling is compatible with sharp transport in two other arrangements: rays continued THROUGH the sharp vertex by sampling its lobe when the next vertex is broad or an area emitter (then the integrand seen through the lobe is smooth and a dozen samples suffice), and rays launched from the source or sender side (every sample carries energy, cost independent of alpha). The second needs the source, so it belongs to source application, not to a source-independent state. None of the alternative arrangements has been measured in this project.
sharp_transport_answers.support_without_exhaustive_rays: The support of a sharp flight is a low-dimensional set fixed by geometry: for each (sender point, incident direction) the outgoing support is a cone of width r50 about the mirror direction. Three ways to find it without enumerating pairs. (1) Follow it: sample the sender's lobe given the incident direction. One ray per carried sample, no search; requires the incident direction, which is known exactly on a ray arriving from a light or from a previous vertex. (2) Reverse it: continue a receiver ray through the sharp surface by lobe sampling; valid whenever what lies beyond is broad or extended. (3) Construct it: for planar sharp patches the receivers reachable from a source element lie in the frustum of the mirrored source through the patch, dilated by r50, so candidate links come from frustum-overlap tests against a BVH rather than from rays; for curved reflectors this becomes root finding per connection (Mitchell and Hanrahan 1992; specular manifold sampling) with cost growing in chain length. A source-independent stored form also exists in principle: resolve the incident direction at sharp patches to lobe width, giving about 2/r50^2 ~ 90 incident cells per patch at r50 0.15 rad, each mapping to a footprint of a few to a few tens of receiver patches. For the WL86 panel (42 patches) that is of the order 10^4-10^5 non-zero links against 6.6e9 dense entries (I, arithmetic only, unmeasured). The count grows as alpha^-2 in incident resolution and again as alpha^-2 once the footprint is smaller than a receiver patch, which is the alpha^-4 scaling the WL84A review derived for tabulation. So stored sharp links are plausible at alpha ~0.07-0.1 on a small sharp area and not at alpha <= 0.02; carrying sharp events as rays has no such term.
sharp_transport_answers.role_of_material_angular_structure: ER makes the angular structure explicit and available without any scene computation: 8 lobes with stated widths and weights in a 69-float state (F). Three consequences. First, the lobe-wise split is an exact, reciprocal, passive partition of the scattering operator (I), so 'sharp' and 'broad' can be assigned per lobe and applied identically on both sides of any table boundary, which the material-level or event-count splits used so far cannot do. Second, each lobe's width is simultaneously (a) the angular resolution needed to carry its output, (b) the tolerance of that vertex to error in its input, since a lobe is a low-pass filter on the incident field and a sharp lobe is a point evaluation, and (c) the criterion for which side can sample it. (M) WL85 census: on the hard population a median 94 % of albedo is in lobes with r50 0.15-0.45 rad and 4 % in broad lobes; on the iid population 50 % broad; sharp share rises to a median 0.51 at 80 deg; the panel lobe narrows from r50 0.146 to 0.09 between 45 and 80 deg. The class is therefore incidence-dependent and must be assigned from the lobe's width at the actual incidence, or conservatively. Third, lobe width bounds the rank of the local bin-to-bin scattering block: about 1 for Lambert, about 2/r50^2 (capped by the bin count) otherwise (I, space-bandwidth argument in the sense of Mahajan 2007 and Lessig and Fiume 2010). ECRO's shared R = 16 per colour is ample for the floor (r50 0.60) and too small for the panel. Material angular structure thus tells in advance which patches a fixed interface can serve; ECRO's generator received the ER state but the architecture gave every patch the same interface.
sharp_transport_answers.preserve_support_or_aggregate: Aggregate when the next operator on the path toward the sensor is a low-pass at least as wide as the aggregation cell and the aggregated quantity is smooth across the cell; preserve geometric support otherwise. (M) Evidence for the first half: with a patch x 64-bin table the oracle is at reference noise (0.0025-0.0032 stationary, <= 0.0137 in the hardest region), and the learned table gives 0.003-0.006 on stationary and broad regions on both edits. (M) Evidence for the second half: averaged over the back wall the learned table is as accurate as the oracle's own noise (0.044-0.045 against 0.043, flux 0.995-1.006), yet region C, which reads 62 % from the back wall and 27 % from box B with 89 % of the weight in one ring of outgoing bins, shows a 7-10 % deficit caused by a few patches 8-26 % low. Two families therefore need their support preserved: (i) anything deposited by a sharp sender from a small source (its level on specific patches is the signal), and (ii) anything a sharp reader may look at, which for a reader-independent table means per-patch accuracy everywhere a sharp surface can see, a sup-norm-like requirement rather than an average one. Everything whose reader is broad and whose senders are broad can be aggregated: broad-to-broad exchange, and broad senders seen by a broad receiver through a sharp surface. The practical rule is a bandwidth match evaluated per path family, not a global choice between sparse support and aggregates.
sharp_transport_answers.representability_vs_identifiability:
Four different statements were measured or can be separated, and only the first two passed.
(1) Container: the table can hold the answer ((M) oracle E_H 0.0115-0.0137 on the panel and region C).
(2) Existence of an operator on the input: a linear, geometry-determined map from the encoding to the table exists for these cases ((M) the encoding-equivalent field leaves region C within 0.002 of truth and adds 0.003-0.008 to E_H, three point-light configurations, one member of the equivalence class, region-level statistic). It does not exist for narrow sources on the sharp sender ((M, post hoc) identical-encoding beams read ~2.9x apart). So the encoding is a sufficient statistic only relative to a source class in which each sharp patch is lit smoothly; a point light averages the within-bin direction error over 42 panel patches, a beam does not (I).
(3) Realisability inside the operator family from the generator's inputs: the family computes the sharp flight through 512 receiver rays, per-(patch, bin) sender radiance and 16 channels. Even with exact intermediate values this internal route is 16-26 % low with 0.38-0.93 patch RMS (M). The answer exists but not along the path the architecture provides.
(4) Learnability from the supervision: the target is the sum of two terms; one term's feature (the ray-sampled flight) has 50-90 % patch-level error; the other term can represent the conditional mean of the missing family given coarse geometry. Least squares then shrinks the coefficient of the noisy feature toward zero and moves the mass to the smooth term. That is regression dilution, and it predicts both the measured 1-18 % delivery and the geometry-blind +0.04 on E1 (I; WL86A states the same as an untested inference; no retraining was done).
The same four-level reading fits earlier results. WL47: irradiance is not a sufficient statistic where transport is direction-selective. WL49: 29 % coverage puts a floor under any weight model. WL66: physics needs 3-5 incoming contrast directions, a rank-8 interface could reach rho <= 0.027, yet the learned basis loses 0.37-0.55 because the contrast is 0.7-1.0 % of the response energy in the broad training fields, so the supervision barely excites what had to be identified. WL68-75: per-source oracle coefficients exist (0.13-0.27) but the geometry -> coefficient map is pinned only within ~5-18 mm of a supervised source.
An identifiable target therefore needs: its own separately tallied path class; inputs whose equal-encoding variance for that class is below the gate; no co-trained term able to represent it; supervision on every quantity that is read; and target and feature noise below the signal at the granularity of the reader.
sharp_transport_answers.avoiding_global_term_compensation: Compensation needs three conditions together: sum-only supervision, a second term whose function space contains the conditional mean of the first term's target, and a first term whose features are noisy or insufficient. Removing any one stops it, in decreasing order of strength. (a) Remove the target from the learned side: if the sharp flight is computed physically and the learned term's class is defined by vertex types (broad-only runs), its target contains no path with a sharp event since the last deposit, so there is nothing sharp to compensate and nothing learned that can under-deliver. (b) Supervise by class: tally each path class separately in the reference (free) and train each term against its own tally with no gradient through the sum. (c) Detect it: a class-swap control in which the sharp lobes of the panel are made absorbing must leave a broad-class term's output unchanged; a geometry-specificity control (move the sharp sender while holding coarse summaries nearly fixed) must change the output only where the truth changes. The E1 / E2 sign pattern in WL86A (+0.04 where the family is 1.4 % of the reading, a deficit where it is 12-19 %) is exactly what such a control would have flagged. Constraining the global term's rank or adding a penalty does not address the cause; in the FNTO history a penalty on one direction (the hinge) left the others unconstrained. An estimator that adds a physically sampled residual would make compensation harmless for bias, but by my arithmetic from the WL86 cost numbers it gives back almost all of the saving (see hypothesis 3).

hypotheses.name: H1. Bandwidth-matched class operator: a learned response restricted to broad-only path runs, with every sharp-lobe event carried as a sampled flight on the side that can sample it
hypotheses.central_principle: A learned operator with a finite patch x bin interface is given exactly the path class for which that interface is a sufficient statistic: runs of broad-lobe scattering events. Sharp-lobe events are never tabulated and never learned; each is carried at ray precision by the side that can sample it with bounded variance (source side when the far end is a small source, lobe-sampled continuation otherwise). The partition is by lobe class at each vertex, which is exact for ER, instead of by event count or distance.
hypotheses.primary_operator_math: S_ER = S_B + S_S lobe-wise (threshold on the lobe's width at the actual incidence, tied to the bin width). Define the extended source e~ = e + C_G (sum_{n>=1} (S_S C_G)^{n-1} S_S) e, i.e. light carried through sharp chains until it lands on a broad lobe, and the extended coupling C~_G = C_G + C_G sum_{n>=1} (S_S C_G)^n, i.e. broad-to-broad links that pass through sharp chains (the extended form factor of Wallace 1987 / Sillion and Puech 1989, with lobe blur). The broad-lobe outgoing field then obeys beta = S_B (e~ + C~_G beta), the canonical K(e + C b) form with K -> S_B and C -> C~_G. Computed: terms k < m of sum_k (S_B C~_G)^k S_B e~. Learned: the tail H_phi(G) ~ Pi [ sum_{k>=m} (S_B C~_G)^k S_B ] Xi, applied once.
hypotheses.what_is_learned: A geometry-conditioned generator of a non-negative, source-independent linear map from the binned extended irradiance on broad patches to the tail of the broad-run outgoing field, trained against a class-tagged path-traced tally of exactly that class. No visibility, no sharp lobe, no source property and no intermediate that is read without supervision.
hypotheses.what_is_physically_computed: State rays from every patch, continued through sharp lobes by lobe sampling until a broad lobe is selected (C~_G); the per-source sharp-chain deposit e~ by tracing from the source toward sharp surfaces; the first m-1 broad events through the rays; the camera prefix, which continues through sharp lobes and terminates into explicit low-order estimation plus a table read only on broad lobes; all ER evaluation and sampling.
hypotheses.runtime_inputs_outputs: Inputs: current patch tables and frames, frozen ER states, the extended ray state, the encoding of direct plus sharp-chain-deposited irradiance per patch and incident bin. No target, reference, source identity or post-edit supervision. Outputs: a patch x bin table of broad-lobe outgoing radiance for the tail class; images by prefix tracing plus lookup.
hypotheses.persistent_vs_edit_dependent_state: Persistent: generator weights, ER states, patch parameterisation in object frames. Edit-dependent: dirty state rays and their sharp continuations, the deposit, the generated factors and the table. As in ECRO the generator and application are re-run in full per edit ((M) 11.3-11.8 ms at 1,270 patches); selective update only touches the ray state ((M) 0.06 against 0.19-0.20 ms kernel), so no saving is claimed from selectivity.
hypotheses.spatial_angular_information: Broad class: bins no wider than the class threshold (64 bins ~0.35 rad) and patches no larger than about half the near-field distance (WL52/54). Sufficiency of the binned input for this class is expected because the class kernel is band-limited at the threshold, and must be verified, not assumed. Sharp class: no table; the incident direction is exact on every carried ray; the deposit resolves a caustic at receiver-patch scale, so sub-patch caustic structure (footprint ~ r50 x distance, ~0.15-0.3 m here against 0.25 m patches) is lost unless receiver patches refine.
hypotheses.path_ownership_and_composition: Each path is owned by its vertex-class word: sharp events and the first m-1 broad events after the last sharp event or deposit are traced; the remainder of a broad run is the learned term's. The reference tallies each class separately by splitting the evaluated closure by lobe class ((F) WL85's pt85 class_eval already does this), and the class tallies sum to the reference by construction. The learned operator is applied once; sharp events inside higher-order transport enter only through C~_G rays, so there is no learned recursion and no learned term whose target another learned term can represent.
hypotheses.unseen_geometry_and_illumination: Geometry enters through rays (exact visibility at ray resolution) and local patch descriptors, as in ECRO, where broad transport reached 0.003-0.006 on unseen poses ((M); but box patches were 1.6-2.7x worse on unseen geometries and region D change slope was 0.78-0.95). Illumination: linear in the encoding; a narrow source on a sharp surface is handled by the deposit, not by the encoding; a narrow source on a broad patch is blurred by S_B ((M, post hoc) WL86A identical-encoding beam pairs on floor and wall patches were not separable from noise). Hard-edged sources with sub-patch structure remain outside any guarantee.
hypotheses.source_of_compressibility: Physical: each broad event low-passes direction at the lobe width, so after two broad events the field's angular content fits the bins and its spatial content is limited by penumbrae and contact. Structural: linearity in the source (one application for any number of lights) and view independence of the table. No statistical compressibility is claimed. Sharp events are not compressed at all; they cost one ray per carried sample.
hypotheses.cost_model: Symbols: N_p patches, N_b bins, N_r rays per patch, f_S fraction of rays meeting a sharp lobe, c mean sharp-chain length, L lights, N_c deposit rays per light, R channels, d dirty fraction, V views, F frames. Offline supervision: N_geo x L_train class-tagged tables (tagging adds no tracing; WL86: 1,024 x 4 at 256 spp in 10.7 min, training 22 min). Geometry state: N_p N_r (1 + f_S c) rays, d of them per edit. Relation discovery: none beyond rays. Learned-state generation: O(N_p^2) with the present dense form-factor message passing plus O(N_p N_b R) heads; quadratic scaling unmeasured. Source application: L x 16 N_p shadow rays + L x N_c x c deposit rays, then one operator application for the summed encoding, O(N_p N_r + N_p N_b R). Per edit: everything except weights. Per frame: spp x pixels x (m-event prefix + camera-side sharp continuation) + lookup ((M) 0.331 ms per spp at 512^2 for a 2-event prefix against 1.806 for the 6-vertex tracer). Memory: 3 N_p N_b table, ray state, 6 N_p N_b R factors. Directional complexity: table size is fixed by the class threshold and there is no alpha^-2 or alpha^-4 term, but the share of transport the table owns shrinks as lobes sharpen. Worst case: when most rays meet sharp lobes (c unbounded in a mirror enclosure) state construction and rendering approach path tracing from every patch and pixel. Workload-dependent: f_S, c and the broad-class share. Amortisation: over lights (deposit still linear in L), over views and frames at fixed geometry and light; none across edits.
hypotheses.is_saving_unique_to_learning: On present evidence, no. The measured ECRO saving is a cache effect: a shorter traced path (5.45x per sample) and removal of the suffix variance (1.6-1.7x fewer samples). A physically filled table gives the same readout saving. The same ray state supports an explicit patch x bin iteration costing O(N_p N_r + N_p N_b^2) per sweep, which I estimate at well under the generator's 11-12 ms for N_p = 1,270 (I, unmeasured; listed as an untimed comparator in WL86). WL52 measured the analogous case and found the explicit update 8-60x cheaper with the same information loss. Learning would be uniquely useful only if the learned tail reaches the gate from a smaller state than the explicit solver needs, or corrects projection error that the explicit coarse solve keeps; WL52 is evidence against the second.
hypotheses.how_it_could_fail: (1) The owned class is too small: on the hard material population a median 94 % of albedo is in lobes of r50 0.15-0.45 rad, at or below a 64-bin threshold, so nearly everything would be traced and the learned term would own a few per cent. (2) Sharp-to-sharp chains make state rays and camera paths as long as path tracing. (3) The deposit is cheap for a point light and a small sharp area but scales with L and with extended sources. (4) The explicit solver through the same rays matches the gates at equal or lower cost, leaving the learned term without a role. (5) Near-contact projection error (box on floor) limits both explicit and learned tails. (6) Even the broad class did not fully generalise in ECRO (unseen box patches, D slope).

falsification.smallest_physical_test: No training. On the frozen WL86 fixtures: (a) tally in the existing reference tracer the share of stationary radiance, of region C's reading and of the T1 - T0 change owned by each class word (deposit; first broad events; broad-run tail; chains with two or more sharp events). (b) Fill the table physically - source-side deposit plus explicit patch x bin iteration through the deployed rays continued through sharp lobes - and render it through the unchanged readout; compare region C and panel E_H with the oracle (0.0137 / 0.0115) and the learned table (0.063-0.072 / 0.052-0.056). (c) Measure the equal-encoding variance of the broad-run tail target for point, cone and beam sources.
falsification.challenging_baseline: The explicit solve of (b) itself, at equal and at reduced ray state, is the baseline a learned tail must beat. Also: a path-traced table on an accuracy-against-kernel-time ladder; cold frozen-ER path tracing with Russian roulette at the g-anchored level (0.39 s GPU on the WL85 fixture); frozen ECRO v0.
falsification.controls: Stale state; class-swap (sharp lobes of the panel made absorbing: the broad-class table must not change); at least 8 independent ray-set realisations to separate bias from sampling noise; identical-encoding pairs on broad and on sharp patches; one never-inspected edit; separate scoring of the signed change in sharp-read regions.
falsification.most_likely_decisive_failure: The physically filled table of (b) already meets the region gates at a cost at or below the learned operator's, so the learned tail has nothing to add; or (a) shows the broad-run tail owns too little of the reading and of the change on any workload that qualifies as sharp glossy interreflection.
falsification.evidence_needed_before_training: Class shares (a); explicit-solve accuracy and kernel time (b); sufficiency (c); the projection error of the explicit solve near contact; and a demonstration that source-side deposit places the light -> panel -> patch family at <= 10 % patch error with ~10^4 rays where receiver-side rays gave 50-90 %.
falsification.which_of_five_test_kinds: (a) and (c): information sufficiency. (b): operator representability. Learned tail against explicit solve at reduced state: learned generalisation and end-to-end economics. T0 -> T1 scoring by class in sharp-read regions: dynamic response.

hypotheses.relation_to_history_and_prior_art: Keeps what ECRO showed to work (the table as container, a one-shot non-negative linear operator, broad regions at 0.003-0.006) and removes what failed (the learned sharp flight, the shared low-rank interface on sharp patches, the co-trained compensating term). Relative to FNTO it keeps the K(e + C b) form with the roles re-read as broad scattering and extended coupling. It is not new as a partition: extended form factors, Jensen's routing of caustics to a light-side pass, and neural radiosity's 'trace specular chains, query at the first non-specular hit' are the same moves. The only component without a direct precedent would be a learned broad extended resolvent that stays valid across rigid edits; Modular Radiance Transfer did this for diffuse low-rank transport only. That component is also the one a physical coarse solver can most easily replace.

hypotheses.name: H2. No learned global mechanism: a physically computed, class-partitioned element transport, with learning confined to local closures (ER, and optionally a footprint-prefiltered compile of ER)
hypotheses.central_principle: The evidence locates identifiable learning targets only where the input determines the output without reference to scene layout: the pointwise closure (ER: 0.057 median error, 44-10,600x cheaper than the layered walk at operator level). The global part contains no quantity that a network knows better than the rays that define it, so it is computed. If a learned piece is added it is local: the integral of an ER lobe over finite sender and receiver footprints, which is what a coarse element transport needs in order not to alias.
hypotheses.primary_operator_math: Same class decomposition as H1. T_h = Pi S C~_G Pi* assembled from rays and solved explicitly (Jacobi or push-pull) for the broad field; sharp events as flights (source-side deposit, lobe-sampled continuation). Optional learned local kernel: f_bar(w_i, w_o; Sigma_i, Sigma_o) = ER lobe convolved with the incident and outgoing footprint kernels, a function of the ER state and two footprint widths only.
hypotheses.what_is_learned: ER as it is. Optionally a compiler output for footprint-prefiltered lobes, trained per material against numerical quadrature of ER over footprints; no scene, no geometry conditioning, no global state.
hypotheses.what_is_physically_computed: Everything global: visibility, extended links, deposit, the multi-bounce solve, the table, the camera prefix.
hypotheses.runtime_inputs_outputs: Inputs: geometry, ER states, sources. Outputs: the same patch x bin broad-lobe table and images. No learned runtime state beyond the 69-float closures (and, if used, a few floats per prefiltered lobe).
hypotheses.persistent_vs_edit_dependent_state: Persistent: ER states, patch layout. Edit-dependent: rays, links, solve, table. Link-level invalidation by the mover's swept volume is available (Drettakis and Sillion 1997 for diffuse links) but at this state size a full rebuild is already sub-millisecond in kernel time (M), so selectivity is not the lever.
hypotheses.spatial_angular_information: Identical requirements to H1 for the broad class. For moderate lobes narrower than a bin, either adaptive directional refinement on those patches (count growing as 1/r50^2) or tracing; the prefiltered kernel makes a coarse element energy-correct but turns sharp transport into transport blurred at footprint width, a bias that does not vanish with more samples.
hypotheses.path_ownership_and_composition: Exclusive by class word, as in H1; because nothing is learned there is no term that can compensate for another. Composition is an explicit solve with a physical operator, so passivity follows from the closure and the closure of the ray weights.
hypotheses.unseen_geometry_and_illumination: Valid for any geometry and source by construction, at the discretisation's accuracy; errors are projection errors (contact, bins), not generalisation errors.
hypotheses.source_of_compressibility: Physical and structural only: smoothness of broad-to-broad exchange (hierarchical or coarse-grid solvers), linearity in the source, view independence of the table. For the optional prefilter: a lobe convolved with a footprint is again a lobe with a larger width, a low-dimensional family.
hypotheses.cost_model: Offline: none beyond ER (prefilter: per-material quadrature, minutes). Geometry state: N_p N_r (1 + f_S c) rays; per edit d of them or all. Relation discovery: rays only. Learned-state generation: none. Source application: as H1. Solve: I x (N_p N_r + N_p N_b^2) with I ~ log(tol)/log(rho). Per frame and memory: as H1 without factors. Scaling: linear in rays; directional refinement on sharp or moderate patches as 1/r50^2; worst case equals path tracing when sharp chains dominate. Amortisation: over lights (one solve for the summed encoding), views and frames; none across edits.
hypotheses.is_saving_unique_to_learning: There is no learning-specific saving by construction. The prefilter is replaceable: lobe-sampled shooting is a Monte Carlo estimate of the same footprint integral, and closed-form polygon or Gaussian integration exists for GGX-like lobes in the wider literature (not surveyed in the prior-art file; my recollection). The saving against path tracing is the cache's and is published in many forms; the prior-art file lists physical caches at ~1.5-3.5 ms per frame for broad transport.
hypotheses.how_it_could_fail: As a research position it fails if the explicit coarse solve cannot reach the gates the learned operator reached, for example because projection error at contact or bin-limited moderate lobes exceed 0.03-0.06; that would be positive evidence for a learned closure. As a contribution it fails on novelty (WL84A reached the same judgement for three learning-free tracks) and possibly on admissibility: the central documents leave open whether a learning-free global solve is a candidate or only a baseline. Economically it must still beat quality-matched path tracing, which no physical arm in this project has done on the small fixtures (WL67/69/70).

falsification.smallest_physical_test: The same physically filled table as H1 test (b), reported as an accuracy-against-kernel-time ladder on E1 and E2, plus an 'exact-coefficient' variant in which the sharp links are integrated by brute-force quadrature at the existing patch and bin resolution. The second separates ray sampling from interface resolution, as WL54's exact-transfer coarse operator did for Lambert ports.
falsification.challenging_baseline: Frozen ECRO v0 at its measured 76-78 ms edit cost and 0.003-0.006 broad error; cold frozen-ER path tracing with Russian roulette; a path-traced table at matched time.
falsification.controls: Independent ray-set realisations; stale state; resolution doubling of patches and bins to show convergence of the projection error; class-tagged scoring.
falsification.most_likely_decisive_failure: The explicit solve is limited by projection error (contact, moderate lobes within one bin) above the gate, while the learned operator, trained on continuous path-traced targets, is not. That would overturn the position and motivate a learned closure of the coarse operator.
falsification.evidence_needed_before_training: None is needed for the position itself; before any prefilter is trained, a count of how many sharp or moderate links per edit need footprint integration and what lobe-sampled shooting already achieves at equal ray count.
falsification.which_of_five_test_kinds: Operator representability (physically filled table against oracle), end-to-end economics (ladder against the comparators), dynamic response (class-scored T0 -> T1 change). No learned-generalisation test applies.

hypotheses.relation_to_history_and_prior_art: This is the position WL80B reached for the medium fixture (the learning-free collision-probability operator as 'physical baseline only') and WL84A reached for GM1 (all three stored-state tracks withdrawn, nothing global learned), restated for the WL86 evidence. It coincides with classical directional finite-element radiance plus two-pass specular handling (Immel 1986; Sillion 1991; Wallace 1987; Jensen 1996) and with the cited 2025 cone-prefiltered radiosity work in spirit. It is what remains if H1's learned tail shows no advantage.

hypotheses.name: H3. Learned table used as a conditional-mean control variate with a physically sampled residual (exact in expectation)
hypotheses.central_principle: Drop the requirement that the learned operator be identifiable at the granularity of every reader. Let it be whatever conditional mean its coarse inputs support, and restore exactness by adding a path-traced estimate of (truth - table) on a fraction of samples, so that operator error becomes variance, not bias.
hypotheses.primary_operator_math: L = E[LOW + B(x2)] + E[(HIGH - B(x2))], the second expectation estimated on a fraction p of paths that are continued to full depth. B is ECRO's table or any other.
hypotheses.what_is_learned: The same geometry-conditioned, source-independent operator as ECRO v0; no change to training.
hypotheses.what_is_physically_computed: The low-order prefix on all samples and the full-depth suffix on a fraction p of them.
hypotheses.runtime_inputs_outputs: As ECRO, plus the residual estimate; output is an unbiased image estimator.
hypotheses.persistent_vs_edit_dependent_state: As ECRO. A stale or wrong table costs variance only.
hypotheses.spatial_angular_information: None beyond ECRO's; the residual carries whatever the interface cannot.
hypotheses.path_ownership_and_composition: Ownership ceases to matter for bias: the sum is exact in expectation for any table. Compensation between learned terms is harmless.
hypotheses.unseen_geometry_and_illumination: Always unbiased; efficiency degrades where the operator is wrong.
hypotheses.source_of_compressibility: None new. The table removes the conditional variance of the path suffix; nothing else.
hypotheses.cost_model: Per sample cost a + p b with a = 0.331 ms and b ~ 1.475 ms (WL86, 512^2); variance per sample c + d / p in units of the path tracer's, with d ~ 0.41 the suffix share implied by the measured 1.6-1.7x sample reduction and c ~ 0.59. The product is minimised at p ~ 0.4 with value ~1.49 against 1.806 for plain path tracing: a gain of about 1.2x (I; assumes the residual's per-sample variance equals the suffix variance, which holds because a table value is the mean of the suffix, not a per-sample correlate). All other costs as ECRO.
hypotheses.is_saving_unique_to_learning: No, and the saving itself nearly disappears: about 1.2x instead of the descriptive 9x. Any table, learned or physical, gives the same result.
hypotheses.how_it_could_fail: It fails on economics by the arithmetic above. It is listed because of what the arithmetic shows: essentially all of ECRO's measured per-frame advantage is conditional on reading the table without correction, i.e. on the table being right where it is read. The economics of a learned global table are therefore those of a biased cache, and its value is decided by identifiability at the reader's granularity, which is the point at issue in H1 and H2.

falsification.smallest_physical_test: From stored WL86 artefacts or one short render: measure the per-sample variance of (HIGH - table) against that of HIGH at the second camera vertex, by region.
falsification.challenging_baseline: Plain frozen-ER path tracing with Russian roulette at equal kernel time.
falsification.controls: Oracle table in place of the learned one (separates table error from suffix variance); stale table.
falsification.most_likely_decisive_failure: Residual variance within ~10 % of the suffix variance, confirming a gain near 1.2x.

hypotheses.relation_to_history_and_prior_art: Two-level and control-variate estimators with learned caches are published (neural control variates 2020; the 2025 neural incident radiance cache with a path-traced residual, both in the prior-art file). Their gains come from evaluating the cache many times per vertex without rays, which a patch x bin table read once at the second vertex does not do.

designs.strongest_counterargument_to_own_best:
The principle behind H1 undermines its own learned component. The path class for which a finite patch x bin input is a sufficient statistic is the class that broad scattering has already smoothed. That same smoothness is what makes the class cheap for a physical coarse solver using the identical rays: I estimate an explicit patch x bin sweep at O(N_p N_r + N_p N_b^2) flops, under a millisecond to a few milliseconds at ECRO's size, against 11-12 ms for the learned generator and application. Conversely, the class that is expensive for path tracing (a small source reflected by a sharp surface and read through another sharp surface) is the class no coarse input identifies. If this identifiability-economics duality holds, there is no region of path space where a learned global operator is both identifiable and worth having, and H1 collapses to H2 with learning confined to ER.

The project's own measurements point the same way. WL52: a learned coupling that was valid, stable and generalising carried no more information than the ray-traced transfer on the same patches and was 8-60x slower. WL86: the state update is 0.06-0.2 ms of kernel time, so nothing geometric is expensive enough to amortise. WL86 economics: the 9x is a cache effect any table would give. WL85: cold path tracing reaches the closure's own gap in 0.39 s of GPU time.

Two further objections. On the material family ER was built for, most energy sits in lobes at or below a 64-bin width (hard population: 94 % moderate, 4 % broad), so the class a learned broad operator may own is nearly empty exactly where the research question lives; the WL86 room passed on broad regions because its floor, walls and boxes are broad. And non-compactness (Soler 2022) applies even to all-Lambertian scenes at edges and contact, so 'broad' does not guarantee a uniformly accurate finite interface; WL54 measured +6 to +44 % there.

The duality has one known gap, which lies outside global transport: local responses that are physically expensive, smooth and determined by local inputs (ER against the layered walk; possibly intrinsic transport in dense media, whose construction cost of 175-380 s per slab is the largest cost measured in the project). The learned-K series WL57-80 failed there for reasons of supervision coverage and conditioning rather than for lack of an identifiable target in principle.
evidence_gaps_that_change_the_decision: Accuracy and uncontended kernel time of an explicit patch x bin solve through the existing WL86 state rays (untimed comparator in WL86). If it meets the broad-region gates at or below the learned operator's cost, no learned global term has room on this workload class; if projection error keeps it above the gates that the learned operator met, a learned closure of the coarse operator becomes the live hypothesis.

Path-class shares by lobe-class word (source-side deposit, broad-run tail, chains with two or more sharp events) for radiance, for sharp-read regions and for the T1 - T0 change, on a workload that actually qualifies as sharp glossy interreflection. WL85's census suggests the broad-only class may be a few per cent on the hard material population; WL85's workload itself failed qualification by one clause.

Whether the -20 % aggregate deficit of exact panel radiance read through the deployed rays is a bias of the shared stratification or sampling noise. Only one ray realisation exists. Bias means the receiver-side relation is structurally wrong for this family; noise means it is a budget question with a known 1/alpha^2 price.

A source-side (sender-anchored) estimate of the light -> panel -> Lambert patch family at equal ray count, scored per patch against the path-traced family. My prediction of <= 10 % patch error with ~10^4 rays is arithmetic only; if it fails, the sampleability argument for the partition fails with it.

Equal-encoding variance of each class target at patch level, for point, cone and narrow-beam sources. The existing encoding-equivalence test covers one member of the class, three point-light configurations and a region-level signed statistic; the beam evidence is post hoc and its statistic has no script in the repository.

A retraining that changes one factor at a time (class-tagged targets, supervised sender radiance Bq, importance-weighted loss, denser state). WL86A did none, so sampling limit and learning failure are not separated. This matters only if a learned sharp flight is to be kept at all.

An accuracy-against-cost ladder at the g-anchored quality level with an optimised comparator (Russian roulette, path-traced table, uncontended kernel times). Both arms in WL86 stopped short of g, and the protocol verdict is NOT TESTED.

The gate on sharp receivers is not physically anchored: the closure's own gap to the layered reference there is 0.059-0.065, the same size as the 0.06 gate and as the failing 0.063 / 0.072. A decision that turns on a 0.003-0.012 miss against the frozen-ER reference is not a decision about physical fidelity.

Edit response on sharp receivers: region C change slopes of 0.36-0.63 are stored, ungated and not decomposed by path family, so it is unknown whether the dynamic failure is the same family as the static one.

Scaling regimes in which a source-independent operator could amortise at all (many lights, many views, larger N_p with the generator's quadratic message passing) have never been measured in either direction.
designs.overall_assessment:
From this lens the evidence does not yet support selecting any learned global mechanism; nothing here is selected.

CONTRADICTED. A learned flight from a sharp sender through a receiver-side, source-independent ray relation and a fixed bin interface (ECRO v0's single-flight term). The measured state-relation result, the counting argument that reproduces its size, WL58's analytic bin limit and the prior art on gathering against shooting agree. Also contradicted: any design in which learned terms share a summed target and are expected to sort themselves into path families (the four-term K, ECRO's two terms).

WEAKENED. ECRO v0 as a whole. Its container and its broad-transport behaviour stand (oracle at noise; 0.003-0.006 on broad regions), but its measured advantage is a cache effect that a physically filled table shares; the explicit comparator was never timed; its broad generalisation is less clean than the aggregate gate suggested (unseen box patches 1.6-2.7x worse); and by my arithmetic an unbiased use of the table would keep only about 1.2x of the 9x. A source-independent compressed composed system is weakened as a general object, because sufficiency of its encoding holds for point lights and fails for narrow sources.

DEFENSIBLE. The partition principle: assign a finite-interface term only the path class on which its interface is a sufficient statistic, defined lobe-wise (exact for ER), and carry sharp events on the side that can sample them. This is defensible as a constraint on any future design, learned or not, and is testable without training. H2 (no learned global mechanism; learning stays in local closures) is defensible as the position the evidence currently supports, with no novelty and with an unresolved admissibility question in the central documents.

WEAKLY DEFENSIBLE. H1's learned component, a learned tail of the broad extended resolvent. Its target is identifiable by construction, which no earlier learned global term could claim, but the same smoothness that makes it identifiable makes it cheap to compute, and on sharp-dominated material populations it may own almost nothing.

WHAT WOULD DISTINGUISH A HYPOTHESIS FROM ANOTHER HEURISTIC DECOMPOSITION. Five checks, all executable before any training: (1) each term's path class is tallied separately in the reference and the tallies sum to it; (2) the equal-encoding variance of each learned term's target is below the gate at the reader's granularity, for every declared source class; (3) every quantity the operator reads internally is supervised or physically computed; (4) a class-swap control leaves each learned term's output unchanged when another class is switched off; (5) the physical solver using the identical state is run as a comparator, and the learned term is required to beat it at equal or smaller state. ECRO v0 would have failed (1), (3) and (4) on paper and (2) for narrow sources; (5) was not run.

Outside the study question but implied by the same reasoning: the places where physical cost and identifiability coincide are local (the closure; possibly intrinsic transport in dense media), not global.
