designs.lens: Operator theory and path-space partition. Labels used throughout: [FACT] = implementation fact verified in code or protocol (by me where stated, otherwise by the dossier's code read); [MEAS] = measured evidence stored in result JSON / worklog tables; [WL] = a worklog's interpretation; [INF] = my own inference; [HYP] = unverified hypothesis.
designs.problem_reconstruction:
Objects. Fields live on boundary ray space (position x, direction w). e = externally incident radiance, b = outgoing radiance at first exit into free space. K maps incident to outgoing inside one optical domain; C_G carries outgoing radiance through editable free space to the next boundary entry. b = K(e + C_G b) has the exact solution b = (I - K C_G)^-1 K e = R_G q with T_G = K C_G, q = K e, R_G = sum_n T_G^n (valid when the spectral radius is below 1).

Operator character [INF from the definitions, consistent with Arvo / Veach / Soler et al. as summarised in the prior-art file].
- C_G is a composition (ray-casting) operator: (C_G b)(x, w_i) = b(hit_G(x, -w_i), -w_i). It integrates nothing, mixes no directions and contains no material information. All geometry dependence of the solution enters through it. A rigid edit changes C only on rays whose segment meets the mover's old or new volume or that start/end on it [MEAS: 8.7-10.2 % of ECRO state rays, WL86; 20-21 % of paths, WL85].
- With the ER baseline, K = S_ER is an integral over incident direction at each point and the identity in position [FACT: closure has no position argument]. It is geometry-independent in the material frame. T = S C therefore integrates over 2 of the 4 ray dimensions and is not compact (Soler et al. 2022, read by the survey). T^2 contains S C S, which after the change of variables direction -> hit point is an integral operator over the full 4D ray space with kernel f(x; y->x->w_o) G V(x,y) f(y; w'->y->x); it is bounded when lobes are bounded and there is no contact singularity [INF, not verified against a source]. So R = I + T + T^2 R is: identity, one non-compact flight, and a remainder that has a kernel. Having a kernel is not low rank: numerical rank grows with area times angular bandwidth (Mahajan et al.; Lessig and Fiume), i.e. roughly as 1/alpha^2 per unit area.
- The resolvent depends on G rationally, not locally: R' - R = R' S (C' - C) R. The source of the change is sparse in ray space, the change itself is dense [MEAS: WL85 broad change reaches nearly all stationary pixels at 1.5 % of T0].

What the four learnable objects are.
(i) Intrinsic K: a geometry-independent (for rigid domains) operator on one domain's boundary field. ER is the pointwise instance and is done [MEAS: WL82-84]; the nonlocal medium K was the WL57-80 series and was not achieved. Exact part: ownership by path segment (in-domain vs free space). Approximation: angular basis, rank, spatial support.
(ii) C_G: replacing ray casting by a generated operator. Exact part: a measure-preserving map of ray space with visibility. Nothing in it is statistical except far-field smoothness of form factors between separated clusters.
(iii) Higher-order response: H_{G,k} = sum_{n>=k} T^n = T^k R_G. b = sum_{n<k} T^n q + H_{G,k} q is an exact, exclusive partition by event count for any k. ECRO v0 is this with the first two camera-side events traced and a patch x bin table holding outgoing radiance of 2..5 scattering events [FACT: pt86.py, protocol]. The approximations are the truncation at 5 events, the projection onto 1,270 patches x 64 bins, the factor form and the learned generator.
(iv) Compressed composed system: a map G -> compressed form of R_G (or of its projection) so that b = R_G q needs no iteration or tracing. Exact part: none beyond the resolvent identity; everything is approximation.

Exact partitions available [INF unless stated].
- By segment owner (K/C): exact [MEAS: WL53 disjoint rho 0.42-0.82, double claim 4.75].
- By event count (ECRO): exact, but not aligned with operator smoothness. The two-event family light -> narrow sender -> broad receiver (S_B C S_N e) sits in the 'higher-order' bucket and is the least smooth term after q.
- By lobe word. ER is a sum of lobes with exact per-lobe eval / sample / pdf [FACT: closure82/83]; WL85's path tracer already splits the evaluated closure exactly by lobe class and the classes sum to the closure [FACT: pt85.class_eval, test V2, read by me]. Hence S = S_B + S_N exactly for any assignment of lobes to a broad set B and a narrow set N, and every n-vertex path belongs to exactly one word in {B,N}^n. With P_N = (I - C S_N)^-1 (propagation through any number of narrow bounces) and C^_G = P_N C_G (the extended form factor of Wallace / Sillion-Puech, generalised from ideal specular to narrow lobes), the broad exitant field beta = S_B i obeys
    beta = q^ + T^ beta,   q^ = S_B P_N e,   T^ = S_B C^_G,   b = beta + S_N P_N (e + C_G beta).
  This is exact and gives three exclusive classes: the light-side narrow prefix (L N* up to the first B vertex), the broad core, and the eye-side narrow suffix. For passive ER (a_B + a_N <= 1) the core's gain is bounded by a_B / (1 - a_N) <= 1. Restricted to the range of S_B the core operator is of exitance type (compact when its kernel is bounded, per Soler et al.).
Optional computational approximations sit on top of any of these partitions: finite patch / bin bases, fixed ray relations, low rank, truncation depth, and a learned generator. The history below is mostly about approximations being placed across a partition boundary rather than inside one class.

what_each_learnable_object_must_preserve.intrinsic_K: Linearity and non-negativity in the incident field; passivity in every exit direction the coupling queries, including grazing [MEAS: WL46 rho 9.4-17.1 when the same kernel is read off-normal; WL81 horizon defect], which non-negative weights do not give [MEAS: WL49/50 gain 8.1-10.5]; reciprocity; the full two-sided angular kernel at lobe resolution where transport is direction-selective [MEAS: WL47 equal-irradiance pairs differ by 0.98-1.11; WL58 64/256 bins lose 52-80 % at GGX alpha 0.04]; for nonlocal media the spatial kernel below port scale near contact [MEAS: WL55 +10..+22 % outgoing flux at 1 cm] and a separately read ballistic term [MEAS: WL55 -33.5 % -> -1.7 %]; material-frame expression so that rigid motion leaves it unchanged [MEAS: WL53 within MC noise]; and identity with the operator the composition applies at interior path vertices, not a camera-vertex variant [MEAS: WL51 slab 0.845 vs 0]. From my lens it must also keep an exact lobe decomposition with sampling densities, because the neighbouring explicit operators need to importance-sample it [INF].
what_each_learnable_object_must_preserve.coupling_C: It is a transport map, so what must survive is which ray reaches which point (exact visibility support), the identity of direction along the ray (C mixes no directions; any binning at either end is a mollifier added by the representation), flux / etendue conservation (row sums <= 1) [MEAS: WL52 closure 0.990-0.997], reciprocity, sub-patch source structure near contact [MEAS: WL54 +6..+44 % at 1 cm ports, 94 % from pairs closer than 1 cm; WL52 patch-level p99 2.3 vs 0.27], and exact response on the dirty ray set with exact invariance elsewhere. There is no material content to compress and it has to beat 5-11 ms explicit updates at 10-40k ports [MEAS: WL52].
what_each_learnable_object_must_preserve.higher_order_response: H = T^k R still begins with a free flight, so it must keep (1) current pairwise visibility and the sender radiance at the sender lobe's angular resolution for the flights that follow a narrow vertex [MEAS: WL86A, exact panel radiance averaged per 64-bin sender bin already misreads the family by -16 / -26 % with patch RMS 0.38-0.47]; (2) patch-level accuracy where a reader's importance concentrates, not aggregate field accuracy [MEAS: WL86A, back-wall field at oracle noise and flux 0.995-1.006 while a handful of patches are 8-26 % low]; (3) linearity and non-negativity in the source and an energy bound per path family, since aggregate flux (0.98-1.00) did not see a missing family; (4) the geometry dependence of its low-order members, which carry the local edit response [MEAS: WL85 enabled region B<-S 0.20, B<-M 0.28 of |change|; WL86 stale state 2.6-3.9x worse in region A, 7-8x on E1's panel]; (5) an ownership boundary that matches exactly what the traced part omits (event counts, lobe classes, next-event conventions) [FACT: the ECRO probe skips next-event at the probe vertex].
what_each_learnable_object_must_preserve.compressed_composed_system: A compression of R = I + T + T^2 R can only compress the last term; I and T have to stay explicit [INF from non-compactness]. It is reader-independent, so it must be right under every importance function including near-point evaluations by mirror-like readers [MEAS: WL86A]. It must respond correctly to source classes outside its training prior [MEAS: WL86 LSPOT hl/h 1.07-1.11, narrow spots 0.78-0.89 field error; MRT states the same limit]. It must not re-represent local scattering in a second, lossier form: ECRO's shared c / a factors pass every patch's 64x64 bin scattering through 16 non-negative channels [FACT: model86.py, read by me], while the panel's bin-projected scattering is close to a permutation of the 64 bins [INF: panel closure r50 0.146 rad gives a 50 % solid angle of about 0.067 sr against a bin of 0.098 sr, and mirror reflection maps bin (ring, sector s) to (ring, s+8)], i.e. numerical rank near 64. And because R depends on G non-locally, a compressed form has to be regenerated globally after an edit; retaining raw coefficients saves little [MEAS: WL59 66 % of edges retained, 1.4-1.7 % saved; WL86 generator and application re-run in full, selective state 21 vs 26-28 ms].

historical_failure_synthesis.common_to_four_part_K_and_ECRO:
Checked item by item; I do not find one common cause.

Exclusive path ownership. Four-term K: only the K-versus-C split was enforced (through how probes were rendered). K_glob, K_band and K_mid were fitted jointly to one residual with nested supports (5 cm inside 30 cm inside global) and no partition or overlap weighting, against the contract's own line 74 [FACT per dossier code read]. ECRO: the top-level split (traced <= 2 events, table 2..5 events) is exclusive [FACT], but inside the learned operator the single flight and the rank-24 global term are trained only on their sum, so which event orders each term carries is an analysis convention [FACT]. In addition ECRO represents local scattering twice: ER in the traced part and learned c / a factors inside the operator [FACT: model86.py; the duplication reading is INF]. Shared: ownership was exclusive at the outer boundary and absent between the learned terms.

Directional support. Four-term K: exit directions supervised only toward cameras; composition read one isotropic normal-direction value per port; the passivity hinge bound one direction [FACT]; read off-normal the same kernel gives rho 9.4-17.1 and 46x flux [MEAS: WL46]. ECRO: 64 piecewise-constant bins on both sides; the single flight composes through the sender's bins and 512 fixed receiver rays; exact panel radiance through that relation is -20 % with patch RMS 0.50-0.93 [MEAS: WL86A amendment 2, post hoc, two cases, one ray realisation]. Shared: the interface between two composed stages discarded angular information at exactly the vertex where the next stage is direction-selective. In my terms a table or bin read at a path vertex turns that vertex into a broad vertex at the table's resolution; both designs put such a read at a narrow-lobe or direction-dependent vertex.

Identifiable targets. Four-term K: one target (camera-pixel first-event radiance of isolated-domain renders) for four terms; 64 % of Yellow area never observed and 82 % of predicted Yellow indirect came from ports no camera saw [MEAS: WL45]; the target was also the wrong operator for interior vertices [MEAS: WL51]. ECRO: one summed 2..5-event field, unweighted relative L2 over 243,840 entries of which the decisive ones are about 44-58 patches, 256-spp targets [FACT / MEAS]. Shared: sum-only supervision with a smooth, visibility-free term available to absorb what the structured term missed. K_glob carried 86 % of the Yellow red mode while the band / mid sender was 5-9x low [MEAS: WL48 / WL51]; ECRO's global term added +0.02..+0.06 regardless of geometry while the panel flight delivered 1-18 % [MEAS: WL86A amendment 1, post hoc].

Stable repeated application. Not shared. The four-term K was iterated and diverged (64/64 in WL41; rho 10.47 in WL42 without the hinge; 6.9-9.0 in WL50) or converged for an unrelated reason (K44 0.55 through a deficient sender). ECRO applies its operator once and showed no instability [MEAS: flux 0.980-0.998, one geometry and light]. A one-shot operator has no instability, but it also has no contraction that would damp its own error and no residual check.

Principled computational partition. Four-term K: distance bands and a rank, with representative sampling that covered 29 % of the red in-support response [MEAS: WL49]; the bands do not correspond to path families or to operator smoothness. ECRO: event count, which is exact but puts the light -> narrow sender -> broad receiver family (18.8 % / 12.0 % of what E2's region C reads [MEAS]) into the bucket handled by a receiver-side gather and a low-rank term. Shared in a weak sense: neither partition followed the line between the non-compact low-order terms and the smoothing remainder.

Evaluation. In both, aggregate measures passed while the composed, importance-weighted quantity failed (WL42 'composition adds no error' overturned by WL44/45; WL86 G1 ratio 1.12-1.13 and flux near 1 while region C failed).
mechanism_specific_findings: Cycles 3.5.1 Burley BSSRDF applied only at vertices without a diffuse ancestor, and the resulting camera-vertex gain 8-10 that made rho = gain x return 6.9-9.0 (WL51): a property of that reference, not of learned operators.
The scalar normal-direction hinge and the K44 normal-direction sender deficit (WL42, WL46, WL48).
Representative-subset aggregation in K_band / K_mid and the 2.2-2.8x element cost of DASQ (WL49).
Per-port 19-bin sender tables at about 35x iteration cost over 850k ports (WL46).

ECRO's 512 state rays per patch with the same stratified offsets on every patch, R = 16 shared non-negative factors, rank-24 global term, 16-point source estimator (effect < 5 %), unweighted loss (WL86 / WL86A). Which of sampling, capacity, loss weighting, optimisation or coverage produced the missing flight is not isolated.
Selective state update giving no measurable saving at 650,240 rays (21 vs 26-28 ms wall) (WL86).
Dense receiver x patch learned coupling being 8-60x slower than ray casting (WL52, one architecture, one patch size).
Position-keyed geometry-to-kernel maps transferring only 5-18 mm from supervised sources on the slab fixture (WL71-78).
Instability under iteration: specific to recursively composed learned operators; not observed for ECRO's one-shot application.
constraints_on_any_future_architecture: Each path family has exactly one owner, and that includes families inside a learned object: two learned terms supervised only on their sum are not separately owned (WL53 double claim rho 4.75; four-term K; ECRO term split).

No stored or learned table may be an internal composition node at a vertex whose lobe is narrower than the table's angular cell: WL58 (64/256 bins lose 52-80 % at alpha 0.04, 10-18 % at alpha 0.25), WL46 (isotropic sender bias 2.2x / 5.6x), WL86A (bin-averaged exact sender radiance -16 / -26 %). A table is adequate as a terminal container read by a broad importance function (WL86 oracle E_H 0.0025-0.0137).

A relation built by sampling the receiver independently of the sender's lobe needs a ray count that grows as 1 / alpha^2 per receiver and cannot place a sharp sender at patch level at fixed budget (WL86A amendment 2; WL48 kappa-8 quadrature 0.139 -> 0.034 with 2,048 rays; Veach's local-sampling criterion in the limit).

Whatever fills a table read through a near-mirror vertex must be accurate patch by patch at the importance-weighted locations; aggregate field error and flux do not bound it (WL86A; also WL57-63: absolute action within 5-7 % while scattered contrast error is about 100 %).

An operator applied recursively must be passive on the fields and directions the composition actually produces; fidelity to a single-application target does not give this (WL41, 42, 46, 50, 51). Not shown to bind a one-shot operator.

The supervision target must be the operator applied at that path position, from a path-history-independent reference, with local-closure bias separated by a frozen-ER reference (WL51, WL53, WL84; on sharp receivers the ER gap 0.059-0.065 equals the WL86 gate).

Source radiance averaged over an area larger than about half the near-field distance loses near-contact and visibility-transition transport whether learned or ray traced (WL52 C0p vs C1 p99 2.30 vs 2.32; WL54).

A low-rank or globally shared factor reproduces only what its training prior spans and behaves as a geometry-unspecific ambient term outside it (WL66 frozen-basis floor 0.37-0.55; WL74 rank 8 floor 0.22-0.27; WL86 global term; MRT's own stated limit).
Linearity plus non-negativity gives exact superposition but neither passivity (WL49/50) nor correctness for unseen source classes (WL86 LSPOT, narrow spots).

Economic bar on measured workloads: cold frozen-ER path tracing reaches the ER-gap quality in 0.39 s GPU with a 2.5 ms edit (WL85); explicit coupling updates cost 5-11 ms (WL52); Cycles meets the medium-fixture contracts in 1.2-4.7 s (WL67-70). A physically computed table and explicit patch-level transport on the same state are unmeasured comparators for ECRO (WL86).

A geometry-conditioned learned part is tested only where a stale state fails; on WL86 that is region A and the panel (stale / ECRO 0.87-1.6x elsewhere, though the stale change slope in D is 0.46-0.65 against 0.78-0.95).

sharp_transport_answers.is_finite_ray_sampling_incompatible: Not as such; the incompatibility is with a fixed, receiver-side relation whose directions are chosen without reference to the sender's lobe. [MEAS, WL86A amendment 2, post hoc] With exact once-scattered panel radiance read through the deployed 512 rays per patch the family is -20.4 % / -19.9 % in aggregate with patch-level RMS 0.50 / 0.93; an important Lambert patch sees the panel through a median 13-17 rays. [INF, order of magnitude] At 512 rays per hemisphere (about 81 rays per steradian) and a panel lobe whose 50 % solid angle is about 0.067 sr, only a handful of rays per receiver fall where the reflected lobe is bright, which gives the observed 0.5-0.9 scatter. Because every patch uses the same stratified offsets [FACT], the error is coherent across patches and does not average out in the aggregate. The estimator is unbiased for non-delta lobes, so more rays converge, but the count needed per receiver scales as 1 / lobe solid angle (about 16 / alpha^2 in the WL84A derivation; roughly 3,000 at alpha 0.07 and unbounded as alpha goes to the closure's lower limit 0.004), and it must be paid for every receiver whether or not a sharp sender is in view. Sampling the same family from the sender side (emit from the light to the narrow surface, sample its lobe, deposit on the receiver) needs a count set by the narrow surface's area and the receiver patch size, independent of alpha [INF; this is the classical light-side assignment of the L S+ D family: Jensen 1996, Veach section 8.3, Xu et al. 2014]. The 'more rays' option is therefore physically valid but computationally the wrong side of the adjoint.
sharp_transport_answers.support_without_exhaustive_rays: The support of a flight leaving a narrow vertex is determined by that vertex's own lobe, which ER can sample exactly [FACT: eval / sample / pdf]. Two cases [INF]. (a) Light-side prefix L N+ B: for each light, sample points on narrow-lobe surfaces, sample the reflected lobe, intersect, deposit into the receiver's incident field. Work per light is proportional to the number of narrow-surface samples times chain length; for a planar panel and a point light the footprint is also available in closed form as the projection of the panel from the mirrored light, widened by the lobe. Curved reflectors need per-sample tracing or manifold root finding (Mitchell and Hanrahan 1992; Zeltner et al. 2020). (b) Broad-to-broad links through narrow chains (B N+ B, source-independent): a receiver ray that lands on a narrow-lobe surface is continued by sampling that surface's lobe until it reaches a broad vertex, where the field is smooth enough for a coarse read. Only the rays that hit narrow surfaces are continued (13-17 of 512 per patch in WL86 [MEAS]). Neither needs exhaustive pair enumeration. The plain cost: (a) is paid per light and per edit that touches the chain, so it is source-dependent work that a source-independent operator does not amortise; (b) grows with the area fraction of narrow surfaces and with chain length, and in a scene dominated by narrow or moderate lobes it becomes path tracing.
sharp_transport_answers.role_of_material_angular_structure: It decides three things. (1) Which vertices may be internal to a stored or low-rank object. A broad lobe projected on the bin basis is a low-rank matrix (rank 1 for Lambert); a narrow lobe projected on the same basis approaches a permutation of bins with rank near the bin count [INF]. For the WL86 panel (ER S1, r50 0.146 rad at 45 degrees, 43 % sharp / 56 % moderate, albedo 0.66 [MEAS: WL85 fixture.json]) the lobe is narrower than one of the 64 bins, while the operator gives it 16 non-negative channels [FACT]. (2) From which side a flight has to be sampled (answers above). (3) How much energy a broad-core state can own. [MEAS: WL85 census] On the general population a median 50 % of albedo is broad and 41 % moderate; on the hard population 94 % is moderate (r50 0.15-0.45 rad) and 4 % broad; lobes sharpen toward grazing (median sharp share 0.51 at 80 degrees on the general population). The moderate class is the unresolved one: at 64 bins it is neither safely representable (WL58: 10-18 % loss at alpha 0.25) nor cheap to trace as chains. ER's mixture form makes the split by lobe exact [FACT], but the width class of a given lobe changes with incidence, so a fixed assignment is a convention that both sides of the partition must apply identically. WL47 adds that angular structure is regime-dependent: the Burley SSS regime was angle-insensitive within 1-2 %, the mirror cavity was not.
sharp_transport_answers.preserve_support_or_aggregate: The evidence separates the two by path family. For the family that follows a narrow sender, the support has to be preserved at the resolution at which a reader's importance concentrates, and an energy-correct aggregate is not enough: in WL86A the wall-level field was at oracle noise and flux 0.995-1.006 while the rendered deficit came from a handful of patches 8-26 % low [MEAS]; the global term's geometry-independent +0.02..+0.06 is exactly an aggregate without support [MEAS, post hoc]. The required resolution on this fixture is the patch (25 cm) and not finer: the path-traced table at patch x 64 bins reads at reference noise through the panel (E_H 0.0137 in E2 region C, 0.0115-0.0121 on the panel) [MEAS]. So support exact at patch level, distribution inside the patch aggregated. For light that has undergone several broad scatterings an aggregate, low-rank description was sufficient on this fixture (learned table 0.003-0.006 on stationary and broad regions; stale state within 0.87-1.6x there) [MEAS]. In operator terms: the sparsity pattern of S_B C S_N has to come from geometry; magnitudes can come from ER evaluation; only the multiply-smoothed remainder is a candidate for aggregation [INF].
sharp_transport_answers.representability_vs_identifiability: Three different statements have been conflated. (a) Output representability: the patch x bin container holds the needed field [MEAS: WL86 Stage 1, E_H 0.0025-0.0137]. (b) Operator representability in the chosen family: whether c / a factors of rank 16, one flight through 512 rays and a rank-24 term can express the map. Evidence against for the sharp-sender flight: the ray relation alone misplaces it by 50-90 % per patch with exact inputs, and the bin-averaged sender by 38-47 % [MEAS, post hoc]; the free-factor fit leaves 49-68 % of the deficit but confounds capacity with optimisation [MEAS]; my rank argument for the panel's bin-projected scattering (near-permutation against 16 channels) would settle the capacity half without training but is unverified [INF]. (c) Identifiability from the supervision: the encoding-equivalent test shows that some linear operator on the source encoding reproduces region C's reading for three point-light cases [MEAS], i.e. the inputs suffice there; it does not show that the training signal selects that operator. The model is trained on a sum of two terms with an unweighted loss in which the decisive patches are a fraction of a per cent of the entries, so many parameter settings with equal loss differ on the panel family. The same pattern recurs earlier: four K terms on one residual (WL41-46), hidden outputs not determined by visible supervision (WL47: error 1.03-1.06, albedo 1.77), equal-fit runs disagreeing at new ports (WL68: contrast 0.94 vs 1.22 vs 1.36-1.44), and the WL80A argument that linearity, positivity, passivity and equivariance do not identify out-of-orbit contexts. Structural constraints restrict the family; they do not identify the member.
sharp_transport_answers.avoiding_global_term_compensation: Compensation needs two things: a shared target and a term with spare capacity that is not tied to pairwise geometry. Remove either [INF]. (1) Give every learned term its own target, defined by a path-family tag in the reference tracer; lobe-class tagging exists in WL85's tracer and event / sender splits in WL86A's [FACT]. (2) Do not learn a term whose kernel is determined by current visibility and a known closure; compute it, so no learned term shares its target. In ECRO the sender's once-scattered radiance (a.c.s) and the first flight are of this kind: both follow from ER and the state rays without training. (3) Restrict a visibility-free low-rank term to a family whose dependence on pairwise visibility is measured to be weak, using a stale-state control per family rather than per region. (4) Score per-family flux and per-family importance-weighted error; aggregate flux of 0.98-1.00 was blind to a missing family. (5) A reference-free check exists for any learned field b~: one explicit transport application gives the residual r = q + T b~ - b~, and the error is bounded by r / (1 - rho); a compensated field has a large residual on the patches where the missing family lands even when its aggregate is right. None of these has been tested in the project.

hypotheses.name: H1. Lobe-word partition with a broad core: narrow-lobe vertices only inside explicitly sampled links; the learned object, if any, is confined to the multiply-scattered broad tail
hypotheses.central_principle: The only part of the solution operator that is both smoothing and separable from current pairwise visibility at lobe resolution is the transport between broad-lobe vertices after at least two broad scatterings. Everything adjacent to a narrow-lobe vertex is a geometry-determined link that must be sampled through that lobe (from the light for the prefix, from the eye for the suffix, by continuation for links between broad vertices). A learned or stored linear operator may therefore sit in the broad core and nowhere else. [HYP] ECRO's sharp failure is a consequence of placing a narrow vertex inside a composed, binned, receiver-gathered operator, not of learning the broad remainder.
hypotheses.primary_operator_math: S = S_B + S_N by ER lobe. P_N = (I - C_G S_N)^-1, C^_G = P_N C_G, T^ = S_B C^_G, q^ = S_B P_N e. Broad exitant field: beta = q^ + T^ beta = q^ + T^ q^ + T^^2 (I - T^)^-1 q^. Total: b = beta + S_N P_N (e + C_G beta). Exact. Gain of the core <= a_B / (1 - a_N). The candidate learned object is M(G) approximating the projection of T^ (I - T^)^-1 applied to y1 = T^ q^ (the tail with at least three broad scatterings), applied once.
hypotheses.what_is_learned: Only a geometry-conditioned generator of the tail operator on the broad patches' basis (per-patch low-rank encode / decode factors, as ECRO's global term but supervised on the tagged tail alone). ER stays frozen. Nothing involving a narrow vertex, the source's first scattering or the first broad flight is learned.
hypotheses.what_is_physically_computed: Direct light at every traced vertex; the light-side narrow prefix (sender-side sampling of narrow lobes, deposited into the broad patches' incident field); the bin-projected broad scattering of each material from ER by quadrature (geometry-independent, per material); the first broad flight through current state rays, with rays that land on narrow surfaces continued by lobe sampling to the next broad vertex; the eye-side narrow suffix by ordinary path tracing to the first broad vertex.
hypotheses.runtime_inputs_outputs: Inputs: current geometry (broad patches in object frames, state rays with narrow continuations), frozen ER states, the current incident field on broad patches (direct irradiance by incident bin plus narrow-prefix deposits). No light identity, no target, no T1 supervision. Output: outgoing broad radiance per broad patch and direction bin for everything beyond the directly computed terms; read once at the first broad vertex of a camera path. No table exists for narrow-lobe patches.
hypotheses.persistent_vs_edit_dependent_state: Persistent: ER states and their per-material bin projections, lobe-class assignment, generator weights, patch layout in object frames. Edit-dependent: state rays crossing the mover's old or new volume and the continuations that depend on them; narrow-prefix deposits whose chains cross that volume (per light); the incident field; the first-flight result; the tail factors (regenerated; keeping them stale is a control, not a design claim).
hypotheses.spatial_angular_information: Broad side: patches no larger than about half the near-field distance (WL52 / WL54) and a direction basis matched to the broadest class only (64 bins lose 10-18 % at alpha 0.25 per WL58, so the class boundary has to sit above that). Narrow side: no stored angular state at all; the lobe is used at full resolution through ER sampling. Sender-side deposits and continued rays must land with patch-level accuracy on broad receivers (the level at which the oracle table passes).
hypotheses.path_ownership_and_composition: Ownership by lobe word, exclusive by construction because the closure is a sum of lobes. Four disjoint families at a broad vertex: direct; narrow-prefix source; first broad flight; tail. Each has its own tagged reference. Composition is a sum with no iteration of the learned term, so no stability condition on it beyond an energy bound rho^2 / (1 - rho) relative to q^. The explicit first flight is applied to physically computed sender radiance, not to a learned estimate of it.
hypotheses.unseen_geometry_and_illumination: Explicit terms are valid for any geometry and source up to discretisation. The learned tail receives a field that has already passed two broad scatterings and one explicit flight, so narrow or hard-edged sources (which broke ECRO's contracts) reach it only after smoothing [INF]. Geometry generalisation of the tail generator is the same open question as for ECRO's global term: field-level error was 1.6-2.7x larger on unseen box patches (WL86A).
hypotheses.source_of_compressibility: Physical and structural, in two parts. (1) Structural: broad scattering is a low-rank map of direction at each point, so the core restricted to the range of S_B is an exitance-type operator with a kernel. (2) Physical: each further application multiplies by the albedo and smooths, so the tail's spectrum decays geometrically and its dependence on any single visibility relation is diluted. Measured support is indirect: ECRO's learned table reaches 0.003-0.006 on broad and stationary regions and a stale state is within 0.87-1.6x there. No compressibility is claimed for anything adjacent to a narrow vertex.
hypotheses.cost_model: Symbols: N_B broad patches, D_B direction bins, kappa state rays per patch, f_N fraction of state rays landing on narrow surfaces, c mean narrow chain length, n_N narrow-surface samples per light, L lights, V views, F frames per edit, delta dirty ray fraction, r tail rank, c_ray cost per ray segment. Offline: tagged path-traced fields over G_train geometries x L_train lights plus training (WL86 order: 15 min supervision + 22 min training per scene family) for the tail only; zero for explicit terms. Geometry state: N_B kappa (1 + f_N c) rays; per edit delta of that (WL86: 650,240 rays, 0.06-0.2 ms kernel, 21-28 ms wall). Per light: N_B x 16 shadow rays + n_N c rays for the prefix + one gather over N_B kappa entries + N_B D_B^2 for broad scattering. Learned-state generation per edit: at least O(N_B r); ECRO's dense message passing is O(N_B^2) (11 ms at 1,270 patches, scaling unmeasured). Render: pixels x samples x (two segments + suffix chains); ECRO measured 0.331 ms per sample against 1.806 for a 6-vertex tracer. Memory: N_B D_B table, N_B kappa state, N_B r factors. Scaling: N_B grows with area and inversely with contact distance squared; D_B with 1 / alpha_B^2; narrow work with narrow-surface area, lights and chain length but not with 1 / alpha. Worst case: scenes whose albedo is mostly in narrow or moderate lobes (hard population: 4 % broad) leave the core nearly empty and the cost is that of path tracing. Amortisation: state and tail over lights and views; table over frames between edits; the narrow prefix is not amortised over lights.
hypotheses.is_saving_unique_to_learning: No for the partition, the links, the first flight and the table readout: these are classical two-pass elements. For the tail the time saving is not unique either: explicit iteration on the same state is a few gathers of N_B kappa entries. The only benefit that would be specific to learning is accuracy at a coarse basis, i.e. approximating the projection of the resolvent rather than the resolvent of the projected operator (a closure for sub-patch and sub-bin structure). That benefit is unmeasured, and the one related measurement goes the other way: in WL52 the learned coupling reproduced the error of ray-traced transfer on the same patches (p99 2.32 vs 2.30).
hypotheses.how_it_could_fail: (1) Explicit transport on the same state already matches the oracle table, leaving the learned tail no role. (2) The moderate lobe class cannot be assigned: as broad it violates the bin interface, as narrow it multiplies continuation rays. (3) Sender-side deposits plus continued rays still miss patch-level placement, falsifying the partition as the explanation of WL86A. (4) The tail's edit response is below the ER gap, so a geometry-conditioned tail cannot be distinguished from a stale one. (5) Path tracing with Russian roulette and a deeper physical table are cheaper at matched quality. (6) The whole construction is ruled a learning-free two-pass renderer with a small learned ambient term.

falsification.smallest_physical_test: On the frozen WL86 fixture, with its existing references, masks, state rays and the WL86A family-split fields and no training: build the table from explicit terms only (sender-side panel and sphere prefix; bin-projected ER broad scattering; first flight through the deployed rays with narrow continuation; explicit iteration for the tail) and render it through the same readout. Compare per family against the split fields (two events via panel 0.188 / 0.120 of region C's reading) and per region against the frozen gates.
falsification.challenging_baseline: The path-traced patch x bin table at equal kernel time (the oracle with a cost ladder, never timed uncontended), cold frozen-ER path tracing with Russian roulette (0.39 s GPU to the ER gap on WL85), and the frozen WL86 learned operator on the same regions.
falsification.controls: Stale state per path family; the explicit construction with the narrow prefix switched off (should reproduce the WL86A deficit); exact per-ray reads instead of bins for continued rays; a lobe-class boundary fixed in advance from the WL85 census; replicate ray realisations (WL86A used one); a source class with hard edges (LSPOT) and a never-inspected edit; scoring against REF-ER with the ER gap reported per region.
falsification.most_likely_decisive_failure: The explicit tail on the same state is as accurate as the learned one on broad regions and as cheap, so nothing global needs to be learned at this scale; second most likely, the moderate class (sphere, hard population) defeats a clean broad / narrow assignment.
falsification.evidence_needed_before_training: (a) Rank and non-negative rank of the bin-projected ER matrices of the panel, sphere and floor at 64 bins against R = 16. (b) Fidelity and kernel time of explicit same-state transport. (c) Share of radiance and of edit response owned by the tail, by lobe-word tagging, compared with the ER gap g. (d) An uncontended accuracy-versus-cost ladder for a path-traced table.
falsification.which_of_five_test_kinds: (a) operator representability; (b) operator representability plus end-to-end economics; (c) information sufficiency and dynamic response; (d) end-to-end economics. Learned generalisation is not tested by any of these and would only become a question if (b) leaves a gap that (c) shows to be measurable.

hypotheses.relation_to_history_and_prior_art: Keeps ECRO's verified pieces (exclusive outer split, terminal table, one-shot application, state rays) and moves the family WL86A localised out of the learned operator. Differs from the four-term K by having one learned term with its own target and no recursion. Close to WL84A Track C (lobe-partitioned graph), which its advocate withdrew because the sharp part is retraced, a point-sampled incident field aliases sharp senders onto rough receivers, the re-solve is dense per edit and nothing global is learned; this hypothesis answers the second objection by sender-side assignment and concedes the first and third. Classical precedents: Heckbert 1990 and Jensen 1996 (light-side pass for L S+ D), Wallace 1987 / Sillion and Puech 1989 (extended form factors), Granier and Drettakis 2001 (operator for diffuse, particles for non-diffuse, incremental), Xu et al. 2014 (sender-centred integration), MRT 2011 for the low-rank tail. No novelty is claimed for the partition.

hypotheses.name: H2. No learned global operator: explicit lobe-partitioned transport on the geometry state, with learning kept in local closures
hypotheses.central_principle: In b = (I - S C_G)^-1 S e the only factor that is geometry-independent, reusable and expensive to evaluate physically is S (and, for media, the intrinsic K). C_G and every operator containing it are functions of current visibility that are cheap to evaluate explicitly at the measured scales and have no demonstrated statistical structure that a generator exploits better than rays. The evidence so far places the learned component at the local closure and has not shown a global learned object doing work that the explicit operator on the same state cannot do.
hypotheses.primary_operator_math: Same exact equations as H1: beta = q^ + T^ beta with T^ = S_B P_N C_G, solved by a short Neumann / Jacobi iteration on the projected core; b = beta + S_N P_N (e + C_G beta) with narrow chains sampled. After an edit the exact update is delta_beta = (I - T^')^-1 (delta_q^ + (T^' - T^) beta), whose source is supported on dirty rays.
hypotheses.what_is_learned: Nothing global. ER (already learned, frozen) supplies eval / sample / pdf and, by quadrature, each material's broad bin-projected scattering matrix. Where learning could still belong, outside the global operator: further local closure families, the nonlocal medium K that WL57-80 did not achieve, and sampling densities (where an error becomes variance, not bias).
hypotheses.what_is_physically_computed: Everything in the transport: visibility relations, narrow links from both sides, the core solve, the readout.
hypotheses.runtime_inputs_outputs: Inputs: current geometry, ER states, lights. Outputs: a broad patch x bin table plus traced low-order paths, or images directly.
hypotheses.persistent_vs_edit_dependent_state: Persistent: ER states and per-material projected matrices; object-frame patch layouts; clean state rays. Edit-dependent: dirty rays and continuations, per-light deposits, the solved field (re-solved, optionally warm-started from the previous field through the update identity).
hypotheses.spatial_angular_information: As H1 for the explicit parts. Its accuracy is exactly the Galerkin accuracy of the chosen patches, bins and ray relation; there is no mechanism to recover sub-patch or sub-bin structure other than refinement (contact-adaptive refinement cost 1.00-1.04x GPU work in WL54 for Lambert links).
hypotheses.path_ownership_and_composition: Exclusive by lobe word; the composition is the physical equation itself, so stability follows from ER's passivity and row sums <= 1 of the ray relation (WL52 / WL53 show this class converges).
hypotheses.unseen_geometry_and_illumination: No generalisation question: there is no fitted global parameter. Errors are discretisation and sampling errors that can be measured per family and reduced by refinement.
hypotheses.source_of_compressibility: Structural only: broad scattering is low rank in direction; narrow chains are sampled, not stored; the dirty set of an edit is a small part of ray space. No statistical compressibility is assumed.
hypotheses.cost_model: Same symbols as H1. Offline: none. State: N_B kappa (1 + f_N c) rays; edit: delta of it. Per light: shadow rays + n_N c prefix rays. Solve: I iterations x (N_B kappa gathers + N_B D_B^2 scattering), I about log(tol) / log(rho) (3-5 at the measured higher-order shares of 3-24 %, tens in a closed high-albedo room). Render and memory as H1 without factors. Worst case as H1: narrow-dominated scenes reduce to path tracing; large N_B with fine contact refinement raises state cost linearly. Amortisation: state over lights and views, solved table over frames; the solve is per light.
hypotheses.is_saving_unique_to_learning: Not applicable; this is the physical representation with the same state against which any learned saving has to be shown.
hypotheses.how_it_could_fail: (1) Projection error: patch-averaged sources lose near-contact and visibility-transition transport (WL52, WL54), and 64 bins lose 10-18 % at alpha 0.25 (WL58); if the explicit table misses the gates where the learned ECRO table passed, a learned closure has a demonstrated role and H2 is weakened. (2) Scale: N_B kappa and the per-light solve may not stay in the millisecond range for large scenes; unmeasured. (3) Admissibility: a mechanism without learned global state cannot be reported as selective recomputation of learned transport, and whether a learning-free global solve around frozen ER counts as a candidate or only as a baseline is an open owner decision (WL84A X7). (4) It has no novelty as a method.

falsification.smallest_physical_test: The same explicit-table construction as in H1's test, read as a test of this hypothesis: does a learning-free table on the deployed state reach the stationary and region gates, including E2 region C, and at what kernel time.
falsification.challenging_baseline: The frozen learned ECRO operator on broad regions (0.003-0.006), the path-traced table, and cold path tracing at matched quality.
falsification.controls: Refinement ladder in patches, bins and rays to separate projection error from sampling error; replicate ray realisations; per-family scoring against tagged references; stale state.
falsification.most_likely_decisive_failure: Projection error at coarse patches on broad regions that the learned operator did not show, or loss of the economic margin once narrow continuations and per-light solves are counted.
falsification.evidence_needed_before_training: None is trained; the evidence needed is the measurement itself plus a statement from the owner on admissibility.
falsification.which_of_five_test_kinds: Information sufficiency and operator representability (fidelity of the explicit table), dynamic response (edit slopes per family), end-to-end economics (kernel time against path tracing and the path-traced table).

hypotheses.relation_to_history_and_prior_art: This is the unmeasured comparator named in WL86's own unresolved questions, the class of the learning-free candidates set aside in WL77A / WL80A / WL80B (collision-probability K) and of WL84A Track C's residual role. Prior art: two-pass radiosity with extended form factors, photon-map style light-side passes, incremental radiosity and line-space invalidation. It is consistent with every measured positive in the project: explicit coupling verified (WL45, WL52), disjoint composition stable (WL53), exact selective equals full (WL56), ER valid locally (WL82-84).

hypotheses.name: H3. Learned operator as a non-owning approximate resolvent: defect correction with a physically computed residual
hypotheses.central_principle: A learned global operator need not own any path family. If it is used only as an approximate inverse M of A = I - T^ and the physical operator is applied once to its output, its error is multiplied by T^ and is bounded by a computed residual. Identifiability and compensation then affect cost, not correctness.
hypotheses.primary_operator_math: b~ = M(G) q^; r = q^ - A b~ = q^ + T^ b~ - b~; output b1 = b~ + r = q^ + T^ b~. Then b - b1 = T^ (b - b~) and ||b - b~|| <= ||r|| / (1 - rho). Iterating gives a preconditioned Richardson scheme with error propagator I - M A, whose fixed point is the explicit system's solution whenever it converges.
hypotheses.what_is_learned: A geometry-conditioned approximate resolvent on the broad core (low-rank plus local terms). Its target is the full core solution, but nothing downstream depends on it being exact.
hypotheses.what_is_physically_computed: The operator T^ itself (state rays, narrow links, ER projections), the residual, and the final application; all terms of H2.
hypotheses.runtime_inputs_outputs: Inputs as H1. Outputs: the corrected table and, as a by-product, a per-patch residual that is an error indicator available at run time without a reference.
hypotheses.persistent_vs_edit_dependent_state: As H2, plus the generator weights (persistent) and the generated factors (edit-dependent).
hypotheses.spatial_angular_information: As H2 for the explicit operator. The learned part only needs the slowly converging, spatially smooth modes of the core.
hypotheses.path_ownership_and_composition: Every family is owned by the explicit operator. The learned operator is an initial guess; exclusivity is trivially satisfied. Stability requires that the residual decreases, which is checked from computed quantities and can gate acceptance of the learned guess.
hypotheses.unseen_geometry_and_illumination: Poor generalisation shows up as a large residual and more explicit work, not as a biased result, provided at least one explicit application follows and the acceptance test is honoured.
hypotheses.source_of_compressibility: Physical: plain iteration converges slowest on the modes with gain near rho, which in an enclosure are the smooth, ambient-like ones, and those are the modes a low-rank geometry-conditioned term represented well in WL86. The complementarity is the standard two-level argument [INF].
hypotheses.cost_model: Per light: one generator application O(N_B r) plus k explicit sweeps of H2's cost instead of I sweeps. Saving is (I - k) sweeps, positive only when I is large, i.e. rho near 1. Offline cost as H1. On the measured workloads the higher-order share is 3 % (WL85) to 24 % (WL86), I is 3-5 and a sweep is at millisecond scale, so the saving is at most a few milliseconds per light. Worst case: a poor M gives more sweeps than plain iteration.
hypotheses.is_saving_unique_to_learning: No. Coarse-grid correction, a per-scene low-rank precompute or warm-starting from the pre-edit solution give the same kind of saving. Learning contributes only the ability to produce the coarse operator for a new geometry without per-scene precomputation (the role DeepPRT plays for self-transfer).
hypotheses.how_it_could_fail: No economic window at measured scales; explicit sweeps already cheap; M not contractive on some geometry so the correction is rejected; the explicit operator's own projection error is untouched.

falsification.smallest_physical_test: Apply one explicit transport step to the frozen WL86 tables (learned and oracle) and compare the per-patch residual with the known per-patch error from WL86A; then count explicit sweeps to a fixed tolerance from the learned start, a zero start and a stale-solution start.
falsification.challenging_baseline: Warm start from the pre-edit solution, and plain iteration.
falsification.controls: Oracle table (residual should be at noise), learned table with a term removed (residual should rise where the family lands), high-albedo variant of the room for the sweep count.
falsification.most_likely_decisive_failure: Sweep count from a stale or zero start is already 3-5 and the learned start saves one or two millisecond-scale sweeps.
falsification.evidence_needed_before_training: The iteration count and sweep cost of the explicit core on the target workload; if their product is small there is nothing to accelerate.
falsification.which_of_five_test_kinds: Operator representability (residual as indicator), learned generalisation (residual on unseen geometry), end-to-end economics (sweeps saved). It is not a dynamic-response or information-sufficiency test.

hypotheses.relation_to_history_and_prior_art: Uses the fact that WL86's learned table is close on broad regions and wrong on a few patches: the residual would localise exactly those patches. Related published ideas: residual minimisation in Neural Radiosity (per scene), two-level estimators with a cached term plus a path-traced residual (NIRC), control variates; the survey found no learned preconditioner for the surface rendering equation, which is a weak negative. Its main use here is as an evaluation instrument for any learned global operator, since a small importance-weighted residual under the explicit operator is evidence that separates a transport operator from a fitted decomposition.

designs.strongest_counterargument_to_own_best:
Against H1 (the best learned hypothesis from this lens).
1. It is the classical multi-pass architecture with a small learned ambient term. Every element except the tail generator is published (light-side pass for L S+ D, extended form factors, final-gather table, incremental update), and the tail generator is the part whose necessity is least supported. WL84A's Track C, which is close, was withdrawn by its own advocate with the remark that nothing global is learned and that the sharp part is a retracer; H1 concedes both.
2. At the measured scale the explicit version of every term costs milliseconds, so the learned tail has no time to save, and the only measurement of a learned operator against ray-traced transfer on the same patches (WL52: p99 2.32 vs 2.30) says the learned operator inherits the projection error instead of correcting it. If that holds, the one benefit specific to learning (closure at a coarse basis) does not exist.
3. The census undermines the premise that a broad core owns much: on the hard material population 94 % of albedo is in moderate lobes and 4 % in broad ones, and lobes sharpen toward grazing. On such scenes H1 degenerates to path tracing with bookkeeping, while cold frozen-ER path tracing already reaches the ER-gap quality in 0.39 s GPU with no state.
4. The explanatory claim is not uniquely supported. WL86A leaves ray sampling, factor capacity, loss weighting, optimisation and coverage un-isolated, the decisive amendments are post hoc and marginal in one case (-20.4 % against a 20 % rule), and my rank argument about the panel's bin-projected scattering is an inference that nobody has computed. A denser relation, a reweighted loss or a higher channel count inside the unchanged ECRO partition might close a 0.003-0.012 gate miss, in which case the re-partition is unnecessary for that workload.
5. The edit response that a geometry-conditioned tail would have to carry may be unmeasurable: outside region A and the panel a stale ECRO state is within 0.87-1.6x, and the broad multi-bounce change on WL85 is 1.5 % of T0 against an ER gap of 1.7 %.
evidence_gaps_that_change_the_decision: Fidelity and uncontended kernel cost of explicit patch-level transport on ECRO's own state (bin-projected ER, deployed rays, explicit iteration), with and without a sender-side treatment of the light -> narrow sender -> broad receiver family. If it matches the oracle table, no learned global operator has a role at this scale; if it fails on broad regions where the learned table passed, learning has a role as a closure; if the sender-side term does not restore region C, the partition explanation of WL86A is wrong.

Rank and non-negative rank of the bin-projected ER scattering matrices of the panel, sphere and floor at 64 bins against the 16 channels of ECRO's shared factors. This separates capacity from optimisation, which WL86A left indeterminate, without any training.

Lobe-word-tagged shares of radiance and of edit response per region: narrow prefix, links through narrow chains, first broad flight, tail. If the tail's change is below the ER gap, a geometry-conditioned learned tail cannot be tested on these workloads and 'learned global edit response' has no measurable content there.

An accuracy-versus-cost ladder, uncontended, for a path-traced patch x bin table and for a path tracer with Russian roulette. Without it no stored-table mechanism, learned or explicit, has an economic reference (WL86 timed neither).

Behaviour of the moderate lobe class (r50 0.15-0.45 rad) at a binned interface: error of composing through such a vertex at 64 bins against the cost of continuing rays through it. This fixes where a broad / narrow boundary can sit and therefore how much energy any stored core can own (4 % on the hard population, 50 % on the general one).

A workload with a gain near one (closed, high-albedo glossy enclosure) or with many lights or views per geometry state. Operator reuse and any learned acceleration only have room there; both g and cost are unmeasured for such a case.

Replication of WL86A amendment 2 with independent ray realisations and a third, never-inspected edit, since the sampling-limit label holds through a different clause in each of two cases and one margin is 0.4 points.

The owner's ruling on whether a learning-free global solve around frozen ER is an admissible candidate or only a baseline, and whether multi-view / multi-light workloads are inside GM1. Both change which of H1-H3 can count as an answer.
designs.overall_assessment:
Nothing is selected and I do not think the evidence supports selecting a learned global mechanism yet.

Contradicted by evidence, for the forms tested: (a) a learned operator that composes internally through a fixed bin or ray interface at a narrow-lobe or direction-dependent vertex (four-term K with an isotropic sender: WL46, WL48; ECRO's single learned flight: WL86A; the analytic bound of WL58); (b) a recursively composed learned intrinsic operator without passivity in the queried directions (WL41, 42, 46, 50, 51); (c) multi-term learned decompositions supervised only on their sum as a way to obtain separately meaningful terms (four-term K, ECRO).

Weakened: a learned replacement of the coupling (WL52, cost and contact fidelity); a low-rank, visibility-free term as owner of any family that depends on pairwise visibility (WL86A, post hoc); the geometry-conditioned generator as the carrier of edit response (tested only locally; stale within 0.87-1.6x elsewhere); the economics of any stored state at WL85 / WL86 scale (0.39 s GPU cold path tracing; explicit comparators untimed).

Defensible: (1) as a structural statement, the lobe-word partition: narrow-lobe vertices only in sampled links assigned to the side that can sample them, stored linear state only between broad vertices, a table only as a terminal container. It is exact given ER's mixture form and consistent with every measurement I checked, but it has not been measured as a whole and its account of WL86A competes with un-isolated alternatives. (2) H2, the explicit operator on that partition with learning kept local: it is the comparator the project has not measured and the null that a learned mechanism must beat. (3) H1's learned tail only conditionally, as a closure for coarse-basis projection error, with one measurement (WL52) pointing against it. H3 is not an economic mechanism on measured workloads; its residual identity is useful as a reference-free test of whether a learned field satisfies the transport equation where it matters.

What would distinguish a physically grounded learned operator from another heuristic decomposition, from this lens: each learned term owns a path family defined by an exact partition of path space and is supervised on that family alone; no learned term contains a narrow-lobe vertex or a current-visibility flight; its output has a small importance-weighted residual under one explicit transport application; and it beats the explicit operator on the same state in accuracy at equal state or in cost at equal accuracy. None of the mechanisms run so far was tested against the last two.

factual_errors_in_proposal.claim: WL46 is in-project evidence that a sharp sender's contribution must be placed by sampling the sender's lobe ('WL46 finding (directional sender read plus lobe sampling)'; 'sharp transport failed exactly where a narrow sender lobe met that sampling (WL46: -16 % vs -0.4 %)'; 'in-project evidence is thin: only WL46').
factual_errors_in_proposal.correction: WL46's sampling gain is lobe importance sampling at the glossy RECEIVER (the analytic GGX plane gathering from the Lego), i.e. ordinary reader-side BSDF sampling. The -16 % / -0.4 % contract is cosine gathers vs lobe sampling at an alpha 0.04 receiver. WL48 KF was fixed by more receiver-side rays (128 -> 2048), not by sender-side sampling. The project therefore has NO measurement of a sender-driven relation; WL86A amendment 2 shows only that the receiver-side relation fails, not that a sender-side one succeeds.

factual_errors_in_proposal.claim: 'Every learned object that took scene geometry as an input failed ... (learned C, WL52; geometry -> spatial factor, WL57-80; ECRO generator)' versus 'the one learned object that met its gates (ER) takes none', used as the basis for confining learning to K.
factual_errors_in_proposal.correction: The WL57-80 object is not a scene-geometry-conditioned global object. It is an intrinsic first-exit K of one isolated slab, conditioned on the domain's own (intrinsic) geometry in material coordinates and never run in a coupled solve. It is exactly the proposal's object (i) and H1's GM2 content. The evidence split is 'geometry-conditioned (intrinsic or scene) fails / geometry-free pointwise succeeds', not 'K succeeds / non-K fails'.

factual_errors_in_proposal.correction: The global term is a.P.(sum_j area_j Q_j.(c.s)_j): it sits once between c and a (a P Q c s), not between two applications of S_hat = a c^T.
