per_hypothesis.name: H1 - Intrinsic-only learning (certified sampleable first-exit K; C and the multi-bounce solve physically computed; no learned global operator)
per_hypothesis.physical_correctness_and_ownership: At GM1 it is correct by construction: it is an unbiased path tracer with the frozen ER closure, so every segment has one owner, nothing is applied recursively outside its certificate, and the K/C contract is respected. But this is reference level (b) of Architecture.md section 3 ('frozen ER with full path tracing as the local-approximation ceiling'), and the roadmap GM1 row states that 'implementing a full retracer does not complete GM1'. The mechanism description is internally inconsistent: it says angular support is obtained 'on the sender side', yet measurement is 'through the adjoint walk from the camera'. In a camera-side walk the light -> sharp sender -> diffuse receiver family is still reached by a cosine gather at the receiver and resolved only by NEE through the sender lobe; by Veach 8.3 this degenerates as the lobe narrows (the closure permits alpha down to 0.004; WL85 exercised only r50 ~0.15 rad). 'Support follows the material' therefore holds for reader lobes only. At GM2 the nonlocal kernel is under-specified: column-normalisation gives passivity but not reciprocity, and a non-reciprocal learned sampler used in a camera-side (adjoint) walk needs a consistent adjoint kernel, which is not provided. Under non-rigid edits K is 'regenerated by the compiler', an operation every learned map in WL71-75 failed (signed-deformation gate).
per_hypothesis.information_and_identifiability: At GM1 nothing global is learned, so there is nothing to identify; the sharp-sender relation is not carried by any representation, only by Monte Carlo variance. At GM2 the claim is that intrinsic local geometry determines a first-exit kernel through a learned compiler. This is the object WL57-80 tested: transfer limited to 5-18 mm from supervised sources; BND_FAR contrast 0.79-0.82 against oracles 0.16-0.27 (WL75); equal-fit runs disagree on held-out sources (0.668 / 0.860, WL78); late-training drift; oracle existence not evidence a rule can produce it. WL47 shows hidden outputs are wrong and non-passive without full-boundary supervision. The proposal's own induction ('geometry-conditioned learning fails, geometry-free learning works') predicts failure of H1's only non-trivial learned content. The proposed four-arm test (L, X, Xs, P tables) cannot identify H1: none of the arms is H1's mechanism (H1 has no table). X shares the 512-ray state's sharp-sender limit (-20 %, patch RMS 0.50-0.93 with exact sender radiance) and the 0.35-rad bin interface, and Xs changes the state, so it is not a same-state control.
per_hypothesis.economics_vs_matched_explicit_computatio: Against plain path tracing with frozen ER the ratio is identically 1.0, because H1 is that computation: 0.73 ms GPU per spp at 512^2, 0.39 s to g, 1.17 s to 1 % error, 2.5 ms edit (WL85; workload formally INDETERMINATE). Against the layered reference the gain is the local-closure gain only: 1.45-1.63x per spp (WL84), 2.86x (WL85), no wall-clock gain; WL80D found parity (eval_pdf 0.94x) against a cheap analytic BSDF. Path-traced table and explicit patch-level transport are not comparators for H1 itself. For the proposed test they are unmeasured as cost ladders: path-traced table 6.3-24.4 s contended wall at 4,096 spp and ~1.2 s per lighting at 256 spp; explicit binned solve on the 512-ray state never timed (nearest: WL52 explicit C update 5.0 / 11.1 ms, apply 0.1-0.6 ms; ECRO state rebuild 26-28 ms wall, 0.19-0.20 ms kernel). GM2: no cost exists for a learned nonlocal sampler; the bar is the in-medium walk itself (Cycles met the medium contract at 4 spp in 4.67 s, WL67), and the oracle K costs 175-380 s and 2 GB per slab. No saving is unique to learning at GM1; at GM2 the candidate saving is the same as a tabulated K or a published sampling model.
per_hypothesis.novelty_and_prior_art: None at GM1: path tracing with a neural/compiled BSDF and BSDF importance sampling. This is a renaming of the project's own REF-ER reference role. The GM2 extension is Vicini, Koltun, Jakob 2019 (learned shape-adaptive SSS sampling model with a pdf, conditioned on local geometry) and Deep Scattering's exact low-order plus learned local remainder. The topic document excludes a fast BSDF surrogate and BSSRDF approximation as contributions; the proposal concedes this.
per_hypothesis.consistency_with_measured_evidence: Supports: ER median E_L1 0.057 on 650 new materials; K rigid invariance 1.00-1.05x seed noise (WL53); learned C loses to explicit C (44 / 672 vs 5.0 / 11.1 ms, WL52). Contradicts or limits: ER's own gap on sharp receivers is 0.059-0.065 against a 0.06 gate, so H1's output sits at the gate against the physical reference exactly where GM1 is defined; the H1-type nonlocal K failed every transfer and deformation gate (WL57-80) and was 6-7 % against a stale exact K of 0.5-1.2 %; the 'learning works only in K' pattern rests on one success (ER, three re-qualified images, one material family); ECRO's broad-class result (E_H 0.003-0.006, 5.45x cheaper samples) is unexplained by H1 until the same-state comparator exists.
fatal_objections: As a GM1 answer it is the reference level, not a hypothesis about learned global transport: by construction it has no learned global object, no edit-response mechanism beyond re-rendering, and a cost ratio of 1.0 against frozen-ER path tracing; the roadmap excludes 'implementing a full retracer' as completing GM1.

Its central induction misclassifies WL57-80. Correctly classified, the evidence predicts that H1's only non-trivial learned content (a geometry-conditioned nonlocal K) fails, so the hypothesis has no supported learned component beyond the existing baseline.
non_fatal_objections: The proposed decisive test compares ECRO with binned physical tables and cannot confirm or refute H1's own mechanism; an L-over-X win could be regularisation of a 512-ray state (WL52 precedent), which says nothing about path tracing.
Sender-side sampling is asserted but the stated walk is camera-side; no in-project measurement of a sender-driven relation exists (WL46 was receiver-side).
Reciprocity / adjoint consistency and certified passivity of a learned nonlocal sampler are unspecified.
Sharp chains with small lights need light-side or manifold methods whose cost grows with chain length; unmeasured in the project.
ER qualification is narrow (3 images, one family) and the bias asymptote is unmeasured.
per_hypothesis.what_would_change_the_verdict: Upward: (a) a human contract decision that a learning-free global mechanism around frozen ER is an admissible GM1 candidate and not only a baseline; (b) a sampleable nonlocal first-exit closure family with a direct-fit ceiling on the WL53/55 oracle scored at sources away from every fitted source and its symmetry images with a low-noise first flight, followed by learned transfer meeting the 0.25 contrast and signed-deformation gates, and a per-sample cost below the in-medium walk; (c) the accuracy-vs-kernel-time ladder (path-traced table, same-state binned solve, learned table) showing no class where the learned operator wins beyond seed spread. Item (c) alone would uphold the null statement but would not make H1 an architecture. Downward to refuted as a research position: any class where a learned global operator beats the best same-state physical arm at matched cost.

per_hypothesis.name: H2 - Enclosure-bounded intrinsic operator (optical domain extended to a rigid assembly including enclosed air)
per_hypothesis.physical_correctness_and_ownership: The Schur-complement operator K_Gamma = R_out (I - T_int)^-1 T_in is exact for a fixed interior, and ownership is exclusive while hulls are disjoint and un-intruded. Three defects as specified. (1) It contradicts Architecture.md section 2 in terms ('Object identity must not freeze exposed interreflection or merge editable air transport into K'; 'C ... includes exposed same-asset and same-domain exit/re-entry paths'); the proposal says so openly, so this is an amendment, not a silent change, but it reverses the clause adopted after WL51 (object-scoped Burley moving light across air) and WL53 (double-claimed air paths: rho 4.75). (2) Rays that cross the hull without hitting the interior need a ballistic (delta) pass-through term inside K_Gamma or a split owner; neither is stated, and WL55 shows omitting the ballistic family costs -33.5 %. (3) The operator maps Gamma to Gamma only. Any camera that sees the assembly's interior surfaces needs the interior field at the first visible vertex, which K_Gamma does not provide; tracing the first interior events and reading the rest reintroduces an event-count partition inside Gamma (the ECRO structure) or needs a second 4D-in / surface-out operator. Validity also fails under hull intrusion and near contact, which WL54/55 identify as where errors concentrate.
per_hypothesis.information_and_identifiability: The kernel is 4D-in / 4D-out. For sharp interior chains its bandwidth is that of the sharpest lobe; WL84A's derivation gives ~alpha^-4 samples and WL58 shows 64/256 bins lose 52-80 % at alpha 0.04, so a compact representation exists only where the exit distribution is smooth, which is not the GM1 regime. WL47's mirror cavity is the in-project instance: equal-irradiance inputs differ by 0.98-1.11, a direction-aware map is recovered only with full-boundary supervision, and visible-only supervision gives non-passive hidden outputs (albedo 1.77). A compiler from assembly shape to kernel is the geometry-conditioned generalisation that WL57-80 failed on a simpler domain. A 'generative sampler' for near-mirror chains would have to emulate ray tracing through the interior; the survey's best cross-scene model handles about three specular bounces.
per_hypothesis.economics_vs_matched_explicit_computatio: Nothing is measured. The only relevant number is 2.36-2.42 segments per path on the open WL85 fixture, which caps the saving well below 2x there; a closed high-albedo glossy enclosure is unmeasured for path length, for g and for cold path-tracing cost. Plain frozen-ER path tracing on WL85 is 0.39 s GPU to g. A path-traced interface table and explicit patch-level transport for an enclosure were never built; the physically matched comparator is a precomputed light-field operator on Gamma holding the same state. The saving is not unique to learning (the proposal concedes it); learning would add only compression or cross-assembly generation, both unsupported. Hull-intrusion testing and fallback are added costs in the common contact-rich case.
per_hypothesis.novelty_and_prior_art: Renaming of object-owned precomputed transfer: PRT self-transfer with interreflection baked in (Sloan 2002), radiance transfer fields on shadow fields (Pan 2007), Modular Radiance Transfer interfaces, extended form factors, and the learned variants NeLT, object-centric neural scattering functions and TransGI. All are low-frequency between or inside objects, and the survey states the composition step is where angular frequency is lost. Inside the project it is the object-scoped K that WL51 and WL53 led the contract to exclude.
per_hypothesis.consistency_with_measured_evidence: Supports: rigid invariance of an isolated domain's K (WL53); contact-creating rigid reuse by re-aggregation (WL55, 18/18). Contradicts: double-claim control rho 4.75 (WL53) whenever hull and C overlap; WL54/55 near-contact errors +6 to +44 % at exactly the hull-intrusion regime; WL47 direction-selective cavity needs full directional input and supervision; WL84A alpha^-4 and WL58 angular loss; WL85 short paths; WL57-80 negative geometry-conditioned transfer.
fatal_objections: In the target regime (sharp glossy interior transport) the 4D kernel has no compact representation (space-bandwidth bound, alpha^-4, WL58); in the regime where it is compact it is known low-frequency object-owned PRT. There is no regime in which it is both new and representable.
As specified it cannot render a visible assembly: K_Gamma returns exit rays on the hull, not interior surface radiance, and the pass-through ballistic family has no stated owner.
non_fatal_objections: Requires a human amendment of an explicit contract clause.
Hull intrusion / near contact is the common case in the project's own fixtures and reverts to full physical transport plus a test.
The only measured path-length figure argues against any ceiling above ~2x; the favourable workload is unmeasured.
The compiler over assembly shapes inherits the WL57-80 transfer record.
per_hypothesis.what_would_change_the_verdict: All of: a contract decision admitting air inside an optical domain; a path census on a closed high-albedo glossy assembly showing an interior segment share large enough for a ceiling well above 2x against cold frozen-ER path tracing; an oracle (physically sampled) K_Gamma, with explicit ballistic and interior-readout terms, substituted into the walk and matching REF-ER on sharp receivers at a state size below the alpha^-4 estimate; and evidence that hull intrusion is rare on the intended workload.

per_hypothesis.name: H3 - Learned broad-class resolvent (restricted ECRO; ownership by ER lobe class)
per_hypothesis.physical_correctness_and_ownership: One-shot and exclusive in principle, but the ownership rule does not do what is claimed. The stored class is defined by the last two lobes being broad; chains such as light -> narrow sender -> broad -> broad remain in the stored class, and the learned operator must still generate them from the encoded direct field through an internal narrow-to-broad link, the same flight that delivered 1-18 % in WL86A. So 'the remainder term has nothing sharp left to absorb' is false unless the operator's input is replaced by a physically computed post-sharp-sender field, which is not specified. The 'sender-driven physical estimator' for the excluded classes is bounded (lit sender area x lobe samples) only for the two-event family; for higher-order chains ending narrow -> broad the incident field at the narrow sender is itself multi-bounce, so the estimator is a full light-side or bidirectional pass of unknown cost. The lobe-class threshold is a convention that must be applied identically on both sides (prior-art survey), and ER's lobes narrow toward grazing (sharp share 0.51 at 80 degrees), so a fixed lobe-index class is not a fixed bandwidth class. The learned parameters are scene-family state with no row in Architecture.md section 4; the generator and application are re-run in full on every edit, so nothing is selectively preserved.
per_hypothesis.information_and_identifiability: Container representability holds on the WL86 room (oracle E_H 0.003; 0.0137 hardest region). Operator-family representability is not shown (free-factor fit leaves 49-68 % of the deficit, confounded), and identifiability under the supervision is not shown: ECRO's two terms were trained on their sum only, and H3 keeps a free additive remainder. Term-wise targets were computed in WL86A amendment 1 but never used in training. In the class H3 keeps, the geometry-conditioned state does least measurable work: STALE is 1.0-1.6x ECRO outside region A and E1's panel, and 'in D most of the response is carried by the current source field' (WL86 worklog lines 198 and 241). A learned generator cannot be identified from data in which a stale state nearly ties.
per_hypothesis.economics_vs_matched_explicit_computatio: No comparator the task names was measured. Path-traced table through the same readout: 6.3-24.4 s contended wall at 4,096 spp, ~1.2 s per lighting at 256 spp, no uncontended kernel time, no accuracy ladder. Explicit deterministic patch-level transport on the same patches and 512 rays: never timed; for broad-to-broad classes this is classical radiosity on the same form factors (the generator already builds the dense N x N form-factor matrix as an input), and nearest measured costs are 5.0 / 11.1 ms explicit C update with 0.1-0.6 ms per application (WL52) and a 26-28 ms wall / 0.19-0.20 ms kernel state rebuild (WL86). Plain frozen-ER path tracing: 0.39 s GPU to g on WL85. ECRO's 3-6x edit-to-first-frame and 9x per-frame figures are against a 6-vertex no-roulette megakernel only (5.45x cheaper samples x 1.6-1.7x fewer samples at noise-level quality; protocol verdict NOT TESTED). The owned class is small: two consecutive broad lobes is about a quarter or less on the iid population and well under 1 % on the hard population (reviewer arithmetic from the census), and WL85's broad multi-bounce change is 1.5 % of T0, the size of g (0.017). Offline cost is ~15 min supervision + 22 min training per scene family with no amortisation count; outside the family it is retraining, i.e. the Neural Full Recompute lifecycle. No saving is shown to be unique to learning; published learning-free broad caches run at 1.5-3.5 ms per frame.
per_hypothesis.novelty_and_prior_art: Renaming. It is ECRO v0 with the sharp-sender family moved to a physical pass, which is Jensen 1996's two-tier structure (caustic family routed light-side), the Sillion 1991 / Chen 1991 rough-sharp multi-pass partition, direct-to-indirect transfer generated per pose (the Diolatzis 2022 interpolation pattern), and MRT-style low-rank operators with their documented 'intelligent ambient' compensation. Inside the project it is WL84A Track C (lobe-partitioned graph), which its own advocate withdrew: sharp part retraced, point-sampled field aliases sharp senders onto rough receivers, dense per-edit solve.
per_hypothesis.consistency_with_measured_evidence: Supports: learned table E_H 0.003-0.006 on stationary and broad regions on both edits; contracts pass (flux 0.980-0.998, superposition 2e-7). Contradicts or limits: region-C change slope 0.36-0.63 (ungated); box-patch error 1.6-2.7x worse on unseen geometry while the aggregate gate passed; remainder compensation +0.017 to +0.064 (E2) and +0.039 / +0.041 (E1) with opposite net sign; STALE nearly ties in the broad class; hard-population census 94 % moderate / 4 % broad; WL52 precedent that a learned operator's apparent gain over an under-sampled explicit one was variance, with worse per-port error (0.158 vs 0.112).
fatal_objections: The lobe-class partition leaves sharp links inside the stored chains, so the mechanism that failed in WL86A (a learned flight from a narrow sender, compensated by a visibility-free remainder) is still present; the claimed cure for compensation does not follow from the stated ownership rule.

No saving is attributable to learning: the owned class is the one where a learning-free solve on the same form factors is the natural comparator, where a stale state nearly ties, and where published physical caches already operate; the comparator was never measured, so the hypothesis has no supported economic content.
non_fatal_objections: The physical sharp-sender estimator's cost is unbounded for higher-order chains and can dominate.
Owned share is small on moderate-lobe materials and shrinks toward grazing.
Scene-family parameters: retraining lifecycle, no selective preservation, dense O(N^2) input.
Held-out evidence is one room family, E2 inside the training distribution margin, two seeds.
per_hypothesis.what_would_change_the_verdict: A restated ownership rule that removes interior sharp links from the learned side (or supplies a physically computed post-sharp-sender field as input), plus: an accuracy-vs-uncontended-kernel-time ladder in which the learned generator beats both the same-state learning-free binned solve and a path-traced table on at least one gated broad class beyond seed spread; a class-share census by lobe pair on the target material population showing a non-trivial owned share; a retrained model with term-wise targets showing the remainder no longer compensates; and a broad-class region where the stale control clearly fails.

reviews.is_any_hypothesis_just_a_renaming: Yes, all three. H1 at GM1 is the project's own REF-ER reference level (frozen-ER full path tracing, Architecture.md section 3 item (b)) presented as a hypothesis; the roadmap states a full retracer does not complete GM1; its GM2 extension is the Vicini et al. 2019 learned SSS sampling model and the WL57-80 learned intrinsic K under a new interface description. H2 is object-owned precomputed transfer (PRT self-transfer, radiance transfer fields, MRT interfaces, NeLT / object-centric scattering functions / TransGI) and, inside the project, the object-scoped K that WL51 and WL53 caused the contract to exclude. H3 is ECRO v0's two-term operator with the sharp family routed to a light-side pass, i.e. Jensen 1996 two-tier / multi-pass radiosity plus ray tracing with a per-pose learned direct-to-indirect operator, and it coincides with WL84A's withdrawn lobe-partitioned Track C. None introduces a mechanism absent from the prior-art survey or the project history. The proposal's criteria for 'not another heuristic decomposition' (partition from an exact sum, term-wise targets, oracle first, beat the same-state physical operator, per-family scoring) are evaluation rules, not an architecture.
reviews.strongest_overall_objection: The proposal's only 'defensible' hypothesis is the null result plus the existing baseline, and the argument that elevates it does not hold. (1) H1 contains no learned global object and at GM1 is exactly frozen-ER path tracing: cost ratio 1.0 against the comparator, fidelity on sharp receivers equal to ER's own gap (0.059-0.065 against a 0.06 gate), excluded by the roadmap's GM1 exit clause. (2) Its justification, 'learning succeeded only where no scene geometry enters', rests on a single success (ER: one material family, three re-qualified images, WL83's frozen render rule failed) and misfiles WL57-80, which was an intrinsic-geometry-conditioned K, i.e. H1's own GM2 content. Read correctly, the record is 'every geometry-conditioned learned object failed, intrinsic or global', which predicts failure of the one thing H1 would still learn. (3) The decisive experiment it proposes does not test H1: it compares ECRO with binned physical tables on a 512-ray state that WL86A already found sampling-limited for the sharp family (-20 %, patch RMS 0.50-0.93 with exact sender radiance), so arm X is expected to fail sharp receivers for the same reason; arm Xs is not a same-state control; and the only in-project evidence cited for sender-side sampling (WL46) was receiver-side lobe sampling. (4) H2 and H3 are judged weak by their own author; H2 is unrepresentable where it would be new, and H3 keeps the failed sharp link inside its stored chains. What the evidence supports is the proposal's closing sentence ('the evidence does not yet support selecting any learned global mechanism') and its list of missing same-state comparators. It does not support 'learning belongs in K': that requires a positive result for a geometry-conditioned sampleable nonlocal K, which does not exist, and the framing leaves ECRO's broad-class result (0.003-0.006 at 5.45x cheaper samples) unexplained instead of refuted.

factual_errors_in_proposal.claim: H1 cost model: '[measured] 109 M rays in 0.105 s trace-only, WL52' used as evidence that exhaustive patch-level visibility is cheap at 10^5-10^8 rays.
factual_errors_in_proposal.correction: Not a measurement of that workload. It is a throughput probe of 16.8 M random rays in the bounding box (1.04 G rays/s) scaled to 109.3 M rays. Port ray setup and device-side hit-to-port mapping for the Lego scene were never implemented or timed, and the Lego BVH build alone is 0.82 s. The WL86 ray rate the proposal derives (2.7-3.4 G rays/s) is for a room of a few dozen primitives, so the 'linear in N*R at the measured rate' scaling is optimistic by at least 3x on a real mesh.
factual_errors_in_proposal.source: dossier.md lines 838, 854, 878 (WL52 Stage A); dossier_core.md WL52-56 open confounds

factual_errors_in_proposal.claim: '[measured] A path-traced 256-spp table costs at most about 0.16 s of GPU time' (also used for the 7.5 ns probe-path cost, the 0.61 ms per table spp figure and the 15,000-edit break-even).
factual_errors_in_proposal.correction: 0.157 s is aggregate wall time per field (1,024 x 4 fields in 10.7 min) with 8 concurrent shards, and it includes state rays, source encoding and file writing. Ctx.field records no kernel GPU time. The single-process figures are 1.24 s per lighting (8 concurrent) and about 1.5 s per lighting alone (dev probe, 6 s per geometry for 4 lightings). It is neither a GPU-time measurement nor a bound; the proposal lists the same number as unverified assumption (3) while tagging it [measured] in the text.
factual_errors_in_proposal.source: dossier.md line 1174; experiments/ecro86/pt86.py Ctx.field (no kernel_history); docs/worklogs/86_WORKLOG_ECRO_GLOBAL_RESPONSE.md throughput probes

factual_errors_in_proposal.claim: 'With a 256-spp path-traced table the edit-to-frame advantage over the plain path tracer would be about 2.3x at quality 0.05 and 4.3x at 0.03 instead of 9x.'
factual_errors_in_proposal.correction: The 2.3x / 4.3x figures use E1 only and are set against the per-frame (resident) 9x, not the measured edit-to-first-frame GPU ratio (E1 7.5x at 0.05, 8.2x at 0.03; E2 6.6x at 0.05). With the same arithmetic on E2 the path-traced-table variant gives 1.35x at 0.05 and 3.0x at 0.03, and it is slower than plain path tracing at quality 0.10 on both edits (0.68x E1, 0.37x E2).

factual_errors_in_proposal.claim: H1 operator: '[code] same stratified offsets for every patch, so M is one 64 x R x 3 table per material.'

per_hypothesis.name: H1. Explicit same-state fill of the higher-order table, sender-side routing of sharp senders, no learned global operator
per_hypothesis.physical_correctness_and_ownership: The event-count cut is the same exact partition ECRO uses, one operator owns every flight, and a finite J = 4 sum cannot diverge, so the instability class of WL41-51 does not apply. It respects the K/C contract more literally than ECRO (S_ER C_G Neumann series). Four weaknesses remain. (a) The gather / deposit split is exclusive only as a per-material convention; the stated rule (closure r50 below the outgoing bin width) is fixed at one incidence while the ER lobes sharpen toward grazing (panel r50 0.146 at 45 deg, 0.09 at 80 deg), and what decides whether a receiver-side gather resolves a sender is lobe width times the sender's subtended solid angle, not r50 alone. The sphere (97 % moderate, 32 patches) is not routed to the deposit. (b) Sharp-sender exit radiance of two or more events is read through 64 bins at every flight j >= 2; that is a fixed-bandwidth blur applied where nothing validates it. (c) The sender-side deposit is source-dependent light tracing outside the stored state, so variant 3 is no longer a 'same-state' control of ECRO, and its Monte Carlo noise is frozen into the table and shows up as spatially correlated error under a mirror read, so the 'noise-free higher-order term' property does not carry over automatically. (d) The discrete passivity bound is an inference; on sphere patches the per-material M table is wrong (see factual errors).
per_hypothesis.information_and_identifiability: Nothing is learned, so identifiability is moot. Information is the issue. WL86A amendment 2 already measured the two purely same-state variants on the failing family: exact once-scattered panel radiance through the deployed 512 rays is -20.4 % / -19.9 % with patch RMS 0.50 / 0.93 (RAY), and bin-averaged sender radiance is -15.8 % / -26.0 % with patch RMS 0.38 / 0.47 (BIN). So variants 1 and 2 do not carry the sharp-sender relation at patch level; only the deposit can, and the project has no measurement of it (prior art only: Jensen 1996, Xu et al. 2014 at one bounce, abstract level). The ray template is one fixed realisation shared by all patches, so its quadrature error is coherent across patches and becomes a bias under a near-mirror read. Patch-constant 25 cm senders next to box / floor contact lose sub-patch structure (WL52, WL54), which the path-trace-supervised ECRO table does not obviously share.
per_hypothesis.economics_vs_matched_explicit_computatio: H1 is the explicit patch-level computation, so no saving is unique to learning by construction. What is unverified is that it saves anything. Its fill cost ('order of a millisecond') is an operation count, never timed; in this harness 0.19 ms of state-ray kernel time costs 26-28 ms wall. Against a path-traced table: 256 spp is about 0.157 s aggregate contended wall with entry noise about 0.10; 4,096 spp is 6-24 s contended wall; no accuracy-versus-cost curve exists for either. Against plain path tracing with frozen ER: the whole advantage is the two-tier estimator's 5.45x per sample times 1.6-1.75x fewer samples, measured only against a six-vertex kernel without Russian roulette at noise-level quality; g was reached by neither arm; in E2 region C the path tracer reaches 0.040 at 4,096 spp while any table must first achieve patch-level accuracy. WL85's cold path tracer reaches g in 0.39 s GPU, which triggers WL84A's own 'about a second or less, no reuse scheme has room' clause. Scaling goes the wrong way: stored state grows with N*R (about 55 M entries and more than 10^8 rays at Lego scale, BVH 0.82 s), receiver rays as r50^-2, the deposit as lights x sharp patches x samples. Published physical caches (path space filtering 1.5 ms, DDGI, SHaRC, Lumen) are the comparators a reviewer would ask for and are unmeasured.
per_hypothesis.novelty_and_prior_art: A renaming, and the proposer says so. View-independent directional finite-element solve (Immel 1986; Sillion 1991) plus a traced final stage (Wallace 1987; Sillion and Puech 1989) plus light-side handling of light -> specular -> diffuse (Heckbert 1990; Jensen 1996). In project terms it is the WL86 Stage 1 oracle with a deterministic fill, the WL52 explicit C0, and WL84A Track C, which its own advocate withdrew for reasons that still apply (sharp part retraced, alpha^-4 tabulation). WL80B classed the analogous learning-free operator C1 as 'physical baseline only, not a method'.
per_hypothesis.consistency_with_measured_evidence: Supports: the patch x 64-bin container is at reference noise through the same readout (E_H 0.0025-0.0137); explicit coupling beat learned coupling 8-60x on update cost (WL52); state rays cost 0.19-0.24 ms kernel; the ENC test shows a linear geometry-determined operator on the encoding exists for three point-light cases. Contradicts or weakens: RAY -20 % and BIN -16 % / -26 % with patch RMS 0.38-0.93 for the failing family (two of the three variants); the learned operator already sits at 0.003-0.006 on stationary and broad regions at 11.3 ms wall from the same 512 rays, a measured point no explicit computation has matched; WL58 puts a 64 / 256-bin interface at 9.9-17.7 % loss for alpha 0.25 while the sphere closure (r50 0.36, alpha about 0.18) is sharper; near-contact patch-averaged transfer p99 2.30 against 0.27 (WL52); the oracle table itself is not at noise for the sphere object (0.0105 vs 0.0059) or class E on E1.
fatal_objections: As an answer to the study question it is not a learned global transport hypothesis: it contains no learned global component, and under the current documents a learning-free global solve around frozen ER is admissible at most as a baseline (open human decision; WL80B precedent). Fatal for candidacy as an architecture, not for use as a comparator.
No novelty: it is classical two-pass radiosity plus ray tracing plus a caustic-style light pass.
non_fatal_objections: Its cost and accuracy are operation counts and inferences; the recurrence was never run.

Two of its three variants are already measured to miss the sharp-sender family at patch level (WL86A amendment 2, post hoc, marginal rule); the third relies on a source-dependent pass with no project evidence.
Variant 3 is not a same-state control: it adds lights x sharp patches x samples of light-traced work and Monte Carlo noise in the table.
The sharp / moderate class rule is a convention at one incidence and ignores sender extent; the sphere and grazing incidence are not covered.
Binned sharp-sender radiance at flights j >= 2 is an unvalidated blur of unknown share.
The two-tier estimator's room is measured only against a no-roulette path tracer at noise-level quality; with roulette, a denoiser or a larger scene the factor may approach one.
Per-material M tables are wrong on the curved sphere patches.
per_hypothesis.what_would_change_the_verdict: Upward (as a null that removes the case for a learned fill on this workload): an explicit recurrence on the frozen WL86 state, through the identical readout, that matches the learned table's 0.003-0.006 on stationary and broad regions and region A, and brings E2 region C under 0.06 with independent ray seeds, at uncontended kernel time below the learned operator's, with the gain surviving a Russian-roulette path tracer at matched quality. Downward to refuted as a null: a level bias of a few per cent on broad or near-contact regions above the learned operator's error, or region C still failing with the deposit, or a fill that costs more than the path-traced re-render it replaces.

per_hypothesis.name: H2. Learned prolongation (sub-patch and sub-bin closure) inside the explicit recurrence
per_hypothesis.physical_correctness_and_ownership: One operator, a multiplicative learned factor and a residual target, so no path family is double counted and it is not ECRO's two additive terms. Three problems. (a) Pi P = I preserves the bin-mean radiance, not the cosine- and area-weighted flux that the receiver gather integrates, so 'cannot create energy' holds only if the constraint is stated in flux; J is finite, so this is a bias issue, not divergence. (b) One prolongation is applied at every flight, although the sub-patch profile of two-event radiance (shadow-edged) and of four-event radiance (smooth) differ; the term is used where its supervision does not define it. (c) The teacher decides what the term means: a refined explicit solve inherits H1's unverified errors (bin blur at sharp senders, fixed ray template), while a path-traced teacher makes the 'prolongation' absorb every discretisation error of H1 at once, which is a residual catch-all of the kind FNTO's contract line 74 forbids. In contract terms it is a learned correction of the discretised coupling C, the class WL52 closed as NOT SUPPORTED.
per_hypothesis.information_and_identifiability: The stated inputs (a pair-local geometry descriptor and the cell's own coarse value) cannot determine the stated output for flights j >= 2. The fine profile inside a sender patch depends on what illuminates it: neighbouring patches' radiance, the occluder's position relative to the light, the field's own gradients. WL54 found the near-contact loss is convex sub-port source structure set at the first interreflection, i.e. produced by the adjacent surface's radiance, which is source-dependent. Equal descriptors with different fine profiles are expected by construction (a floor patch beside a lit versus an unlit box face). Sub-bin structure of sharp lobes is excluded by the proposer on information grounds, so the sharp-sender relation that WL86A identifies is not carried at all. The single term is identifiable from its residual, but only relative to a teacher that has not been validated.
per_hypothesis.economics_vs_matched_explicit_computatio: No saving is unique to learning, and the proposer concedes it. The physically matched alternative is explicit adaptive refinement, measured at 1.00-1.04x GPU work at an equal ray budget (CASP, WL54), on a solve the proposal itself prices at about a millisecond. The learned part needs a descriptor and a network evaluation per (patch, ray) pair, 650,240 evaluations per geometry, against 0.19-0.24 ms of kernel time to trace all of those rays; the only measured learned-versus-explicit coupling comparison went 8-60x against learning (WL52: 44 / 672 ms versus 5.0 / 11.1 ms). Against a path-traced table and against plain path tracing it inherits H1's unverified position and adds training cost and a generalisation risk. The upper bound on the prize is H1's bias on broad and near-contact transport, which is unmeasured, and the oracle container already sits at 0.0033-0.0075 in region A.
per_hypothesis.novelty_and_prior_art: Explicit forms are hierarchical and wavelet radiosity, higher-order elements, discontinuity meshing and three-point transport; a learned interpolation inside a coarse discretisation is the learned sub-grid closure / data-driven discretisation idea. In the project it is CASP (WL54) and CAK (WL55) with the rule learned, and DASQ (WL49 / WL50) moved from the K side to the C side. WL80A's objection to candidate C2 (a learned compression that depends on the explicit operator as teacher) applies unchanged.
per_hypothesis.consistency_with_measured_evidence: For: near-contact loss has a regular local form on Lambert fixtures (exponential decay, 94 % from pairs closer than 1 cm, WL54). Against: the learned coupling given patch-level inputs was no better than the ray-traced transfer on the same patches (p99 2.32 versus 2.30, WL52); explicit refinement reached 35 / 36 groups at 1.00-1.04x GPU work (WL54; 34 / 36 against the 0.5 mm references per the WL55 replay); DASQ's gain came from coverage, and its matched learned A/B was formally INCONCLUSIVE (WL49); learned geometry-conditioned maps transferred only within 5-18 mm of supervised sources and drifted after 2k-6k steps (WL71-78, different operator and fixture); the WL86 failure is the sharp-sender family (level error of a few Lambert patches fed by the panel), which H2 excludes.
fatal_objections: No saving unique to learning at any measured scale: explicit refinement costs 1.00-1.04x of a millisecond-scale solve, and the one measured learned-versus-explicit coupling comparison is 8-60x against learning. The economic prize is at most zero on current evidence.

It does not address the failure the study is about: sharp senders are excluded by its own information argument, and no broad or near-contact deficit of the explicit or oracle fill has been shown on the GM1 fixture.
non_fatal_objections: Pair-local descriptors cannot determine sub-patch sender radiance at flights j >= 2; the equal-descriptor test is likely to fail.
Mean preservation is stated in radiance, not flux.
The meaning of the learned term depends on an unvalidated teacher; with a path-traced teacher it becomes a catch-all residual.
Its existence is conditional on an H1 measurement that has not been made.
per_hypothesis.what_would_change_the_verdict: All three together: (1) a measured H1 bias on broad or near-contact transport above the frozen gates and above the learned ECRO table's error; (2) explicit adaptive refinement shown unable to remove that bias below about 2x kernel cost on the same fixture, with no analytic profile fitting; (3) an equal-descriptor test showing the fine profile is a function of the local descriptor, and a learned evaluation whose kernel time is below the refinement it replaces. None of these exists; (2) is contradicted by WL54 on the fixtures measured.

per_hypothesis.name: H3. Learned generator of the intrinsic nonlocal K for domains whose shape changes, with explicit coupling and explicit solve
per_hypothesis.physical_correctness_and_ownership: It is the contract's K, so segment ownership is correct, the target can be path-history independent (Cycles volume, WL53), and a column-substochastic construction gives passivity on every tested field (max column sum <= 0.9997). The composition, however, was never run: coupling with C was skipped at eligibility in WL57, WL59 and WL64, and the project's own record (WL50, WL51) is that first-exit fidelity does not predict coupled behaviour. Near contact the K side must resolve below the port (WL55: +10 to +22 % outgoing flux at 1 cm), which no learned K has attempted, and the computed ballistic term has a resolved error of its own (9.3 % of pair-7 contrast). More basically, it changes the question: ER materials have no nonlocal K, the 64 / 256-bin angular interface cannot carry a sharp GGX lobe (WL58: 52-80 % loss at alpha 0.04), and nothing in it is global transport between surfaces.
per_hypothesis.information_and_identifiability: Whether a source-independent, geometry-conditioned member of the family exists below the edit signal is undecided (WL71 unresolved 1): the oracle T is a per-source latent. The supervision cannot identify the deformation response at affordable cost: deformed-minus-rest stays below SNR 3 in 492 of 576 cells at 128-512 M photons (WL65). Runs with equal fit disagree on held-out boundary sources (0.668 versus 0.860, WL78), so the stated constraints do not identify the map. Where the learned scattered term was isolated its directional contrast error was 0.91-1.12 of its own signal (WL63); the total-response scores are carried by the computed ballistic term.
per_hypothesis.economics_vs_matched_explicit_computatio: The claim that this is the one place where learning is the unique source of a saving rests on the wrong comparator. The 175-380 s Monte Carlo oracle is not the matched explicit computation: a path-traced re-render through the medium meets the 3 % contract in 4.67 s (W1) and 1.2 s (C1), and learning-free deterministic operators (three-scalar diffusion profile, collision-probability C1) have structural transfer and unmeasured cost. The 2.5 mm oracle composition itself fails the contract (9 / 12, blue +3.6 to +10.3 %), so neither the '175 s physical K' nor the '0.685 s update' is quality matched against the path tracer. The '0.7 s learned K' figure splices the oracle pipeline's resident state update with W+UV generation; no learned K has been timed in a coupled pipeline, and every learned K is 6-7 % off where reusing the stale exact operator is 0.5-1.2 % off, so regenerating is both costlier and less accurate than not updating. The hypothetical factor against path tracing is 1.7-6.7x at unmatched quality.
per_hypothesis.novelty_and_prior_art: A renaming of an earlier project mechanism, as the proposer states: the FNTO contract K in its WL57-80 form (computed ballistic term plus one learned collided term, global angular bases, geometry-conditioned spatial factor). External precedents are DeepPRT (geometry in, linear low-frequency transfer out), the shape-adaptive SSS model of Vicini et al. 2019 and Deep Scattering. WL77A, WL80A and WL80B found no reviewed candidate defensible as a learned K on this fixture.
per_hypothesis.consistency_with_measured_evidence: For: K construction is the one large measured physical cost (175-380 s, 1.7-2.0 GB per slab, 92.9 % of a selective update); rigid reuse holds within noise; a dent's change is local and low rank (rank90 8-18, with the red locality figure vacuous). Against: learned 6-7 % versus stale exact 0.5-1.2 % (WL57 / WL59); new-source error 0.56-0.94 against fit 0.04-0.13 (WL68); far-boundary contrast 0.67-0.95 against oracles 0.13-0.27 (WL73-78); no learned map met the signed-deformation gate in any batch; late-training drift by a factor of about five (WL71A); the exact oracle selective update took 189 s and failed the contract that a 4-spp path trace met in 4.67 s (WL67).
fatal_objections: Out of scope for the question: it carries no sharp glossy interreflection and no global transport with ER, and its angular interface is measured unable to hold a sharp lobe (WL58).
Measured fidelity is against it across more than twenty batches: every learned K is 5-6x worse than not updating, and none met the directional or deformation gates.
Its economic case is not quality matched: path tracing meets the contract in 1.2-4.7 s while the exact oracle composition it would approximate fails it.
non_fatal_objections: Learning-free operators for homogeneous media were never costed, so uniqueness of the saving to learning is unproven even in its own regime.
Never composed with C; composed stability and accuracy are unknown.
Deformation supervision is precision-bound, so the target is expensive to obtain at all.
All evidence is one homogeneous index-matched slab fixture.
per_hypothesis.what_would_change_the_verdict: A workload with a nonlocal medium in scope where a contract-quality path trace through the medium costs at least an order of magnitude more than the shared state update; an oracle fit showing a source-independent geometry-conditioned family member below the roughly 1 % edit signal at independent sources; a generated K that beats the stale exact operator on an unseen dent with independently qualified labels, is composed with C and passes the contract; and a measured cost for a learning-free operator on the same fixture that the learned generator beats.

reviews.is_any_hypothesis_just_a_renaming: Yes, all three in different degrees, and the proposer concedes two. H1 is classical two-pass rendering under a new label: a view-independent patch x direction finite-element solve (Immel 1986, Sillion 1991) with a traced final stage (Wallace 1987) and a light-side pass for light -> sharp sender -> receiver (Heckbert 1990, Jensen 1996); inside the project it is the WL86 Stage 1 oracle with a deterministic fill, the WL52 explicit C0, and WL84A Track C, which was withdrawn. H3 is the FNTO contract K in its WL57-80 form (computed ballistic term plus one learned collided term), not a new proposal. H2 is not ECRO's two terms or the four K terms renamed, but it is CASP / CAK / DASQ with the refinement rule learned, i.e. a learned correction of the discretised coupling, the class WL52 already closed. None of the three is a new learned global transport mechanism.
reviews.strongest_overall_objection:
The proposal's central claim is that ECRO's saving belongs to the two-tier estimator and that an explicit fill on the same state would match the learned table at about a millisecond, so learning has no economic role. Both halves of that are unmeasured, and the measurements that do exist cut against the second half.

- **The explicit same-state fill already has a measured result on the failing family, and it fails.** WL86A amendment 2 read exact once-scattered panel radiance through the deployed 512 rays (-20 %, patch RMS 0.50-0.93) and bin-averaged sender radiance (-16 % / -26 %). Those are H1's first two variants. The proposed remedy, a sender-side deposit, is source-dependent light tracing outside the stored state, with no project measurement and with Monte Carlo noise frozen into the table.
- **On broad transport the learned operator holds a measured point nothing explicit has matched.** It reaches 0.003-0.006 on stationary and broad regions from 512 rays per patch at 11.3 ms wall. Whether a bin-to-bin recurrence at 64 bins does the same is unknown, and WL58 and the near-contact results give reasons to doubt it.
- **The cost side is an operation count.** The millisecond solve was never timed, the path-traced-table cost is contended wall time mislabelled as GPU time, and the 2.3x / 4.3x figure is E1 only (E2 gives 1.35x / 3.0x and a loss at quality 0.10).
- **The frame above all of it is thin.** The estimator's 5.45x was measured only against a six-vertex path tracer without Russian roulette at noise-level quality. WL85's cold path tracer reaches the ER-gap level in 0.39 s GPU, so the two-tier structure itself may have little room.

The result is that the lens produces no defensible learned hypothesis (H1 has no learned part, H2 has no prize, H3 is refuted by the record) and its null is itself unverified. What the evidence supports is narrower than the proposal's conclusion: the same-state explicit and path-traced comparators are missing, so a learned global operator is neither shown necessary nor shown unnecessary.

factual_errors_in_proposal.claim: ECRO's geometry state is '512 cosine-stratified rays per patch'; the panel count is derived as '~15-25 cosine rays'.

factual_errors_in_proposal.claim: Overall assessment: the learned sharp flight through a receiver-side ray relation is 'CONTRADICTED. ... The measured state-relation result, the counting argument ... agree.'
factual_errors_in_proposal.correction: The state-relation result is post hoc, uses one fixed ray realisation with no uncertainty on the RAY estimate, and its SAMPLING-LIMITED label holds through a different clause in each of the two cases (E2 T1: -20.4 % passes the > 20 % clause by 0.4 points with patch RMS 0.496; E2 T0: -19.9 % fails that clause and passes on RMS 0.926). per_hypothesis.name: H1. Bandwidth-matched class operator (learned response on broad-only path runs; sharp-lobe events carried as sampled flights)
per_hypothesis.physical_correctness_and_ownership:
The algebra is right: with S = S_B + S_S, beta = S_B(e~ + C~_G beta) follows exactly, and for a fixed lobe assignment each class of the frozen ER closure is reciprocal, non-negative and passive (checked in closure82.py). Four ownership problems remain.

- **Learned class is defined two ways.** The formula puts every broad -> sharp chain -> broad link inside the learned tail through C~_G. The ownership text says sharp events are traced and nothing sharp is in the learned target. The first reading puts sharp-mediated transfer back into a learned term; the second requires re-applying the operator after each sharp event, which ends the 'applied once, no recursion, no passivity question' property. Until one is chosen, the class cannot be tallied.
- **Incidence-dependent threshold breaks the exactness claim.** A class assigned from the lobe width at the actual incidence makes S_B non-reciprocal, and the boundary is only 'the same on both sides' when both directions are known at the vertex.
- **m is never fixed.** The event boundary between the traced first broad events and the learned tail is left open, and so is the form of the learned operator, so 'no intermediate read without supervision' cannot be checked.
- **The K/C contract is changed, not kept.** C~_G contains material scattering (sharp lobes) and is a Monte Carlo lobe convolution, not an exact geometric relabelling; K becomes a lobe subset. Ownership by path segment is replaced by ownership by lobe class. Architecture section 8 asks for such a conflict to be reported; the proposal calls it a re-reading.

Stability is not at issue for a one-shot tail, but nothing bounds its gain: the frozen ECRO operator overshoots by 7-11 % on a source class it was not trained on.
per_hypothesis.information_and_identifiability:
The learned term's target is identifiable in principle, and class tagging can give it its own supervision. Three things the proposal relies on are not shown.

- **Sufficiency of the binned input for broad patches.** The beam-pair test had truth noise 0.40-0.80 and no power. The cone source LSPOT gives stationary E_H 0.026 / 0.035 against 0.004-0.006 for point lights. The operator was trained on single point lights only, which is the 'reproduces only what its input prior spans' limit of Modular Radiance Transfer.
- **Carrying broad -> sharp -> broad links.** If these stay in the tail, they pass through the 13-17 state rays per patch that hit the panel, each continued by one lobe sample. Variance is lower than for a point source, but the far field after one broad event still has shadow edges and a caustic footprint of 0.15-0.3 m against 0.25 m patches.
- **The sharp-sender relation is carried by physics, not learning.** The light -> panel -> patch family goes to a source-side deposit. The deposit's accuracy (<= 10 % per patch from ~10^4 rays) is arithmetic only, and it resolves the caustic at patch scale.

Compensation between learned terms is removed only if the operator is a single term. The proposal does not say whether ECRO's flight-plus-global form, which is the form with measured results, is kept.
per_hypothesis.economics_vs_matched_explicit_computatio:
No saving is shown to be unique to learning, and the proposal says so itself. The measured anchors are:

| Item | Cost | Quality |
|---|---|---|
| Learned operator (ECRO v0) | 11.3-11.8 ms wall; whole edit 76-78 ms | entry error 0.043-0.056 incl. oracle noise; rendered broad E_H 0.003-0.006 |
| Path-traced table, 256 spp | 0.157 s GPU wall per lighting in aggregate (1.24 s per process, 8 concurrent) | entry noise about 0.10; rendered error never measured |
| Path-traced table, 4,096 spp | 6.3-7.9 s warm, contended | rendered E_H 0.0025-0.0137 |
| Explicit patch x bin solve, same rays | not measured | not measured |
| Path tracer, frozen ER, no roulette | 1.806 ms per spp; edit 35-36 ms | level g not reached by either arm |
| ECRO readout | 0.331 ms per spp (5.45x) | bias floor 0.073 in E2 region C |

- **Against the path-traced table:** the learned fill is 13-100x cheaper at lower entry error for in-distribution point lights. This is the one matched comparison with numbers, and it favours learning for the broad tail, contrary to the proposal's blanket 'cache effect' reading.
- **Against the explicit solve:** nothing is measured. The 'under a millisecond' sweep is an untimed estimate, and its accuracy with 8 rays per incident bin and patch-constant senders is unknown.
- **Against plain path tracing:** H1 lengthens the camera prefix wherever a sharp lobe is met (at least three vertices in region C against ECRO's two) and adds deposit and continuation rays, so the 5.45x per-sample figure is an upper bound that holds only on broad-dominated views. With mostly sharp lobes the cost tends to that of the path tracer plus overhead. Cold frozen-ER path tracing reached the ER-gap level in 0.39 s GPU on the WL85 fixture.
- **Edit response:** outside region A and E1's panel, a stale table is within 0.87-1.6x of the updated learned table, so the geometry-conditioned broad response has almost no measured economic or fidelity role yet.
per_hypothesis.novelty_and_prior_art:
A recombination, not a new mechanism.

- The lobe partition with sharp events as ray chains and broad events through a compiled bin matrix is WL84A Track C (LPTG), withdrawn by its own advocate because the sharp part is retraced, the incident field aliases sharp senders, and the per-edit solve is dense.
- Extended links through specular chains are extended form factors (Wallace 1987; Sillion and Puech 1989).
- The source-side deposit is Jensen's caustic map (1996) and the particle pass of Granier and Drettakis (2001).
- 'Trace through specular vertices, query at the first rough one' is Neural Radiosity (2021) and every guarded cache read (NRC, SHaRC, Lumen roughness bands).
- 'Path-trace low orders, predict the smooth remainder from geometry' is Deep Scattering (2017).
- A source-independent learned broad operator reused across re-arrangement is Modular Radiance Transfer (2011) and direct-to-indirect transfer (2006).

The learned term itself is ECRO v0's broad behaviour with the failing family moved to physics. The proposal concedes most of this.
per_hypothesis.consistency_with_measured_evidence:
**Supports**
- A learned, geometry-conditioned one-shot table reaches 0.003-0.006 on stationary and broad regions of both edits, two seeds.
- The oracle table through the same readout is at noise on the panel (0.0115-0.0121).
- The WL86 room's higher-order share is 0.23-0.24 of stationary radiance, so a tail has something to own there.

**Contradicts or limits**
- WL85 census: on the hard material population a median 94 % of albedo is in lobes of r50 0.15-0.45 rad and 4 % is broad. The WL86 panel is 43 % sharp / 56 % moderate with 0.2 % Lambert, and the sphere 97 % moderate. Under any bin-tied threshold both are traced, and the learned class is a near-diffuse tail.
- Broad generalisation is weaker than the gate suggests: unseen box patches are 1.6-2.7x worse, broad patches with panel form factor >= 0.03 are 1.3-2.5x worse, and the region D slope is 0.78-0.95.
- LSPOT: 5-8x the point-light error on mostly broad pixels.
- The premise that the sharp flight must leave the learned side rests on a post hoc, single-realisation, marginal test; the bulk of the missing flight (1-18 % delivered against 80-84 % through exact rays) is unattributed.
fatal_objections: As written, the learned term's path class is not defined: the operator formula includes broad -> sharp chain -> broad links in the learned tail while the ownership text and the compensation argument exclude every sharp event from it. Each reading gives up one advertised property (nothing sharp in a learned target, or a single non-recursive application). The hypothesis cannot be tallied or tested until this is re-specified; it is repairable, so this is fatal to the text, not to the idea.
non_fatal_objections: The learned component has no demonstrated role: the decisive comparator (explicit patch x bin solve through the same rays) is unmeasured, and the proposal's own argument predicts it wins. This becomes fatal if that solve meets the broad gates at or below 11-12 ms.

On sharp-dominated materials the learned class is nearly empty (4 % broad on the WL85 hard population), so the learned part does not address sharp glossy interreflection at all; requirement (1) is met only by physical tracing, and cost tends to path tracing.
Incidence-dependent class assignment makes S_B non-reciprocal; the 'exact for ER' claim holds only for a fixed per-lobe assignment.
The K/C contract is silently re-read (scattering inside C~_G, ownership by lobe class); no contract conflict is declared.
Input sufficiency on broad patches is unverified and the available evidence (LSPOT, beam responses) points against source generality of a point-light-trained operator.
The deposit is source-dependent state rebuilt per light and per edit; its accuracy and its cost for area lights, many lights and sharp-to-sharp chains are unmeasured.
Near-contact projection (0.25 m patches, boxes on the floor) limits the tail's input and output as in WL52 / WL54; H1 has no answer to it.
m, the operator form, and whether ECRO's unsupervised sender-radiance intermediate survives are unspecified.
Edit response of the broad tail is barely exercised on the measured workload (stale table within 0.87-1.6x outside region A).
per_hypothesis.what_would_change_the_verdict:
Toward 'survives':
- A single consistent class definition whose class-tagged tallies sum to the reference and pass a class-swap control.
- The explicit patch x bin solve through the WL86 state rays measured above the broad-region gates, or clearly dearer than the learned fill at matched table error, on uncontended kernel time.
- Class shares on a workload that qualifies as sharp glossy interreflection showing the broad-run tail owns a material part of the radiance and of the T1 - T0 change in sharp-read regions.
- Equal-encoding variance of the tail target below the gate for cone and beam sources, measured with enough samples to have power.
- A ladder at the g-anchored level against path tracing with Russian roulette and a low-spp path-traced table.

Toward 'refuted':
- The explicit solve meets the gates at or below the learned cost.
- The broad-run tail is a few per cent of the reading on every qualifying workload.
- At least 8 ray-set realisations show the -20 % state-relation deficit is noise, which removes the stated reason for the partition.

per_hypothesis.name: H2. No learned global mechanism (physically computed, class-partitioned element transport; learning confined to local closures, optionally a footprint-prefiltered compile of ER)
per_hypothesis.physical_correctness_and_ownership:
As a statement about evidence ('nothing measured supports selecting a learned global mechanism') I could not refute it. As an architecture it has these problems.

- **Ownership** is exclusive only under the same fixed lobe assignment as H1, and has the same incidence-dependence issue.
- **Passivity** of the projected operator does not follow automatically from the closure: it needs conservative bin-to-bin blocks and closed ray weights. WL54 had to build this explicitly, and WL53's spectral-radius estimator was invalid on refined operators.
- **Projection error is known and large for this kind of solve.** WL52's ray-traced patch transfer had near-contact p99 2.30; WL54's coarse exact-transfer operator reproduced +6 to +44 % at contact; WL58 showed a 64 / 256-bin interface loses 10-18 % at alpha 0.25 and 52-80 % at 0.04.
- **Moderate lobes** are either traced or need directional refinement growing as 1/r50^2, so for the hard population the 'element transport' is path tracing with a small diffuse radiosity attached.
- **The optional prefiltered kernel** replaces sharp transport by transport blurred at footprint width, a bias that does not vanish with samples (the proposal says this).
- **Contract:** the same re-reading of K and C as H1, and under the central documents a learning-free global solve may be a baseline only; a result from it cannot be reported as selective recompute of learned transport.
per_hypothesis.information_and_identifiability:
With nothing learned globally there is no identifiability question, and no term can absorb another. The information questions move to the discretisation and are unanswered.

- 8 rays per incident bin and patch-constant sender radiance are the same relation that read exact panel radiance 16-26 % low with patch RMS 0.38-0.93.
- The sharp-sender relation is carried by the deposit, which is unmeasured.
- The central sentence, that the global part 'contains no quantity that a network knows better than the rays that define it', is not established. A network trained on continuous path-traced targets can hold an expectation that a finite ray set only estimates. The measured table errors (learned 0.043-0.056 including oracle noise at 11-12 ms; path-traced table about 0.10 at 256 spp and 0.157-1.24 s) are a counter-indication against one physical comparator. WL52's image-PSNR result (+1.76 dB for the learned coupling over the 128-gather explicit one) is a second, weaker one.
- The optional learned prefilter has an identifiable local target but no evidence of need.
per_hypothesis.economics_vs_matched_explicit_computatio:
There is no learning-specific saving by construction, so H2 must win as physics, and nothing measured says it does.

- **Explicit deterministic patch-level solve:** accuracy and time never measured on any ER workload; the sub-millisecond figure is an estimate.
- **Path-traced table through the same readout:** 0.157 s GPU wall per lighting at 256 spp (aggregate), 6.3-7.9 s warm at 4,096 spp, contended; no rendered-accuracy-against-spp curve exists.
- **Plain path tracing with frozen ER:** 1.806 ms per spp at 512^2 without roulette; cold tracing reaches the ER-gap level in 0.39 s GPU on the WL85 fixture with a 2.5 ms edit.
- **Project record for physical arms:** none has beaten quality-matched path-traced re-render on the small fixtures (WL67: 4.67 s against 189.8 s; WL69: 2.4 s against 24 s; WL70: 2.09 against 2.40 s, a tie by one timing definition).
- **Published physical caches** already deliver broad transport at 1.5-3.5 ms per frame, with lag after edits.

H2's cost converges to the path tracer's when sharp chains dominate, which the proposal states.
per_hypothesis.novelty_and_prior_art: None, and it is a renaming of an earlier project design. The mechanism is WL84A Track C (LPTG) with a light-side caustic pass added, which in turn is directional finite-element radiance with two-pass specular handling (Immel 1986; Sillion 1991; Wallace 1987; Jensen 1996; Granier and Drettakis 2001). As a position it repeats WL80B ('physical baseline only') and WL84A (all three learning-free tracks withdrawn). The optional prefiltered lobe corresponds to cone-prefiltered radiosity (Neural Cone Radiosity 2025, abstract level), virtual spherical lights (2009) and closed-form spherical-Gaussian integration (Xu et al. 2014). WL80D found a compiled analytic closure has no evaluation-cost advantage over a cheap analytic BSDF, so a learned prefilter has no measured motivation.
per_hypothesis.consistency_with_measured_evidence:
**Supports the negative thesis**
- ECRO v0: NOT SUPPORTED under frozen gates; economics NOT TESTED.
- WL52: learned coupling 8-60x slower than explicit, failed contact fidelity.
- WL57-80: no learned K met its contract.
- WL86: state rebuild is 0.19-0.20 ms of kernel time, so selectivity has nothing to amortise.

**Against the positive claims**
- A learned global table has in fact reached 0.003-0.006 on broad regions on unseen poses, which no explicit patch-level solve in the project has been shown to do on an ER room.
- The known explicit-solve errors (WL52 patch transfer, WL54 contact, WL58 bins) are of the size of the 0.03-0.06 gates or larger.
- WL85 census: on the hard population the element part owns about 4 % of albedo.
- The physical quality floor of even exact oracles is unresolved (WL56: 9/12, blue +3.6 to +10.3 %).
non_fatal_objections: Its affirmative content (an explicit class-partitioned solve reaches the gates; learning has no possible global role) rests entirely on a comparator that was never run; the one matched comparison that has numbers (path-traced table against learned fill) goes against it.
Known projection errors of coarse explicit transport (contact, patch-constant senders, 64-bin moderate lobes) are at or above gate size; H2 offers refinement, whose cost is unmeasured.
On sharp-dominated materials it is the path-tracing comparator with a small radiosity attached, so it cannot deliver the economics requirement there.
Admissibility is an open human decision; under current documents it may only be a baseline.
It is WL84A's withdrawn LPTG under another name; the reasons for that withdrawal (sharp part retraced, dense per-edit solve) are not answered, only the aliasing reason is addressed by the deposit.
The optional learned prefilter is unmotivated by any measurement and biased by design.
It answers the study question by declining it; that is a valid outcome, but it supplies no learned-architecture hypothesis and no test that distinguishes one.

per_hypothesis.name: H3. Learned table as conditional-mean control variate with a physically sampled residual
per_hypothesis.physical_correctness_and_ownership: Correct and unbiased for any table; ownership stops mattering for bias, and nothing is applied where supervision does not define it. It is an estimator wrapped around ECRO, not a transport architecture: it leaves the K/C question, the sharp-sender relation and the edit response exactly where ECRO left them. A wrong table adds a term of order (1/p - 1) x E[(table - conditional mean)^2] to the variance, which the proposal's model omits; on sharp receivers (table 7-10 % low) this is not negligible.
per_hypothesis.information_and_identifiability: It removes the identifiability requirement by construction; the residual carries whatever the interface cannot. Nothing is learned beyond ECRO v0, so it distinguishes no hypothesis from a heuristic decomposition. Its only informational content is the observation that ECRO's per-frame advantage is conditional on reading the table uncorrected.
per_hypothesis.economics_vs_matched_explicit_computatio:
I re-derived the arithmetic and it is correct under its assumptions: a = 0.331 ms, b = 1.475 ms, variance c + d/p with c about 0.59 and d about 0.41 (from the 1.61-1.73x sample reduction), optimum p about 0.40, cost x variance about 1.49 against 1.806, a gain of about 1.2x.

That is before three things that make it worse.
- **Edit path:** ECRO's edit costs 76-78 ms wall against 35-36 ms for the path tracer, so with about 0.32 ms saved per sample the scheme is slower edit-to-frame below roughly 130 spp at 512^2 (my arithmetic; it mixes wall for the edit with kernel time per sample).
- **Comparator:** the path tracer had no Russian roulette; an optimised one may erase 1.2x.
- **Attribution:** in this harness Python tracing is 70-95 % of wall, so a 1.2x kernel difference is not attributable.

d is taken from a ladder at noise-level quality that includes the learned table's bias. Any table, learned or path-traced, gives the same result, so nothing is unique to learning.
per_hypothesis.novelty_and_prior_art: A renaming of published estimators: neural control variates (2020) and the two-level Monte Carlo neural incident radiance cache (2025). Those gain by querying the cache many times per vertex without rays; a patch x bin table read once at the second vertex does not.
per_hypothesis.consistency_with_measured_evidence: Consistent with the WL86 economics numbers it is built from (5.45x per sample, 1.6-1.7x fewer samples, 9x per frame) and with the bias floor of 0.073 in E2 region C that motivates it. No measurement of the residual variance exists. The proposal itself rates it not defensible.
fatal_objections: By its own (verified) arithmetic the per-sample gain is about 1.2x before the 41 ms of extra per-edit cost and before an optimised comparator; it cannot meet the economics requirement and is slower than plain path tracing after an edit at low sample counts.
It contains no transport hypothesis: nothing about sharp transport, edit validity or learned state changes relative to ECRO v0, and the estimator is published.
non_fatal_objections: The variance model omits the extra term from table error and takes d from a biased, noise-level ladder.
Its one useful conclusion (ECRO's advantage is that of a biased cache) is already implied by the WL86 protocol verdict NOT TESTED and the recorded bias floor.
per_hypothesis.what_would_change_the_verdict: A measured per-sample variance of (suffix - table) far below the suffix variance at the second camera vertex, which the definition of a conditional-mean table rules out; or a different estimator design that queries the learned quantity many times per vertex without rays, which would be a different hypothesis.

reviews.is_any_hypothesis_just_a_renaming:
Yes, all three to different degrees.

- **H2** is WL84A Track C (LPTG: ER lobes split at a roughness threshold, rough events through a compiled bin matrix, sharp events as ray chains, no learned global parameters) with a light-side caustic deposit added. LPTG was withdrawn by its own advocate. Outside the project it is directional finite-element radiance plus two-pass specular handling and a caustic map (Immel 1986; Sillion 1991; Wallace 1987; Jensen 1996). As a position it repeats WL80B and WL84A.
- **H1** is the same partition with ECRO v0's one-shot learned table kept for the broad tail. Its learned term is ECRO's already-passing broad behaviour with the failing family moved to physics. The parts correspond to extended form factors, Neural Radiosity's specular-chain tracing, Deep Scattering's 'trace low orders, predict the smooth remainder', and Modular Radiance Transfer / direct-to-indirect transfer. Nothing in it is a mechanism without precedent; the proposal concedes most of this but does not name LPTG.
- **H3** is a published estimator (neural control variates; two-level Monte Carlo with a neural incident radiance cache) applied to ECRO's table.

None of the three is a renaming of FNTO's four K terms.
reviews.strongest_overall_objection:
The proposal contains no learned global architecture hypothesis that is both specified and distinguishable from what the project already has, and the two arguments it uses to reach 'select nothing' are stronger than its evidence.

- **H1's learned term is ECRO v0's passing part.** Its only new content is physical (lobe-class partition, source-side deposit, continued rays), which is WL84A's withdrawn LPTG plus a caustic pass. The learned class is defined two incompatible ways (sharp-mediated links inside the tail through C~_G, or no sharp event in any learned target), so the proposal's own first check, separately tallied classes, cannot be run on it as written.
- **The 'identifiability-economics duality' rests on a comparator nobody ran.** The explicit patch x bin solve through the WL86 rays has no measured accuracy or time. The one physically matched comparison with numbers goes the other way: a path-traced table costs 0.157-1.24 s per lighting at about 0.10 entry noise, the learned fill 11.3-11.8 ms at 0.043-0.056 including oracle noise.
- **'CONTRADICTED' for the learned sharp flight is overstated.** It rests on one post hoc, single-realisation test that passes its rule by 0.4 points in one case and through a different clause in the other. Exact radiance through the same rays still delivers 80-84 % of the family with patch correlation 0.78-0.88, against 1-18 % for the learned flight, so the regression-dilution story does not explain the size and the bulk of the failure is unattributed.
- **The owned class is nearly empty where the question lives.** On the WL85 hard population 4 % of albedo is broad; the WL86 panel and sphere would both be traced.

The conclusion 'the evidence does not yet support selecting any learned global mechanism' survives, but as an absence of evidence. It is not shown that identifiable global targets are always cheap to compute, nor that receiver-side learned sharp flights are impossible.
